Good thing you have an affinity for death, so I will help you clean more of those tattoos."
He turned into a mist and then augmented Lani and her weapon.
At once, Lani’s body surged with so much power that the dark fiends panicked.
She stood her ground and clashed with them, this time augmented by death, which made her immune to it.
The Dark Empress’s eyes narrowed, but she didn’t linger on it for long since she had yet again spotted another familiar face...

chapters.title: Chapter 1810: The Dark War (12)
paragraphs: As it appeared, there were far more than two people here who had fought in the Dark Wars. While the spotlight had been on the Night Riders and a select few, many warriors from different backgrounds had joined the campaign against the enemy in the first Dark War.
Two of them were Fallon and Vika.
The two had a rocky relationship in this life, just as they had in their past lives. It could even be said that they were not friends, more like rivals.
However, considering they were dating the same man in this life, it was only natural to assume they were now friends.
Looking at their cohesion in battle, it was plain that they might be rivals, but they also understood each other very well.
Fallon was the daughter of a very wealthy king in her past life, while Vika was an orphan.
Well, if one looked at it, even in this life, they had nearly repeated the same backstory. Fallon was the daughter of a rich merchant, while Vika was once again an orphan.
The only difference was that Fallon was not a princess but a wealthy merchant herself.
And just like in their past life, they met as a wealthy woman and an assassin.
Fallon was not much of a warrior in their past life. However, when she met Vika, an orphan who had crawled out of the slums and made a life for herself, she became inspired.
They became friends, but it was later revealed that Vika had only befriended her to get close to her father and assassinate him.

Unfortunately, Vika had genuinely wanted that friendship, so she failed to complete her mission. But that changed nothing since, despite her failure, the assassination was carried out on her behalf just like how it happened in this life too.
Their friendship went downhill from then on, and the rest was history.

But as fate would have it, they reunited later, and after Fallon tried many times to kill Vika without success, she stopped and rekindled their friendship, which blossomed into something even more magical.
That magic was revealed during that arduous battle, the one where they single-handedly defended their planet from hordes of Dark Creatures.
Today, they were doing exactly the same thing, and despite not having memories of their past lives, things seemed to be connecting even more than they would have if they did.

"Fallon, you know this moment feels all too familiar, almost as if we have been in this exact scenario before, surrounded by hordes of monsters, yet we prevailed," Vika said with a small laugh as her dagger spun from her throw, circling three Demigod Dark Fiends.

A few meters from her, Fallon blocked the weapon of a Dark Fiend with her sword. Then, almost as if she knew a dagger was coming, her hand moved and caught it, driving it through the Dark Fiend’s neck.
She twisted it, then pulled it forward, cutting its throat cleanly. The Dark Fiend staggered and fell, but even before it did, Fallon was already on the move, wielding both a dagger and a sword.

"Isn’t this a terrible time to make such assumptions? We have Demigods gunning for our heads here, my friend," Fallon replied with a laugh. "Then again, it would be great if we shared a past together. I bet we were the best of friends back then."

Vika pushed through the hordes of Dark Fiends around her and closed in on Fallon, who handed the dagger back to her. They allowed themselves a brief moment of respite, but before long, they were beset by yet more hordes of monsters.
The more they fought, the deeper their battlefield chemistry became. It grew so profound that they could feel their powers rising by several degrees simply from fighting side by side.

"I doubt we were the best of friends, Fallon. But I know for sure we share a past together," Vika said, then turned to look at her friend. "That said, we are surrounded, so maybe activate that ridiculous ability of yours, or else we will die."
Fallon, lost in the slaughter, snapped back to her senses, finally coming to terms with what had happened.
Three Supreme Dark Fiends, oozing an even more sinister energy, stood surrounding them. Both ladies were now Demigods, but against the Supremes, they were outmatched.
Regardless, a smile formed on Fallon’s face.
"You know, I saw Unity kill a God King a few minutes ago, and she is just an Immortal Lord. What do you say we kill a Supreme or two... or maybe three?" Fallon said, and Vika smiled.
"Ah, I feel death crawling closer to me, but why not? I want to see how hard it is to kill a Supreme."

And so they moved, Fallon running left and Vika going right. Two followed Vika, and one followed Fallon. Naturally, the Supremes caught up to them soon enough. However, they had also fallen into the trap that the two ladies had conjured.
Fallon had a unique ability called [Ghost Tactic]. It basically allowed her to turn either herself or someone who trusted her enough to place a marker in their soul into a ghost.
Once activated, not even a Celestial could kill them for 15 mins. More importantly, even if they were separated by a million light-years, they could each teleport to one another.
This was already possible with Ghost Tactic, but it became even more powerful after joining the Chaos Dragon Harem.
Only one Supreme followed Fallon, so she made Vika a ghost, and just as she was surrounded, she vanished, appearing behind the lone Supreme.
Her dagger shot forward, aiming for a deadly stab at the Dark Fiend’s neck.
However, it reacted quickly, moving to catch her dagger.
"Don’t turn your back on me."
Fallon unleashed a deadly slash, severing the Dark Fiend’s arm. Then, with a somersault, she landed a vicious kick on its chin, throwing its head back.
This gave Vika the perfect chance to assassinate it.
"Poison Embodiment Daggers."
Both daggers became shrouded in purple mist, and with a deadly lunge, she embedded them directly into the Dark Fiend’s neck and ripped them out, tearing through its flesh.
"DIE!"
Fallon moved, lightning dancing across her sword.

The next second, the Dark Fiend was dead, and a new record was set on the battlefield, making the two ladies the first Demigods in the Chaos Dragon Harem to kill a Supreme in less than twenty seconds.

They had no time to celebrate since they were surrounded once again, this time by five more Supreme-level Dark Fiends. The ones they had evaded, allowing them to kill the lone Dark Fiend, had now returned with reinforcements.
"Very shameless of you people. Can’t you have pity on harmless ladies?" Fallon said with a smile, then winked at Vika. The latter understood what had to be done.
However, before the two ladies could make their move, someone with disheveled hair whipping wildly through the air, as though she had no sense of beauty, appeared before them.
Their hair surged forward, wrapping itself around the five Dark Fiends.
It happened so fast that before the ladies could make a sound, all five Supremes had been captured within a domain of hair.
"What in the hell?" Vika muttered, trembling in sheer horror as she felt an overwhelming resentment radiating from the Hair Domain. "Since when could Dia do that?"
"I don’t know, but she has been in seclusion ever since they returned from their mission. Maybe she awakened some hidden abilities," Fallon replied, taking deep breaths.
"And she seems to have become a God too, I suppose."
The Hair Domain trembled, and more strands of hair began whipping across the battlefield, capturing dark fiends.
Far away, Kent, in his demi-human form, frowned as he looked in the direction of the Hair Domain.

chapters.title: Chapter 1811: The Dark War (13)
paragraphs: Panic surged through Kent’s body in all three forms.

Unfortunately, such an intense surge of emotion caused him to falter, allowing one of the three Pseudo-Primordial Dark Fiends he was locked in battle with to get close to him and stab its sword straight toward his heart.
The distance between them, coupled with the force behind the stab and the intense nature of the attack, would be fatal if it were to land on his body.
Thankfully, Kent reacted just in time, tilting himself just fast enough to limit the impact of the stab. But it still landed on his shoulder, causing bone and flesh to burst out.
He retreated, and he was healed the next second. Barely a moment after healing, he was back in an intense dance of steel and blood.
The source of his sudden panic was the Hair Domain that Dia had unleashed.

The first time he saw it was when Jest was returning to Inaya during the Divine Era. Back then, when they met, she was known as the Horror of the Stars, his heart demon, and the incarnation of Hera, Artemis’s big sister.

Learning that her sister had died following the Primordial Chaos Dragon, she was consumed by hatred and anger, allowing external corruption to take root within her and turning her beautiful self into a heart demon for the Chaos Dragon.
Chaos killed her, but she followed him into his next life. When they fought again, Jest suffered greatly before he managed to bring her down.
The Crimson Hair Entanglement Domain proved to be a very dangerous domain to shatter back then. So seeing it again brought back memories.
But something else seemed to make Kent panic, and it had to do with how she could unleash such power despite her cultivation base.
The last time he saw Dia, while she was able to harness her power as a Heart Demon, she could only affect others, taking over their minds.
She hadn’t gotten to the point where she could unleash the power of the Horror of the Stars. So seeing her unleash such power made him panic.
Thankfully, Tower was prepared for everything, so she calmed him down.

[The master has nothing to worry about. It appears Lady Dia has finally tapped into a bit of her power. I have already put measures in place that will prevent her from going beyond 50% of her second incarnation...]
’Uhm, that is good to hear, Tower. Though I must ask, if she can harness the power of the Horror of the Stars, then can she unleash the power of her other incarnations?’
Kent wanted to know mainly because he had faced her other incarnations, and each was a danger to him.
During the Shadow Era, she revealed herself while Faceless was exploring the Shadow Realm. Their battle lasted 100 days, resulting in Faceless sustaining numerous injuries.
Ruthless Bandit conquered her by devouring her. Well, he was a maniac himself, so it was only right that he had an easy time devouring her.
But if she could harness the powers of her other incarnation just like how Kent could, then when he managed to break free from his heart demon, Dia might just become the strongest in his harem.
[She would eventually awaken all those powers. But before she can make them her true power, we first have to handle the insidious power that stole her fate and destiny.]
’That is good, Tower. Keep an eye on her, and if she gets out of hand or is being influenced, knock her out and lock her inside the tower.’
[Okay, Master. But I believe you have nothing to worry about. If anything, you should be ready to witness her power once she is prepared.]
Kent could sense the joy in Tower’s tone, so he just smiled and sank his claws into the skull of a Dark Fiend, ripping its head off.

Just then, the sound of grass breaking reached his ears. His head turned due east, where a breathtaking beauty clad in silver armor swung her sword, unleashing an arc of glass that cut through and shattered everything in its path.
Enzi wasn’t messing around, especially now that she was a Demigod.
With every swing of her sword, her Glass Domain spread outward, shattering the Dark Fiends as though they were made of mere crystal.
"Gosh, she is breathtaking," Kent admired Enzi’s beauty before turning away to handle his own growing number of opponents. The battle was far from over, not by a long shot.
Kent knew killing all the Dark Fiends was impossible, but winning was possible if only he could take the Dark Empress off the board.
She was the source of this infestation, so with her gone, the rest would find themselves stripped of power, turning into dust.

But killing her was proving difficult. He had to break through the three Pseudo-Primordials, which wasn’t proving easy. Regardless, he was making headway, and his legion and wives were doing an impeccable job as well.
Not too far from Enzi, Liora stabbed a Dark Fiend through the head, killing it.
She took a deep breath and surveyed the battlefield.
"Goodness gracious, Enzi, slow down a bit." She smiled proudly as she watched her friend and sister shatter the Shadow Fiends as though they were glass statues.

Enzi turned and looked at Liora, flashing a mischievous smile. "Obviously, I am going extra hard because I want more time with Kent. If I were you, I would quicken my pace unless you want to wait in line for months."
The smile on Liora’s face died down, replaced by a dark and insidious one. At once, her body released intense darkness. Then she moved, and before her reply came, three Demigods had lost their heads.
"Let’s see who gets to spend time with him first and who gets stuck in line."
She became the Shadow of Death, killing without reservation.
Enzi smiled and also unleashed a more potent ability, instantly manifesting thousands of glass swords. More shattering sounds filled the battlefield, showing she had no plans to lose to her sister.

With Kent’s dick on the line, she didn’t care if she had to win one over her best friend. They each wanted to spend the first and the most time with Kent since they had already tasked Tower with tracking who had the most kills.
That ranking would then determine the order in which they would take their turn with Kent.
As they say, even in the darkest times, there are moments worth celebrating.

Kent had no idea his wives had made such a bet. But even if he did, it wasn’t like he planned to stop them. With the time he had in the Chaos Chasm, he already had plans to spend time with them and awaken their True Names before he left again.
So if they had found a way to make things simpler for him, who was he to complain? The easier they made things for him, the more time he got to spend with them.
The only question now was who would get to go first...

Would it be the Mother of Killers, or the Joker augmented by Death himself? The race was tight, but one thing was certain: while all eyes remained on the two deadly women, some of their sisters were also proving to be a force to be reckoned with.
The race to be the first to climb the dragon rod might just be the most intense battle within this dark and twisted war.

chapters.title: Chapter 1812: The Dark War (14)
paragraphs: Sure, the likes of Neomi, Vexthra, Lani, Meiko, Pandora, Unity, Liora, Enzi, and a couple of others are killing much faster, putting their names at the top of the ranking.
That speaks volumes about their strength, and it goes without saying that they are some of the most powerful warriors in the harem.
However, a much more serious threat loomed. One that, if the ladies currently at the top of the list weren’t careful, would be dethroned.
One such threat was the succubus, Adina. Just like some of her sisters, she had also become a Demigod, boasting incredibly powerful illusion abilities.

Unlike the rest of her sisters, who had thrown themselves into the carnage of battle, cutting down their foes with their own hands, Adina sat in an elegant lotus posture, surrounded by a formation naturally created by Alina.

Resting on her lap was a zither that oozed an insidious pink mist. With every note she played, waves of illusory energy that seemed to reach into the soul, worm their way into the heart, and finally invade the mind spread across the battlefield.
Those who lacked the will to resist her spreading power were dragged into illusions. With a mere whisper, she planted commands into their ears, turning them into her swords and blades.

The longer her zither played, the farther her encroaching power spread, taking hold of more minds and hearts. As a succubus, even the Dark Fiends found it difficult to resist the budding feelings of lust and the overwhelming desire to please their mistress.

The Dark Empress was powerless against what her Dark Fiends felt and how those feelings controlled them. She knew she had to kill Adina, or else all she could do was watch the carnage unfold around her.
But to reach Adina, one first had to get past the Ancient Evil Grand Shaman Vorgun.
That was nearly impossible because, when it came to the highest death count on the battlefield, the kills kept piling up under Grand Shaman Vorgun’s name.
Shade King Nykali had been thoroughly humbled by Grand Shaman Vorgun. While the former specialized in cultivating Soul Wraiths, Grand Shaman Vorgun specialized in cultivating Soul Fiends.
The two arts were similar, yet fundamentally different.

Shade King Nykali could preserve only the original form of the soul he had harvested. If the soul came from a human, then no matter how powerful he made that Soul Wraith, it would always retain its human form.

Grand Shaman Vorgun, however, could reshape souls entirely. Using nothing but his imagination, he could manipulate a soul into any form he envisioned. As long as he could picture it vividly enough, he could create it.
Aside from that, Grand Shaman Vorgun was a Celestial Supreme, far stronger than Shade King Nykali, who was only a Demigod.
Shade King Nykali boasted forty thousand quality Soul Wraiths, but compared to Grand Shaman Vorgun, he still had a long way to go.
Currently, Grand Shaman Vorgun stood atop a mountain of Dark Fiend corpses, holding his staff as he gazed across the battlefield with a chilling smile.
Scattered across the battlefield were ghastly Soul Fiends, each towering over 200 meters tall, their presence both chilling and devastating.

Every single one of them was above the rank of a Supreme King. The more they killed, the stronger they became. It was as though they would continue growing until they reached the point where even the heavens could no longer contain them.
That point was still far beyond them. But even so, the mere fact that he alone commanded such power spoke volumes about the might possessed by the Twenty-Four Grand Shamans.
Of course, the others weren’t messing around either.

Veera and her undead legion were advancing relentlessly, growing stronger and more devastating in every regard. She and Shade King Nykali also had a bet of their own, one that revolved around who could claim the most kills.
But if commanding vast armies was under discussion, then the Mind Cultivators also deserved a place in the conversation.

Zaila had already taken over the minds of ten thousand Dark Fiends, with two Celestials among them. The reason the Dark Fiends were struggling to gain the advantage was their lack of versatility compared to Kent’s side.
Someone like Zaila, who was merely a Demigod, had managed to seize control of ten thousand Dark Fiends, including two Celestials, whom she had sent after Demigods and Gods.
It was like opening a dam and letting the floodwaters pour into a city of mortals. They were practically defenseless against such a tide.
It was what Zaila had done. The Celestials and Supremes she had mind-controlled are not killing gods and demigods.
In the end, everything depended on whether the Dark Empress could kill her before her mental powers spread deeper into the minds of even more Dark Fiends.

Some members of Kent’s legion who cultivated the Mind Path were also using their abilities to their fullest potential. The legion of Mind Cultivators continued doing their part, constantly adding more forces to Kent’s side.
Suddenly, a sense of tension enveloped everyone.
The feeling came from the direction where Kent was locked in battle against the three Pseudo-Primordials. Those who managed to turn and look witnessed a truly chilling sight.
High in the air, millions of swords hovered behind Kent, each one empowered by Sword Energy and infused with evil qi, chaos qi, and abyssal qi.

However, that alone wasn’t enough. Thousands of blood runes lit up across the swords, further augmenting them and boosting their power to such an extent that the moment they appeared, everyone sensed overwhelming danger.

Perhaps the greatest source of that danger was the subtle trace of Origin Qi hidden within some of the swords. Kent made sure to use only the smallest amount to avoid provoking a backlash from the heavens.
Yet that tiny amount of Origin Qi was more than enough to shake the hearts of the three Pseudo-Primordials.
"Die, you worthless maggots!"
Kent slashed forward, and the millions of swords surged ahead, causing the very ground beneath them to tremble.
The Dark Empress panicked and quickly summoned her defense, manifesting the silhouette of a gigantic scorpion. It covered her entire body just as the swords arrived.
The three Pseudo-Primordials didn’t back down either. They each activated their own defenses, meeting the oncoming storm of swords with determined expressions.
The danger didn’t last long because the moment they became preoccupied, Kent realized he couldn’t kill them with his usual techniques.
So he changed tactics.
"Gaap, turn into a hammer."
His sword changed form, becoming a massive hammer with a black steel head and a brown handle.
"Pseudo-Primordials are indeed worthy opponents. However, I didn’t come all this way just to be stopped by mere bugs."
Kent’s Barbarian nature awakened, causing his body to expand into that of a giant barbarian with arms powerful enough to wield the hammer Gaap had transformed into.
"Today, you will witness the power of my Sixty-Six Hammer Art."
Kent’s body surged with power, the air crackling with elemental force, leaving everyone watching the battle with numb scalps.
He flew into the air and raised the hammer...
RUMBLE! RUMBLE!
"First Hammer."

The clouds churned as lightning flashed through them. Within the lightning, the silhouette of a colossal hammer appeared. The moment it manifested, an invisible force crashed down upon the three Pseudo-Primordials and the Dark Empress.
"DIE!"
Kent descended and struck with a devastating force.
A gigantic hammer split the clouds apart, and a large hammerhead came crashing down with overwhelming force...

chapters.title: Chapter 1813: The Dark War (15)
paragraphs: The Sixty-Six Hammer Art was a technique Fjorge created during the Flame Era.
He named it the Sixty-Six Hammer Art because, in his mind, that was how far he planned to master the technique. However, even up to the point he died, he hadn’t mastered half of it.

It wasn’t because he wasn’t serious enough or that he lacked the comprehension speed to master a technique he had created himself. It was because, despite being a Barbarian and a blacksmith, his body still wasn’t strong enough to handle even the 23rd Hammer.
His peak was the 22nd Hammer. Even then, he could only use it once with a 48-hour cooldown.
Kent knew he himself wasn’t strong enough to unleash the 66th Hammer. However, his body was strong enough to unleash a much better form of it, the Sixty-Six Hammer Art - the First Hammer.
As the giant hammer split the clouds and descended, the entire planet trembled.
[Master, isn’t this a bit too much even for you?]
Tower chuckled, causing Kent to smirk. Indeed, he had gone overboard. Perhaps he was fed up with using the Pseudo-Primordials as training dummies, so he chose to kill them.

But instead of using Flame Qi alone to harness the power of the Sixty-Six Hammer Art, he used all his energies. He tapped into 5% of each energy - Chaos Qi, Abyssal Qi, Evil Qi, Blood Qi, Ice Qi, Flame Qi, and Lightning Qi.
But as if that wasn’t enough, he used 20,000 Blood Runes to augment it and even harnessed 5 Blood Death Tattoos.
The first layer of defense that the three Pseudo-Primordial Dark Fiends had activated crumbled even before the hammer was fully out of the clouds.
By the time it closed the 100 meters between them, only one defense remained.
They all ignited their Celestial Cores, burning their energy to reinforce their shields.
In the end, they defended against the First Hammer at the expense of their energy and several broken bones.
Kent grinned and looked at the hammer in his hand. "Mjonir would have shattered every bone in their bodies." He missed his hammer, the one he had used during the Flame Era.
Regardless, he wasn’t done yet.
He raised the hammer into the air again, causing the clouds to gather once more. From within, the silhouettes of two gigantic hammerheads appeared, doubling the pressure the First Hammer brought.
"Taste my Second Hammer."
With a deadly swing, two large hammers broke through the clouds, first sending out two deadly arcs. The three Pseudo-Primordials turned pale, their bodies tense as the two hammers descended.
The Dark Empress, who was still being suppressed by the tower within a 100-meter radius, wore the same expression.
But in the end, they all survived the Second Hammer, showing the kind of powerhouses they were. But as if to mock their achievement, the Third Hammer descended, and they all crashed to their knees.
The Fourth Hammer sent them all lying on the ground, and by the time the Fifth Hammer came, all three Pseudo-Primordials were left broken.
Kent didn’t waste any time and quickly moved in for the kill, knowing that if he missed his chance now, he might regret it.
He turned into a blur, and before the three Pseudo-Primordials could read his movement, he was already before them with his sword raised. Gaap had turned back into his sword form.
Kent unleashed a wide swing, aiming for all three of them.
However, just when his sword was mere inches away, a crimson light so powerful came out of nowhere and crashed into his sword.
Gaap flew out of Kent’s hands, flying several kilometers away.

Kent himself was sent flying several meters back, his gaze narrowing at the sudden source of the attack. All around, the crimson light that slammed into his sword shattered the void, sending void shards flying everywhere.

Many Dark Fiends died from them, and even two members of the Eternal Wrath Legion weren’t lucky either. The shards claimed their lives, sending their souls back to the last floor of the dungeons they had come from.
They would be reborn with their strength intact, but for now, they were out of the battle.
Kent slammed into a Supreme-level Dark Fiend before coming to a halt.
But before he could steady himself, his sixth sense told him to move forward, and he did.
Just then, a hand dripping with blood burst out from the void, aiming for his throat. If he had been a split second slower, his neck would have ended up in those deadly hands.
"Genesis, so you are still alive, huh?" Blood Ancestor’s voice came from the void, followed by a loud shatter, splitting the void open.
From the crimson door that had opened, the familiar figure of the Blood Ancestor stepped out with a grin tugging at the corner of his lips.

"Killing me isn’t as simple as forcing me to jump into a Chaos Portal. But indeed, I am still alive, and as you can see, I am in the middle of something, so step aside and let me finish first. You can use that time to come to terms with your impending death."
Kent moved, tapping into his Void Storm Domain to teleport away, completely ignoring the killing intent surrounding him. Blood Ancestor, who never saw this sudden exit coming, was taken aback.
However, he also moved, only to find himself face-to-face with Han, standing on a sword as though he were some kind of sword sage.
It appeared it had taken him just 15 minutes to kill all 25 Celestials he had rendered mortal using his Eternal Karmic Sword Domain.

They stood no chance against him to begin with. So the battle ended, and now he had blocked the path of a Primordial who had come with only one motive: to kill Kent, who happened to be the reincarnation of his old-time nemesis, Lord Genesis.
The first time they met, Kent pulled a fast one and escaped, failing to kill him. Now, he had come again after sensing Kent unleash his Sword Realm once more.
Of course, this time Kent didn’t run, but he also failed to land a killing blow with his first attack.
He was a Primordial, so fighting using Origin Qi wasn’t something he could afford for long. That one attack was a sure-kill move, but he missed.
So Han blocking his path wasn’t something he planned to take lying down.
"Move aside, peasant."
His hand made a sweeping motion, attempting to push Han aside. However, he found himself staring at an unmoving bastard who held a smile on his face, almost as if he had anticipated this move.

"I know what you are wondering right now. You want to know how a mere Celestial could withstand the pressure of a Primordial," Han smirked. "It is simple, really. I simply ignored it, just as I will ignore all attacks from you unless you lower yourself to my standard."
As he said that, his cultivation started to drop. In less than a minute, he went from being a Celestial to a mere Root Saint. He had become a mortal.

"You see, my Eternal Karmic Sword Domain works in multiple ways. Either I make both of us mortals and duel it out, or I make myself mortal and change the rules of combat, making sure attacks above the level of mortals cannot touch me.
Right now, you are in my Eternal Karmic Sword Domain, which means you have to abide by my rules. So what do you say, Blood Ancestor? Are you prepared to face me in combat as a mortal...?"

chapters.title: Chapter 1814: The Dark War (16)
paragraphs: Han was what one would refer to as the Bane of Existence.
His Eternal Karmic Sword Domain was just too overpowered, to the point that even a Primordial found himself at a disadvantage against him.

Blood Ancestor could sense and feel it deep within his soul that the only way he could leave this domain and go after Kent was by killing Han. But to kill him, he would have to lower his cultivation base to the Root Saint stage.
Of course, by doing so, he also ran the risk of dying at the hands of the bastard, who clearly wasn’t going to make things easy for the almighty Blood Ancestor.
"We can also stand here and chat. I would love to know more about what it’s like being a Primordial with no backbone," Han taunted, and Blood Ancestor took the bait, something he shouldn’t have.
But he did, and his anger compelled him to move, which resulted in his cultivation plummeting until he was a Root Saint as well.
Then their weapons met, and for a moment, Blood Ancestor still thought himself a Primordial, anticipating Han’s body flying back with a mangled arm.

However, the opposite happened because the moment their weapons met, he was pushed back. But more shocking, and perhaps the most insidious aspect of the Eternal Karmic Sword Domain, kicked in the moment he was pushed back.

He tried to harness more power than what a Root Saint could wield to steady himself, but to his utter shock, he couldn’t. This put a frown on his face, and when he turned to look at Han, he saw him smiling.
"I forgot to tell you, but the moment you lower your cultivation, you can only increase it again after an hour. Meaning, I have an hour to kill you." Han winked teasingly, then spun his sword.
"I learned you are an immortal. But know that since Big Brother has given you to me, then one death is all I need to completely kill you. So please, don’t die easily."

Han moved, and Blood Ancestor cursed the day he was born. He had fallen into the trap of a mortal, and that pained him deep in the heart, causing him to throw all caution into the wind and attack as if his life were on the line.
Well, his life was already on the line.
Meanwhile, Kent was too slow to take advantage of the battered state of the three Pseudo-Primordials. However, he managed to get one.
Just when he rushed back, his sword moved, and one head flew into the air. But the healing speed of Pseudo-Primordials wasn’t something to look down on.
The other two managed to heal in time and retreated, saving their skins.
Kent moved forward, hoping to prevent them from healing, but he found himself surrounded by thousands of Supremes who came at the command of the Dark Empress.
"Damn it," he cursed, and then his Blood Qi surged, and his eyes turned crimson.

Kent had gone mad, and the effects of his madness began to show as he cut the dark fiends down. He had lost the chance to kill the two Pseudo-Primordials, but he got the Supremes and Celestials, who clearly had a death wish.
The Blood Sea Annihilation surged, creating a domain of blood for Kent to carry out his unholy massacre, one that left the thousands of Dark Fiends overwhelmed.
Amid the chaos, a message in golden text flashed before his eyes.
[You have unlocked the first page of the Chaos Ascension King Legacy Manual.]
He had no time to ponder it since he was already being besieged on all sides. He had already surrounded himself with hundreds of Chaos Scale Shields, but even so, he dared not divide his attention.
Meanwhile, 3 km away from him, Vexthra, who, despite facing terrifying Supremes and Celestials, had kept part of her attention on Kent.

She saw how frustrated Kent had become after he failed to kill the Pseudo-Primordials. She witnessed him come close to killing all three, but Blood Ancestor prevented him from doing so. Now, he had lost his chance.
She turned to Pandora and Fiannarel.
"It seems the person who attacked Kent, leading to him vanishing for 50 days, is back," she said, pointing her bow in the direction of Blood Ancestor, who was now locked in a fierce battle with Han.
"It appears so, but I doubt he will last long against Han," Pandora replied, and Vexthra nodded.
They were experienced warriors, so they knew when someone was at a disadvantage. Right now, Han seemed to have the upper hand while Blood Ancestor was barely keeping up.
"I wish I could kill him for attacking my little brother," Fiannarel said, a cold light flashing across her eyes as she looked at Blood Ancestor, who had been sent flying by Han.
"Same here. It took all the self-control I had not to go after him the last time." Pandora clearly wished she could be the one to kill the bastard who had made them worry about their man’s safety.
Vexthra smiled and said, "I don’t know about you ladies, but my domain has become powerful enough to kill even a Pseudo-Primordial."
Her eyes shone darker as she locked her gaze on one of the Pseudo-Primordials that had survived Kent’s first five forms of the Sixty-Six Hammer Art.

"You are probably biting off more than you can chew, but for some reason, I want to see how you manage that." Pandora patted Vexthra on the shoulder and added, "Just know that if you get hurt, you will be out of the race in this battle."

Vexthra scoffed and shrugged Pandora’s hand off her shoulder. "As if you wouldn’t be happy about that. But hear me now, my dear sister: I will not get hurt, because right now those two are more than furious.
Their bodies, souls, and minds are oozing hatred and resentment, and as it happens, I am the Goddess of Hatred and Resentment."

Vexthra flew into the air and retrieved her bow. A dark arrow appeared on it, and with a pulling motion, she drew back the bowstring. At once, a large dark silhouette of her appeared behind her, and a much larger bow materialized as well.
One of the Pseudo-Primordials sensed danger immediately and activated his defenses.
"Futile," Vexthra smirked.
Then she let go of the string, sending the arrow flying. The Pseudo-Primordial, confident in his defense, sneered as the arrow approached.
However, when it landed on his shield and passed through, his eyes widened.
But it was already too late.

He had defended his body when the arrow had been meant for his soul. The moment it passed through the shield, it pierced his soul, and that was how the second Pseudo-Primordial on the Dark Empress’s side died.

The last remaining Pseudo-Primordial narrowed his eyes at Vexthra and moved, appearing behind her in an instant. However, his fist never reached her. That was because the moment he attacked, someone grabbed it.
"Punk, do you think it would be that easy to kill my sister?"
"Indie!" Vexthra’s eyes widened when she turned and saw the familiar face of her sister, who had descended into the Underworld to inherit the position of Underworld Empress.
"Hey, Vex. Missed me?" Indie’s hand moved, and the poor Pseudo-Primordial, who had attacked someone he shouldn’t have, found himself slammed into the ground, debris flying everywhere.
"You have no idea how much we all missed you, Indie," Vexthra said as she hugged her, forgetting they were in the middle of a devastating battle.
"So you are now a Celestial," Pandora remarked, walking toward Indie.
Meanwhile, Fiannarel stood with a nonchalant expression, staring at the Pseudo-Primordial as though he were nothing more than a mere bug before her.

sentences.text: Han was what one would refer to as the Bane of Existence.
His Eternal Karmic Sword Domain was just too overpowered, to the point that even a Primordial found himself at a disadvantage against him.
Blood Ancestor could sense and feel it deep within his soul that the only way he could leave this domain and go after Kent was by killing Han.
But to kill him, he would have to lower his cultivation base to the Root Saint stage.
Of course, by doing so, he also ran the risk of dying at the hands of the bastard, who clearly wasn’t going to make things easy for the almighty Blood Ancestor.
"We can also stand here and chat.
I would love to know more about what it’s like being a Primordial with no backbone," Han taunted, and Blood Ancestor took the bait, something he shouldn’t have.
But he did, and his anger compelled him to move, which resulted in his cultivation plummeting until he was a Root Saint as well.
Then their weapons met, and for a moment, Blood Ancestor still thought himself a Primordial, anticipating Han’s body flying back with a mangled arm.
However, the opposite happened because the moment their weapons met, he was pushed back.
But more shocking, and perhaps the most insidious aspect of the Eternal Karmic Sword Domain, kicked in the moment he was pushed back.
He tried to harness more power than what a Root Saint could wield to steady himself, but to his utter shock, he couldn’t.
This put a frown on his face, and when he turned to look at Han, he saw him smiling.
"I forgot to tell you, but the moment you lower your cultivation, you can only increase it again after an hour.
Meaning, I have an hour to kill you." Han winked teasingly, then spun his sword.
"I learned you are an immortal.
But know that since Big Brother has given you to me, then one death is all I need to completely kill you.
So please, don’t die easily."
Han moved, and Blood Ancestor cursed the day he was born.
He had fallen into the trap of a mortal, and that pained him deep in the heart, causing him to throw all caution into the wind and attack as if his life were on the line.
Well, his life was already on the line.
Meanwhile, Kent was too slow to take advantage of the battered state of the three Pseudo-Primordials.
However, he managed to get one.
Just when he rushed back, his sword moved, and one head flew into the air.
But the healing speed of Pseudo-Primordials wasn’t something to look down on.
The other two managed to heal in time and retreated, saving their skins.
Kent moved forward, hoping to prevent them from healing, but he found himself surrounded by thousands of Supremes who came at the command of the Dark Empress.
"Damn it," he cursed, and then his Blood Qi surged, and his eyes turned crimson.
Kent had gone mad, and the effects of his madness began to show as he cut the dark fiends down.
He had lost the chance to kill the two Pseudo-Primordials, but he got the Supremes and Celestials, who clearly had a death wish.
The Blood Sea Annihilation surged, creating a domain of blood for Kent to carry out his unholy massacre, one that left the thousands of Dark Fiends overwhelmed.
Amid the chaos, a message in golden text flashed before his eyes.
[You have unlocked the first page of the Chaos Ascension King Legacy Manual.]
He had no time to ponder it since he was already being besieged on all sides.
He had already surrounded himself with hundreds of Chaos Scale Shields, but even so, he dared not divide his attention.
Meanwhile, 3 km away from him, Vexthra, who, despite facing terrifying Supremes and Celestials, had kept part of her attention on Kent.
She saw how frustrated Kent had become after he failed to kill the Pseudo-Primordials.
She witnessed him come close to killing all three, but Blood Ancestor prevented him from doing so.
Now, he had lost his chance.
She turned to Pandora and Fiannarel.
"It seems the person who attacked Kent, leading to him vanishing for 50 days, is back," she said, pointing her bow in the direction of Blood Ancestor, who was now locked in a fierce battle with Han.
"It appears so, but I doubt he will last long against Han," Pandora replied, and Vexthra nodded.
They were experienced warriors, so they knew when someone was at a disadvantage.
Right now, Han seemed to have the upper hand while Blood Ancestor was barely keeping up.
"I wish I could kill him for attacking my little brother," Fiannarel said, a cold light flashing across her eyes as she looked at Blood Ancestor, who had been sent flying by Han.
"Same here.
It took all the self-control I had not to go after him the last time." Pandora clearly wished she could be the one to kill the bastard who had made them worry about their man’s safety.
Vexthra smiled and said, "I don’t know about you ladies, but my domain has become powerful enough to kill even a Pseudo-Primordial."
Her eyes shone darker as she locked her gaze on one of the Pseudo-Primordials that had survived Kent’s first five forms of the Sixty-Six Hammer Art.

"You are probably biting off more than you can chew, but for some reason, I want to see how you manage that." Pandora patted Vexthra on the shoulder and added, "Just know that if you get hurt, you will be out of the race in this battle."
Vexthra scoffed and shrugged Pandora’s hand off her shoulder.
"As if you wouldn’t be happy about that.
But hear me now, my dear sister: I will not get hurt, because right now those two are more than furious.
Their bodies, souls, and minds are oozing hatred and resentment, and as it happens, I am the Goddess of Hatred and Resentment."
Vexthra flew into the air and retrieved her bow.
A dark arrow appeared on it, and with a pulling motion, she drew back the bowstring.
At once, a large dark silhouette of her appeared behind her, and a much larger bow materialized as well.
One of the Pseudo-Primordials sensed danger immediately and activated his defenses.
"Futile," Vexthra smirked.
Then she let go of the string, sending the arrow flying.
The Pseudo-Primordial, confident in his defense, sneered as the arrow approached.
However, when it landed on his shield and passed through, his eyes widened.
But it was already too late.
He had defended his body when the arrow had been meant for his soul.
The moment it passed through the shield, it pierced his soul, and that was how the second Pseudo-Primordial on the Dark Empress’s side died.
The last remaining Pseudo-Primordial narrowed his eyes at Vexthra and moved, appearing behind her in an instant.
However, his fist never reached her.
That was because the moment he attacked, someone grabbed it.
"Punk, do you think it would be that easy to kill my sister?"
"Indie!" Vexthra’s eyes widened when she turned and saw the familiar face of her sister, who had descended into the Underworld to inherit the position of Underworld Empress.
"Hey, Vex.
Missed me?" Indie’s hand moved, and the poor Pseudo-Primordial, who had attacked someone he shouldn’t have, found himself slammed into the ground, debris flying everywhere.
"You have no idea how much we all missed you, Indie," Vexthra said as she hugged her, forgetting they were in the middle of a devastating battle.
"So you are now a Celestial," Pandora remarked, walking toward Indie.
Meanwhile, Fiannarel stood with a nonchalant expression, staring at the Pseudo-Primordial as though he were nothing more than a mere bug before her.

chapters.title: Chapter 1815: The Dark War (17)
paragraphs: Indie left for the Underworld as an Immortal and returned as a Celestial.

But on top of that, she was now even more beautiful. First of all, between the time Kent left the Underworld and now, she had undergone so many changes, now sporting long silver hair that nearly swept the floor behind her.

Her figure had also become even more athletic, with a firm ass and a heavy chest. Indie was already good-looking even before she became the Underworld Empress, but now she seemed to have taken on an aura of authority, the kind that made her an empress, someone who commanded kingdoms.
Her eyes were shades of silver, and she seemed to have awakened a unique purple flame. Looking at her posture, one could tell she had become both powerful and feared.

"Tower informed me there was fun to be had, so I decided to come. Who knew I would be saving your skin, Vex," Indie joked before turning to look at Kent, locked in battle with thousands of Dark Fiends surrounded by a Blood Sea.
"Do you think he needs our help?" Indie asked.
Vexthra shook her head.
"Probably not, but we will help him regardless. But first, how are you, and where is Miryssa?"
"I am more than fine, and Miryssa will be here in a couple of minutes along with some friends. I came faster than them because I am the Empress. Crossing the boundary is very simple for me."

"Hmm, then in that case, go help Kent. You have some catching up to do, since we have been fighting and killing for half an hour now," Vexthra teased, and it worked. She knew Indie would go all out just to put her name on top of the list.
But before Indie could fire back, an explosion came from the distance.

Turning in that direction, they saw a vast domain of hair moving across the battlefield at a terrifying speed. At first, the ladies didn’t know where the hair was heading, but it soon became clear that it was moving toward Kent.
Before they could panic, they saw Dia’s terrifying figure emerge from the Blood Sea domain. For a moment, the ladies who knew Dia’s history and nature with Kent panicked.

However, none of them made any attempt to move since the moment she appeared inside the blood domain, her Hair Domain merged with the Blood Sea Annihilation, creating an even more chilling domain, one that made everyone widen their eyes.
"Leave them to me, Kent. I will handle them," Dia said to Kent. Then she moved, and what followed was the most chilling massacre yet.
Her hair turned into deadly blades, stabbing, slicing, and dicing through the thousands of Dark Fiends. Some strands turned into deadly whips, while most transformed into arrows.
The more she killed, the more devastating the Blood Hair Domain became.
Kent only spent a few seconds watching before he vanished from the domain and appeared a couple of meters away from the Dark Empress, who stood with a surprisingly calm expression.

All the people she wanted dead were alive, and more of her Dark Fiends kept dying. Aside from that, she had lost two of her Pseudo-Primordial Dark Fiend Guards, with the third one almost at death’s door.
Such events should have left her on edge, her body shuddering, her heart beating wildly, with anger and hatred surging through her body.
However, she seemed calm, almost too calm for Kent’s liking.

"You seem too calm, Dark Empress. What insidious plan do you have left?" he asked, a smile forming on his face. He had thought he alone would have to break through the thousands of Dark Fiends that had besieged him.
But Dia came, and everything was handled. Then even the Pseudo-Primordials were no more. The only one he needed to kill now to end the war was the Dark Empress.
But seeing her smile, Kent frowned.
"You know, I seem to have grasped your nature, human," the Dark Empress said, summoning a black staff.
"You are someone who faced the Dark Creatures, died, and reincarnated. If I had to make a guess, you were the Evil Combat Mage who stopped the Dark Invasion back then. Am I wrong?"
Kent smiled and shook his head.
"You are not wrong, Dark Empress. I was indeed the Ruthless Bandit, the one who stopped you back then and will stop you here yet again, this time for good."
The smile on the Dark Empress’s face remained.
"I have no doubt you will be able to stop me. I have already seen you hold back three Pseudo-Primordials and even come close to killing them with a single swing.
So trust me, I know you can stop me. However, you must be joking if you think killing me would solve your problems. In fact, killing me would only escalate things."
As she spoke, her staff moved, and a spell circle appeared. Inside the spell circle, Kent counted 250 nodes, and at the center was a much larger node.
Seeing this made Kent uneasy. He could sense something dangerous was amiss, or perhaps had already happened, and the Dark Empress was about to reveal it.
"It’s been several eras since your spell sealed me away. However, over the years, the Jian Family helped me break one layer after another. Thankfully, they managed to break the last layer an era ago.
Since then, I have been planning my revenge, one that would sweep across planets," she said, pointing at the nodes in the spell circle.
"Each node represents a world with less than enough firepower to defend against my Dark Fiends. This larger node is this planet, the heart of the formation.
I have already activated it, and right now, Dark Gates are opening, or are about to open, in those worlds. You can go ahead and kill me or keep me alive. Regardless, those 250 worlds are doomed."
The Dark Empress laughed manically, and Kent’s frown deepened.

"I will not compromise with you, human. You have already dug the graves of billions, and so I will show you the kind of darkness you have unleashed. There is no negotiation to be had, human. You’ve lost."

[Master, I have deciphered that the spell is indeed real, and she has already activated it several minutes ago. Killing her now will not stop the Dark Fiends as we had initially thought. However, it appears these nodes are linked to God and Immortal worlds, meaning the Dark Fiends sent there are not as strong as the ones here.]
’That is a bit troublesome,’ Kent muttered, narrowing his eyes at the Dark Empress.
"I will kill you now."
He moved and appeared before her. Then, in one decisive motion, his sword pierced her chest.
"This is where your journey ends, Dark Empress."
Cough.
She coughed up blood but smiled through the pain.
"Go rot in hell, Ruthless Bandit."

Her core ignited, and before Kent could blink, she exploded, causing flames to rise far and wide. A terrible shockwave swept across the planet’s surface, sending thousands flying through the air, with the unlucky ones dying on the spot.
Inside the flames, Kent stood virtually unaffected.
’Tower, can you reverse-engineer the spell and shut it down?’
[That is impossible, Master. But I can create portals that will take us to the 250 planets.]

’Do that. And while you are at it, see if you can locate some members of the Midnight Shadows. Also, inform the tribe leaders of the Blood Vein Tribe and the other races inside the Tower to prepare to deploy their forces.’

chapters.title: Chapter 1816: The Dark War (18)
paragraphs: [Planet Doorma - Immortal World]
Planet Doorma is one of the largest planets in the Eastern Region of the Immortal Realm. It is also one of the few immortal planets that holds more mortals than even many mortal worlds.
Due to its massive population, every continent on the planet is protected by highly trained immortals.
The Lasmid Continent is the second-largest continent on Planet Doorma and is home to both Humans and Elves. It is also one of the most peaceful and most visited continents.

The number of mortals on this continent alone numbered in the billions. If all fourteen continents were combined, the population of the planet would exceed sixteen billion, with 60% of the people being mortals.
Nobody knew that when they went to sleep and woke up, the first thing to greet them would be a massive portal spewing out Dark Fiends.
However, that was the sight that greeted the natives of the Lasmid Continent.
The attack was sudden and devastating. It came with a terrifying tide of Dark Fiends, both humanoid and beastly, with the majority of them being Peak Immortal Lords and Demigods.

At first, the defenders were able to hold back the tide, allowing many civilians to be evacuated. However, it took just fifteen minutes for the tide to turn against them as more Demigods emerged from the Dark Portal.
In no time, the battlefield descended into carnage, with hundreds dying every second.
"Just who have we offended?" a warrior whose left arm had been bitten off by a Dark Fiend asked, his grim expression reflecting the desperate state of the battle.

This morning, he told his family he was going to work and would return before dinner. However, looking at his missing arm and exhausted expression, one could tell he would not be able to keep his promise.
He took a deep breath and closed his eyes just as a Demigod humanoid Dark Fiend charged at him with a large jagged spear.
He knew death had come for him, so he prepared to welcome it.
However, after two seconds had passed and nothing had happened, he opened his eyes to the sight of a man with flowing purple hair holding the spear aimed at his heart.
Kent clenched the spear, and it shattered. Then, using the fragments of the broken weapon, he forged a new spear and commanded it with his mind, sending it hurtling toward the Demigod.
"Are you alright?" Kent asked, turning to face the one-armed warrior, who seemed too stunned to speak. "Of course, you are not alright. You lost an arm, after all."
He waved his hand, and a green mist flew toward the warrior and merged into his body. The very next second, a new arm grew where the severed one had been.
"Can you still fight?" Kent asked.
The young man looked at his newly regenerated arm before nodding, still unable to recover from the shock.
"That is the spirit. And don’t worry, reinforcements have arrived."
As soon as Kent finished speaking, a portal opened, and the warriors of the Blood Vein Tribe, one of the strongest tribes inside the tower, marched out under the leadership of their chief, Malthar.

Over the years, the people Kent had brought into the Tower City had trained tirelessly for the day he would need their help. Every time he fought a large-scale battle, they wished he would summon them.
However, the threats they had faced before were never great or daunting enough to require such overwhelming reinforcements.
Today, however, things were different.
Today, he needed every bit of strength he could gather to save 250 planets.
Kent had suspected something like this from the very beginning. However, even he had not expected the Dark Empress to prepare so extensively over the years.
Rigging 250 planets with enough Dark Fiends and patiently waiting for the day she could unleash them sounded like one of the most evil acts anyone could ever commit.
Then again, she wasn’t a person, so Kent never expected her to play by the rules.

Still, severing her connection to her Dark Fiends while retaining the authority to command them told Kent that if Paragon hadn’t given him this opportunity today, perhaps the next time they met, the Dark Empress would have become even more powerful.

The original plan the Ruthless Bandit had cooked up during the Dark Era, when the Dark Fiends had grown increasingly chaotic, was to locate their creator and kill them, which would naturally have stopped the Dark Fiends.
However, as things stood now, that plan hadn’t worked. He had killed her, but the dark fiends are still here.
If not for Kent arriving at the least opportune moment for the Dark Empress, things would have become far more chaotic than they already were.
But even so, many people were dying on every planet where the Dark Portals had opened.
He had deployed his legion and wives to rescue them, just as he had come here. But he was aware that many would have already died before they arrived.

As for the battle on the main planet, he had left everything to Grand Shaman Vorgun, Veera, Shade King Nykali, Dia, the Blood Warriors, and Indie, who had brought with her an army of Underworld warriors.
She had brought some of her Grim Reapers, along with warriors from every level of the Underworld.
The Underworld Kings and Queens hadn’t come since she could not afford to leave the Underworld undefended, but Nyx and Miryssa were with her.

They alone were enough to handle the remaining threat of the Dark Fiends. Grand Shaman Vorgun had already created over 2,000 Soul Fiends, each a terrifying powerhouse that thousands of Dark Fiends could not even scratch, regardless of how formidable they were.

The longer the battle raged on, the closer they all came to breaking. But Kent trusted and believed they would be able to hold on. He knew that with Indie’s reinforcements and Grand Shaman Vorgun’s ever-growing army of Soul Fiends, they would prevail.
He just had to finish things here as quickly as possible so he could check on the other planets where he had deployed his wives and legion.

With Kent’s arrival and the Blood Vein Tribe joining the fight, the battle quickly began to shift. Kent alone was a force to be reckoned with, and his appearance had completely changed the momentum of the battlefield.

Thankfully, just a couple of minutes after he arrived, reinforcements from the other continents finally reached the battlefield in large numbers, turning the battle into one that could be won with far fewer casualties.
One thing Kent was also grateful for was his Shadow Fiends. His Faceless Shadow Realm granted him the ability to unlock Shadow Fiends through the kills made by himself, his legion, and his wives.

This Dark War had resulted in the deaths of thousands of Dark Fiends, allowing him to unlock thousands of Shadow Fiends, including several Celestial-grade Shadow Fiends and an even more dangerous variant.
He had overlooked them during the battle on the main planet. However, when the need to save the other planets arose, Tower reminded him of their existence.
So now, across this battlefield and the others where he had deployed his wives, thousands of Shadow Fiends were fighting to save the planets while also protecting his wives.
His legion was essentially undead. As long as he remained alive, they could never truly die. Because of that, he wasn’t overly worried about them, especially the Eternal Wrath Legion.
The battle was steadily moving in his favor, and after an hour, he could tell that even if he left now, the situation here would not worsen.
So he departed and began visiting the other planets.

As soon as Kent finished speaking, a portal opened, and the warriors of the Blood Vein Tribe, one of the strongest tribes inside the tower, marched out under the leadership of their chief, Malthar.
Over the years, the people Kent had brought into the Tower City had trained tirelessly for the day he would need their help.
Every time he fought a large-scale battle, they wished he would summon them.
However, the threats they had faced before were never great or daunting enough to require such overwhelming reinforcements.
Today, however, things were different.
Today, he needed every bit of strength he could gather to save 250 planets.
Kent had suspected something like this from the very beginning.
However, even he had not expected the Dark Empress to prepare so extensively over the years.
Rigging 250 planets with enough Dark Fiends and patiently waiting for the day she could unleash them sounded like one of the most evil acts anyone could ever commit.
Then again, she wasn’t a person, so Kent never expected her to play by the rules.

Still, severing her connection to her Dark Fiends while retaining the authority to command them told Kent that if Paragon hadn’t given him this opportunity today, perhaps the next time they met, the Dark Empress would have become even more powerful.

The original plan the Ruthless Bandit had cooked up during the Dark Era, when the Dark Fiends had grown increasingly chaotic, was to locate their creator and kill them, which would naturally have stopped the Dark Fiends.
However, as things stood now, that plan hadn’t worked.
He had killed her, but the dark fiends are still here.
If not for Kent arriving at the least opportune moment for the Dark Empress, things would have become far more chaotic than they already were.
But even so, many people were dying on every planet where the Dark Portals had opened.
He had deployed his legion and wives to rescue them, just as he had come here.
But he was aware that many would have already died before they arrived.

As for the battle on the main planet, he had left everything to Grand Shaman Vorgun, Veera, Shade King Nykali, Dia, the Blood Warriors, and Indie, who had brought with her an army of Underworld warriors.
She had brought some of her Grim Reapers, along with warriors from every level of the Underworld.
The Underworld Kings and Queens hadn’t come since she could not afford to leave the Underworld undefended, but Nyx and Miryssa were with her.
They alone were enough to handle the remaining threat of the Dark Fiends.
Grand Shaman Vorgun had already created over 2,000 Soul Fiends, each a terrifying powerhouse that thousands of Dark Fiends could not even scratch, regardless of how formidable they were.
The longer the battle raged on, the closer they all came to breaking.
But Kent trusted and believed they would be able to hold on.
He knew that with Indie’s reinforcements and Grand Shaman Vorgun’s ever-growing army of Soul Fiends, they would prevail.
He just had to finish things here as quickly as possible so he could check on the other planets where he had deployed his wives and legion.
With Kent’s arrival and the Blood Vein Tribe joining the fight, the battle quickly began to shift.
Kent alone was a force to be reckoned with, and his appearance had completely changed the momentum of the battlefield.

Thankfully, just a couple of minutes after he arrived, reinforcements from the other continents finally reached the battlefield in large numbers, turning the battle into one that could be won with far fewer casualties.
One thing Kent was also grateful for was his Shadow Fiends.
His Faceless Shadow Realm granted him the ability to unlock Shadow Fiends through the kills made by himself, his legion, and his wives.

This Dark War had resulted in the deaths of thousands of Dark Fiends, allowing him to unlock thousands of Shadow Fiends, including several Celestial-grade Shadow Fiends and an even more dangerous variant.
He had overlooked them during the battle on the main planet.
However, when the need to save the other planets arose, Tower reminded him of their existence.
So now, across this battlefield and the others where he had deployed his wives, thousands of Shadow Fiends were fighting to save the planets while also protecting his wives.
His legion was essentially undead.
As long as he remained alive, they could never truly die.
Because of that, he wasn’t overly worried about them, especially the Eternal Wrath Legion.
The battle was steadily moving in his favor, and after an hour, he could tell that even if he left now, the situation here would not worsen.
So he departed and began visiting the other planets.

chapters.title: Chapter 1817: The Dark War (19)
paragraphs: Kent left the battle on Planet Doorma to Tribe Chief Malthar and left for the second planet that Tower had pointed out as being at high risk of getting overrun.
Planet Kokoro is an all-Orc-dominated planet.
It is one of the few planets in the Eastern Region where humans are not welcomed. Orcs and humans don’t get along much, so naturally, no human with a functioning brain cell would go there.
However, today, they found themselves besieged on all sides by Dark Fiends.
It took only a few minutes for them to understand that their end had come. The Dark Empress had sent over 500,000 Dark Fiends, with almost half of them being Immortal Lords.

Basically, that was just too much for them to handle. Luckily for them, when things became dire, a new portal opened, and Lilian, Elsa, Selene, alongside some warriors from the Sky Fox Race, walked out and started to cut down the horde of Dark Fiends.

But even with the reinforcements, many Orcs kept dying, while some also chose to run for their dear lives. Regardless, the battle soon changed when Elsa finally met the requirement that had been holding her back for years.
She is the Soul Warden, leader of the Soul Sentinel, one of the most dangerous legions to ever grace the universe and battlefields with their presence.
When Kent awakened her true name, she was able to summon four Soul Sentinels. However, ever since then, she hadn’t been able to summon even a single Soul Sentinel.
She knew that if she could summon more, she would be able to offer more help in large battles like the one they were now fighting.
However, even during the battle in the Supreme Realm, the last requirement, which was unknown to her, remained unmet, preventing her from summoning them.
That was until now.
Just when she cut off the head of a Dark Fiend, she sensed her connection to the summoning reestablished. So she clapped her hands together and spoke the words.

"Standing with the authority of the Chief Soul Warden, I call ye all, my Soul Sentinels, to heed my call and take up arms once again. March into battle and cleave all filth from the face of the universe..."
She took a deep breath, and then her eyes shone brightly...
"Soul Sentinel Call."

Instead of portals, large gateways opened, and from within, hundreds of Soul Sentinels, each clad in silver armor, rushed out, some seated on beast mounts, others riding their weapons. In no time, over five thousand Soul Sentinels appeared, and more kept coming.
When Kent arrived, he was shocked to see that the number of Dark Fiends left was less than two thousand.
"What happened?" he asked, walking toward Selene, who was standing atop a stone platform, watching the last of the Dark Fiends get cut down.

"Don’t ask me, ask the Soul Sentinel wife of yours," Selene replied with a pout. Clearly, watching the Soul Sentinels kill, knowing their kills would count as Elsa’s, made her a bit jealous. So she used her chin to point in Elsa’s direction.
Kent laughed, planted a kiss on her forehead, and teleported to Elsa’s side. "I suppose you have finally met the requirement to summon your Soul Sentinels back from the dead."

Elsa jumped into Kent’s arms, causing the already jealous Selene to roll her eyes. "It appears so. However, I was only able to summon 10% of them. I need to raise my cultivation to the Demigod Stage to summon more."

"That is good to hear. But still, 10,000 gods is no small legion of warriors, Elsa. You should be proud of yourself. Also, you should head back to the Supreme Realm with your legion. Leave the bugs to Lilian and Selene."
Elsa nodded and allowed herself to be kissed before she vanished. A few seconds later, her Soul Sentinels were also gone. But she left 100 of them to protect her sisters.

This made Kent smile, knowing that to his wives, protecting each other was more important than their personal glory. Even Selene, who had been a bit jealous, smiled when she saw a lineup of 50 God-level Soul Sentinels bow before her.
"At least she isn’t as annoying as Big Sister Pandora," she muttered before joining the battle again.
Kent walked to Lilian’s side, and after sharing a kiss, he left for the next planet.

Tower kept updating him in real time, so he knew where to go next and what help to send. While he wasn’t able to get ahead of the Dark Empress’s threat, he was able to manage it and minimize the damage.
Many worlds would have perished had he not sent help when he did.
Kent was thankful that he had finally managed to awaken the Tower when he did.
If the Tower had been the previous version, perhaps it would have taken time to reverse-engineer the spell, or it might even have been impossible, leading to the destruction of dozens of worlds.

But that didn’t happen, and from the worlds he had visited, while many warriors and innocents had died, the death toll wasn’t anywhere near what it would have been without the help of his legion and wives.
Meanwhile, back on the Supreme Planet, the battle, while still chaotic, had been brought under control by the arrival of the Soul Sentinels.
Already, Grand Shaman Vorgun had created more Soul Fiends, so they were no longer being overwhelmed. Indie’s legion of Grim Reapers and Underworld Warriors also seemed to have worked wonders.
They were also crushing their enemies, and more importantly, Grand Shaman Vorgun, Veera, and Shade King Nykali kept adding to their legions.
After this battle, the three of them would probably have the most to gain since their legions of Soul Fiends, Undead, and Soul Wraiths would increase in both numbers and quality.
However, while the larger battle was devastating, another equally dangerous battle had finally come to an end. This was the battle between the Blood Ancestor and Han, the Grim Blade.
Of course, Han won, but instead of killing the Blood Ancestor, he allowed him to live, as per Kent’s instructions before he left.

"You are a weakling, Blood Ancestor. Just because you have become a Primordial doesn’t mean you are unkillable. You may have thought yourself untouchable, but the truth is, even if you had fought Big Brother, he would have wiped the floor with you.
So go back and never, ever show your face again. Trust me, it is for your own good."
Han turned away, vanished into the tide of Dark Fiends, and started cutting them down.
Meanwhile, the Blood Ancestor was left stunned, unsure of what to say. He was completely stunned, in shock, and utterly humiliated.
He had come with his shoulders held high, thinking he would finally be able to kill the one person he had dreamed of killing for years.
However, not only had he missed yet another opportunity to kill Kent, but he had also been completely defeated in combat by a mere Celestial.
And as if that wasn’t bone-chilling enough, the immortality that had made him invincible in the past meant nothing before Han.

It was as though a single swing aimed at his head was all Han needed to kill him. That was simply too much to bear, but in the end, he was spared, and now all he could think about was where to hide his face.
’I lost,’ he said inwardly, his body staggering back a few steps. Inwardly, he was just as stunned as he appeared on the outside.
Eventually, the words left his lips...
"I lost."

chapters.title: Chapter 1818: The Dark War (20)
paragraphs: The first time they met, Jest had just won a duel against a Sword Immortal who, over the years, had bragged that he was undisputed at the Sword Immortal Stage.
Many tried to defeat him but failed, except for Jest, who was already widely known as the Genesis Swordsman. He defeated him in less than five moves.
This caused Jest’s fame to skyrocket. However, that day, he also met someone whose understanding of the sword was deep and sharp.

The Blood Ancestor was known as Blood Eye Blade back then. They clashed in a fierce battle, one that caused an entire forest and the surrounding mountains to crumble to the ground. The battle was legendary.

However, Jest won, and despite sensing the Blood Ancestor’s killing intent during their battle, he spared him and left. Years later, they met again, and just like the first time, the Blood Ancestor attacked him.
Yet again, he was defeated by Jest.
It happened a third time, leading to his third defeat.

However, years later, someone issued a death match against Jest. Initially, he had planned not to go, but when word started to spread that he was afraid of a death match, something that had started to tarnish his reputation, he accepted the duel, and that was the first time he killed the Blood Ancestor.
However, 100 years after he had killed him, the Blood Ancestor returned, and ever since then, whenever they met, they fought, and Jest always ended up killing him.
It continued for thousands of years until Jest eventually lost interest in fighting him, since he had more pressing issues.
The last time they met, Jest defeated him, and he could have killed him for good. However, for some reason, he let him go.
Today, the Blood Ancestor had returned for revenge, thinking he would finally be able to defeat Kent and wash away the shame he had carried for years.

Unfortunately for him, the one who defeated him wasn’t even the person he had come after. It was plain disrespect, and when he thought he had finally reached the end of the line, he was spared, leaving him confused and humiliated.
Regardless, he had no idea what to do after such a defeat.
But seeing that no one was paying him any attention, after standing there for a few minutes, he opened the portal he had come through and left, not knowing what to think.
Maybe he would return again, asking for another beatdown, or maybe he would change his ways and finally come to terms with his defeat. Regardless, Han had brought him down a peg.

The battle grew even more chaotic for a couple more hours before things eventually calmed down. The tide of the Dark Fiends had died down considerably, causing the pressure on everyone to lessen a bit.
Meanwhile, on the other planets, some battles had come to an end, while others were still raging on, especially the ones taking place in the God Realms.

But while all this was happening, somewhere in the Celestial Realm, a woman clad in a red gown, with flowing red hair, stood atop a small hill overlooking a lineup of heavily armored warriors, each clad in metallic red armor.
The weakest among them were Demigods, and they numbered in the tens of thousands. The rest were Gods and Supremes, with about 5,000 Celestials and five Pseudo-Primordials.
The woman herself was a Primordial, known to all who were familiar with the Blood Temple as the Blood Empress.
She was one of the few people in the universe whom everyone knew not to mess with. Even the Celestial Supreme dared not provoke her.
The last thing he wanted was to incur her wrath.
It was said that, aside from the Soul Temple, the next cult to fear was the Blood Temple. Of course, many also said that the Blood Temple, like the Soul Temple, was an evil organization.
In a way, they were right, for people who cultivated blood generally did so by devouring the blood of the innocent. So the Blood Temple was branded an evil cult.
But in truth, they weren’t as evil as the Soul Temple, nor were they all rainbows and sunshine like the Divine Temple claimed they were.
They existed in the gray zone, and that alone made them an organization filled with powerful people whose loyalty nobody truly knew.
But one thing was certain. Unlike the Soul Temple, at least they were not looking to collude with outside forces to dominate the universe.
The Blood Temple had two leaders: the Blood Empress and the Blood Emperor. Most of the affairs were handled by the Blood Emperor. But the Blood Empress wasn’t inactive either.
She had her fair share of missions, and today, one had fallen into her lap from an unknown source.
"Listen up," her voice spread across the space, causing every murmur to die down.

"I have received word from a very reputable source that a major family in the universe has betrayed us all. They have colluded with the Dark Empress, who, as many of you are aware, was the true leader of the Dark Creatures that nearly destroyed the universe during the Dark Era.

"From the reports, the Jian Great Family has been keeping her alive and supplying her with resources for years. Naturally, that is something unforgivable, so we are being given the chance to exterminate them down to the last one in return for good karma and cultivation resources.

"Now, I don’t have to stress how important this mission is. If we can bring them to justice, we will naturally gain good karma, and as we all know, good karma means good luck. So everyone should give it their all and, most importantly, stay alive."
"Yes, Blood Empress!"
"Good. Now, you all can collect your mission tokens from the outpost before heading out. This time, I will personally escort everyone, so know that I will be watching."
They quickly dispersed and moved toward the outpost to collect the mission tokens they had been assigned.
Meanwhile, the Blood Empress looked to her left, where a lone figure with bruises around his left eye and a few cuts here and there stood, wearing a gloomy expression.
"Long day?" the Blood Empress asked, a smirk playing at the corner of her lips.
The Blood Ancestor turned to look at her and scoffed. "Stay away from me, Big Sister. I am not happy right now."
The Blood Empress finally laughed and walked toward her little brother, whom she had lived with since the Divine Era.
"I take it your rival is back, and judging by the bruised eye, things didn’t end well for you."
The Blood Ancestor said nothing, which told the Blood Empress everything she needed to know.

"Sorry, little brother. I know you truly wanted to defeat him, but we both know he isn’t someone to look down on. I myself have crossed swords with him before, and while it was just to test the waters, he was someone I knew could not be defeated easily.
"So losing to him is only natural."
"I didn’t lose to him. Rather, I lost to one of his subordinates. I believe you are aware of that lonely swordsman rumored to possess the strongest Sword Domain after the Genesis Sword Domain."
"The Grim Sword?" the Blood Empress asked, her brow furrowing.

"Yes, him. I lost to him in the most humiliating way possible." The Blood Ancestor gritted his teeth and added, "He dismantled my moves as though I were a child. Honestly, I am spent, so I will probably enter seclusion for a few thousand years to calm my heart."
The Blood Empress said nothing, but the expression on her face turned solemn.
"Where did this happen?" she asked.

"On the planet where the Dark Empress had been living. Oh, they were the ones who killed her, so if you want to find out who sent you the mission, maybe go there, I am sure they also recieved the same mission."
The Blood Ancestor vanished from sight, entering seclusion a few minutes later.
