I myself have crossed swords with him before, and while it was just to test the waters, he was someone I knew could not be defeated easily.
"So losing to him is only natural."
"I didn’t lose to him.
Rather, I lost to one of his subordinates.
I believe you are aware of that lonely swordsman rumored to possess the strongest Sword Domain after the Genesis Sword Domain."
"The Grim Sword?" the Blood Empress asked, her brow furrowing.
"Yes, him.
I lost to him in the most humiliating way possible." The Blood Ancestor gritted his teeth and added, "He dismantled my moves as though I were a child.
Honestly, I am spent, so I will probably enter seclusion for a few thousand years to calm my heart."
The Blood Empress said nothing, but the expression on her face turned solemn.
"Where did this happen?" she asked.
"On the planet where the Dark Empress had been living.
Oh, they were the ones who killed her, so if you want to find out who sent you the mission, maybe go there, I am sure they also recieved the same mission."
The Blood Ancestor vanished from sight, entering seclusion a few minutes later.

chapters.title: Chapter 1819: End of the Dark War
paragraphs: "Finally," Runa muttered, lowering her bow as ice seeped from her body, mixed with green colored lightning.
She, alongside Arien and Elina, had been sent to a god world where one of the Dark Gates had opened.
This god world had a population of 200 million, but only a million were warriors. The rest were scholars, people who strove for peace and knowledge.
Out of the million warriors, 10,000 were gods, with the rest ranging between the Demigod and True Immortal stages.
Naturally, the moment over a hundred thousand God-tier Dark Fiends appeared, the planet was doomed. There was no way they could handle such a tide of devastating Dark Fiends.
It appeared the Dark Empress had done her homework, picking the most vulnerable worlds to infest with her insidious spell.

Thankfully, just when things turned dire for them, the three ladies, alongside some of Veera’s undead warriors and Shade King Nykali’s soul wraiths, arrived and, as they were instructed, started killing just to save the natives.

Runa’s arrows were like missiles fired from powerful war machines. She is a member of the 14 Chronicles of the Storm, a team that rose from mere slaves to universe-shaping warriors whose arrows dominated the Great War.

Runa herself did the universe a great service during the Great War. Back then, when the Universe Guardians betrayed the Universe and the Chaos Dragon, things reached a point where, if no miracle occurred, Chaos wouldn’t be able to finish the Spell of Origin.
At that moment, it was Runa, then known as Aelthyr, who made the ultimate sacrifice. She burned her soul and bloodline to unleash an arrow that reversed time by an hour.
Within that hour bought for Chaos, he was able to finish the spell that brought the 13 Legions from the future. Her sacrifice gave the universe one last hope, and that hope saved everyone.
Today, she graced the battlefield with her chilling and devastating presence. Just like some of her sisters, she also uses a bow, and she is damn good with it.
Runa stood atop a stone parapet overlooking the vast battlefield that she and her sisters, alongside the guardians of Planet XBX, had protected, clad in silk armour.

Green, lush hair fell down her back, crackling with energy, and her deep green eyes also seemed to capture the chilling moment around her. She is undoubted one of the most beautiful women in the universe.
Her large, majestic bow, lined with ice and lightning runes, remained in her arms.

"I need a cold bath and good rest." She had gone out of her way to unleash some arrows that her current body wasn’t strong enough to handle. However, to ensure they ended the battle on a good note, she didn’t hesitate.
"Hey, are you coming down or what?" Arien called out from the ground, looking up at Runa, who seemed to have been caught up in the moment.

Looking down, she smiled at her sister, then jumped and landed before her. They embraced each other, knowing that even though Kent never came to watch them fight, the three of them, despite being Demigods, had each killed over a hundred gods.
Even if those gods didn’t have their own divinity and domains, they were gods regardless, each wielding divine qi, so their victory wasn’t one to look down on.
"I know I only recently joined the harem, but if you have to look at it, I knew Kent the longest, so don’t exempt me from the group hug," Elina said with a pout as she walked toward her sisters.
They opened their arms, and she jumped in like the spoiled brat she is.
This was her first official major battle after she had become the Nine Tribulation Dragon. So far, she had proven herself worthy of the power Kent had given her.
In the battle, the tactic that helped them was largely shaped by Elina’s overwhelming strength and the power of her Tribulation Lightning.

Arien, being a Foxkin who specializes in illusions, used a large portion of her power to create a very powerful illusion. While she knew she wasn’t at the point where she could affect thousands of Dark Fiends, she was confident she could affect them long enough for Elina to eliminate them.
As for Runa, her job was to watch her sisters’ backs, especially Arien’s, and make sure she wasn’t attacked in any way while her illusion was up.
Their teamwork was solid, and now it appeared they had each reached their limit.
Arien still looked as radiant as ever.

Her fluffy fox ears were streaked with soft silver-white fur. Long, flowing moon-silver hair with subtle violet streaks cascaded down her back like a waterfall. Her facial features were as flawless and sharp as ever, making her even more beautiful.
A mage’s robe, woven from Void Silk and layered with spatial threads, fitted her body perfectly.

As she looked at the beauty whom they had been told to keep alive no matter what, Arien’s silver eyes sparkled with love and joy. Elina was just like Unity; every one of her sisters wanted to protect her.
The two of them had been the most unfortunate in their past lives.
Just when they broke their hug, a couple of the warriors they had fought alongside approached them.
"Thank you, fairies, for aiding us in saving our planet. If you all don’t mind, we would like to thank you properly if you could follow us to the palace, where the Queen has humbly invited you."
Arien and her sisters exchanged glances.
A few seconds later, they made their decision.
Since their man grew stronger by becoming the guardian of worlds, then why not use this opportunity to make this planet one of his vassal worlds?

They followed them, but they made sure to inform their sisters on the other planets, some of whom were already meeting the leaders. They knew what was good for their man, so they weren’t wasting any time.
The battles on all 250 planets ended just as Kent wanted. Though many died, it was better than no one surviving or the planets getting destroyed.

Kent had managed to make it to 102 planets before the battles ended. Thankfully, none of his wives sustained any life-threatening injuries. Of course, some of his subordinates perished, but as long as he lived, they wouldn’t die permanently.
The last planet he appeared on was one where the battle would have overwhelmed everyone had it not been for one particular warrior he never knew would one day become this important.
When they first met, he was the son of a very evil man and someone who thought he could have Lilian for himself. That thought soon left his mind when he met Kent and got thoroughly trashed.

Later, Kent rescued him after his family had sent him away to die. He became a member of Kent’s inner circle, and over the years, under the tutelage of Kaizo and most of his legion, Krex had become a fine warrior.
But Krex was a cockroach, someone who just wouldn’t die even if he wanted to. He was incredibly hard to kill, and in this battle, he had proven to Kent why he deserved to be part of his legion.
Kent wanted to approach him to express his appreciation.
However, just before he could make a move, Vexthra’s voice entered his mind, causing him to open a portal back to the Supreme World.
"Uhm, my love, the Blood Empress requests your presence."

Kent walked through the portal, and the next second, he was back on the Supreme Planet, where the battle had already come to an end. However, the sky was now painted red, and a beauty stood in the air whom Kent had recognized long before she arrived.

chapters.title: Chapter 1820: Blood Empress
paragraphs: Of course, Kent never expected the Blood Empress to show up here, especially right after a battle that had drained his legion and wives.
The last time they met, it wasn’t on good terms, but it wasn’t on bad terms either.
In fact, Kent had no idea what went on in her head, so even if she had a bad impression of him, he had no way of knowing. At least from his perspective, they were neither enemies nor friends.
So, for her to appear here now, it could only mean one thing...

"I take it your brother came to complain to you like last time, and you’ve come for revenge," Kent asked with a smirk. "If that’s the case, then kindly give me a few days to recover before we fight, since I’m spent now."
Of course, it was a lie. With his regeneration abilities, he wasn’t tired at all. If anything, he welcomed more battles to build his endurance.
He just didn’t want to fight her, at least not when he would lose so easily.

The Eye of Chaos was still activated, so he could see through almost anything. Yet right now, not even a needle hole could be seen in this woman. This meant she had no weaknesses, or perhaps she did, but Kent was simply too weak to perceive them.
The second reason, of course, had to do with something Fiannarel and the Blood Warriors had said to him the moment he arrived on the planet.
"Little Brother, be careful around this woman. She is more than she appears to be."
They had all said the same thing, making Kent realize the Blood Empress he knew was far from ordinary.
The Blood Empress looked at Kent for a long moment before she spoke, causing Kent and his wives to widen their eyes.

"So that is how it is, huh? You were him all along," she smirked. "You know, I had my suspicions that somehow you were the Chaos Dragon, Lord Genesis, the Ruthless Bandit, and even that elusive shadow who used to call himself the Faceless Assassin."
She flew forward and landed two meters away from Kent before saying,
"It appears you’ve been busy, Chaos Ascension King."
"HUH? What are you talking about? My name is Kent, and yes, I am a Chaos Dragon, but not whoever you claim I am." Kent chose to feign ignorance.
While he had no problem telling his wives, legion, and some of his allies who he really was, this lady was a mystery, and he didn’t trust her.
Of course, his excuse would have worked if not for one tiny flaw...
The Blood Empress smiled.
"Oh, please, don’t insult my intelligence. Or do you think I wouldn’t recognize your fingerprint in all seven of these? I know your creations, Avalon, so there’s no need to hide anymore."
Kent frowned, locking into an intense stare with the Blood Empress. A few moments later, a sigh escaped his lips, and he asked,
"Who are you, and what do you want?"
"Oh, hey handsome. Why all the hostility? I come in peace, you know."
A smile escaped the Blood Empress’s lips, sending chills down Kent’s spine. He took two steps back, and the Blood Empress took two steps forward.

"You know, I never expected to find you here, Avalon... well, you said you’re Kent now. I thought you and that maniac brother of yours... what was his name again? Ah, Paragon. I thought you two had long perished in that foolish endeavor of yours."
She paused for a brief moment, her smile widening.
"I guess I was wrong. And with the universe being so kind, I’ve finally found you here. Only this time, I can kill you easily... really."
Kent took a few more steps back, but the Blood Empress smiled and advanced toward him. Fiannarel teleported to her brother’s side, and so did Grand Shaman Vorgun and the seven Blood Warriors.
Even the Tower seemed uncertain of the Blood Empress’s intentions, so it raised the cultivation of the seven Blood Warriors from Celestial to Pseudo-Primordial.
"Don’t come any closer, lady," Fiannarel warned, an arrow appearing in her hand. The others also started circulating their energy.
The Blood Empress spared her and the rest a glance before muttering a single word.
"Sleep."
To Kent’s horror, all his subordinates and wives, including his Big Brother, Grand Shaman Vorgun, went limp and passed out.
His eyes widened, but before he could make a move, the Blood Empress appeared before him like a ghost and placed her slender hands on his shoulders.
Kent instantly lost all access to his cores and everything that made him who he was. At once, he felt like a mortal again, back in the body he had on Earth.
He could even feel that his body had become completely ordinary, just as it had been back on Earth when he had no idea there were cultivators who could fly and unleash powerful abilities.
"I really wanted your head, Kent. You were the one person I always wanted to kill, yet not only did you ignore me, you never even considered me a worthy opponent.
"I was humiliated many times, and on top of that, I lost my chance to ascend back then because you took that opportunity from me, just as you’re going to take it from me again this time.
"So tell me, Kent, should I keep you alive knowing that one day you’ll take everything from me, or should I kill you, knowing I’d be doing the universe a favor?

"I mean, you’re the Chaos Dragon. You hid it well back then, but as it happens, old habits die hard, so you had to reincarnate as your true self. If I allow you to grow, you’ll bring calamity upon everyone... Ah, I forgot you also have another brother who is the embodiment of calamity.
"Seriously, Kent, do you always have to surround yourself with troublemakers? First, it was that white-haired bastard whom I’d probably run from if I met him..."
"Then maybe let go of my brother before I have to kill you this time for good, Phanesha."
A cold voice laced with sarcasm came from nowhere, yet it echoed everywhere.
Suddenly, space cracked apart, and a familiar face Kent couldn’t have been happier to see walked out, holding a bunch of grapes and casually munching on a few.
The Blood Empress, whose real name was Phanesha, narrowed her eyes the moment she saw Paragon emerge from the void.
"Paragon, what are you doing here?"

"What does it look like I’m doing, if not saving my brother from your evil claws? You know, I had my suspicions something like this would happen, so I left a fragment of my Primal Soul in this universe, waiting for you to show your face.
"I guess I made the right decision leaving contingencies in places else, who knows what evil you will do to my vulnerable and harmless brother.

"Jeez, Phanesha, how many times do I have to repeat myself? My brother doesn’t like you. He’s more into women who won’t try to kill him every time simply because he’s the second most handsome man after me, of course.
"Just take the hint and move on, or you’ll only end up hurting yourself."
Phanesha’s eyes burned crimson, anger surging behind them as she glared daggers at Paragon.
"Bastard, do you think I am afraid of you? You may be the Paragon, but right now you’re merely a Celestial. Killing you is simple, really."

"Oh, you think so? Just so you know, unlike my dear brother here, I don’t follow the rules, so you can’t cut my connection to the Daos and render me mortal like you did to them. So tell me, Phanesha, are you confident you can kill me before I sever your head?"

chapters.title: Chapter 1821: Compromise
paragraphs: Kent remained a mortal, vulnerable and weak, still held in Phanesha’s firm grip, her eyes burning with anger as she gazed back at the nonchalant Paragon, who threw a grape into the air and caught it with his mouth.
Watching this, Kent cursed inwardly, ’This bastard clearly is enjoying my peril.’
Kent also cursed himself for not having any knowledge of the life he had lived before all this.
It appeared that everything happening now was connected to the life in which he was known as Avalon, the same person he had suspected was somehow connected to him.
If he had any idea of that life, perhaps things would have been different for him.

But as it stood now, his life was in Phanesha’s hands, and he couldn’t ask for a better person to come to his rescue than that Paragon who, as it stood, had a much deeper rivalry with Phanesha than even Kent himself had with her.
Phanesha and Paragon had an intense staring contest for a few minutes before Paragon laughed.

"Relax, Phanesha. We both know if you kill him now, he would return, and what happened the last time would repeat itself. So how about we all take a step back and have an adult conversation where we both get what we want?"
"And what is it that you want?" she asked, still holding on to Kent. Normally, Kent would have loved to have two big boobs pressed against the sides of his head.
However, despite finding himself in such a position, his mind hadn’t even caught up to it.

"Well, I want you to first let go of my brother and apologise to him. I am not one to brag, but he has done more for this universe than you can ever imagine, so at least show some dignity. And about him being the Chaos Dragon, yes, he is chaotic, but in the good ways.
So cut him some slack and maybe, and this is a big maybe, but maybe, I might be lenient on you and not make things hard for you."

Paragon looked at the people passed out on the floor and added, "He hates it when someone tries to hurt his wives, you see, and right now, not only did you force them to sleep, but you also sent them into terrible nightmares that would leave scars on their minds when they woke up.
If I were you, I would release them now and beg for forgiveness."
"Huh, what kind of nonsense are you talking about? I merely sent them to sleep, not into any nightmare," Phanesha frowned, looking at Paragon with an angered expression.
Clearly, Paragon wanted her to seem more evil than she already was. Even Kent, who knew what had happened to his wives, couldn’t help but curse at Paragon for being shameless.
"Oh, my bad. I mistook you for an old rival of mine who loved to send people to sleep and then send their minds into a nightmare, leaving them scarred for life," he laughed and added...

"But I am serious. Let go of him, and I will let today’s events be a thing of the past." Phanesha didn’t want to, but she understood that offending Paragon when she had already offended the Chaos Dragon wasn’t good for her at all.
So after a few complicated emotional digestions, she let go of Kent, who immediately regained his abilities and power.
He glared hatefully at Phanesha, who smirked but said nothing.

Paragon patted Kent on the shoulder. "It would be good if you recovered your memories, buddy. Things are picking up much faster than we had anticipated, so the earlier you got things done here, the better."

"As for you, Phanesha, all of this started because you just can’t appreciate greatness. You and I both know when it comes to who rules, he is the one standing before you. So instead of hating him for taking the Primal Ascension Platform, maybe appreciate what you have.

Who knows, maybe one day you will get another chance. In fact, one of my wives has already located an Ascension Platform somewhere in the Primordial Chaos, so if you want, I can ask them to give it to you at a cost, of course."
"What do you want?" Phanesha asked, and in response, Paragon smiled and moved closer.

"You see, my dear brother had just recently inherited his legacy. Soon, he would start training it, and while I would say he had all the resources to fully train it, we both know that, unless someone from the bygone era aided him, he wouldn’t be able to fully cultivate it and reach the peak.
So when the time comes, become his training buddy. Once you are done training, I would be happy to share the location of the Primal Ascension Platform with you.
You know me, and you know I don’t lie, so do we have a deal or not?"
Paragon looked at Kent and gave him a simple nod that told him that, although he didn’t understand it now, a time would come when today’s deal would aid him in every way possible.

Phanesha thought hard about the offer and, after weighing the pros and cons, she nodded. "Very well. I will compromise with you two, but this is only because I want something more important than your life, Chaos Dragon.
One day, I will reach a level where you cannot ignore me any longer. When that day comes, be sure to prepare to die."
Kent smirked and said,
"I may not have memories of the life y’all are talking about, but I can feel it in my bones that even if I close my eyes and tie both hands behind my back, you couldn’t kill me."
Phanesha frowned, and Paragon exploded in laughter. "Good response, buddy."
Phanesha gritted her teeth but said nothing to counter what Kent had said. Rather, she sneered and turned to Paragon. "Better remember our deal, Paragon."
"I will, Phanesha, and hey, when you return to your main body, say hi to your mother for me."
"Hey, bastard, stay away from my mother, you shameless womanizer." Phanesha exploded with so much anger that Paragon jumped back a few steps just to escape her outburst.
"Womanizer is such a strong word, Phanesha. I prefer man of culture, and who are you kidding? Unlike you, who would never get laid, your mother is delicious and ripe for picking."
"I will kill you!" Phanesha charged forward, but a gateway opened before her, and she was pulled inside, leaving behind her angered voice.
"Tch, what an upright woman." Paragon turned and looked at Kent. "I pity you, buddy. Conquering her would be impossible."
Kent smirked. "And who said I have any plans on conquering her?"

Paragon just laughed and looked at the devastation caused by the dark war. "I suppose you succeeded, huh? Congratulations, buddy. Next, you should focus on spending some time with family. As for me, I will leave for now. I might pop up somewhere else soon."
He turned to mist and drifted off.
Kent took a deep breath and sighed. "What a tiring day."
He stared at his people, still sleeping, and sighed again. "Tower, wake them up."
Meanwhile, somewhere far away inside the Universe Ocean, a portal opened, and Phanesha walked out with a gloomy expression.
"Mother, why did you pull me away?" Phanesha asked, glaring at a woman who, just like her, had crimson hair and red eyes. It appeared she was also a blood cultivator.
She smiled and answered, "Haven’t you missed your mother? It has been 13 eras since we last saw each other, so why don’t you give me a hug?"

chapters.title: Chapter 1822: Blood Matriarch
paragraphs: Phanesha looked at her, the red-haired beauty who had her arms open, asking for a hug.
For a brief moment, she considered her options. She came close to landing a slap on Paragon’s face—which would have felt nice and vindictive—only to pull away by this woman.
The pain from that, and the fact that the Paragon had won one over her, made her consider not hugging her mother.
However, after a few seconds of acting spoiled, she walked into her waiting arms and hugged her.
"I miss you so much, Phanesha," the woman said, enjoying the hug.
"No need to be overly dramatic, Mother. It has only been thirteen eras. You sleep longer than that," Phanesha said with a smirk, causing her mother to pout.
"There is no need to be heartless, Phanesha. If you were to have your own children one day, you would understand just how a day away from them feels. Let me tell you, it is the worst feeling ever."
Phanesha didn’t reply to her mother, but she took her words to heart and decided to hug her a little longer. This made her mother very happy.
After five minutes, they broke the hug, and the woman scanned Phanesha’s body for a few moments before a smile formed on her face.
"How have you been? I can see you have fixed all the flaws in your soul. How is your brother? Still as troublesome as ever?"

"I have been well, Mother, and yes, I have fixed all the flaws in my soul, as you can see. As for little brother, he is still as chaotic as ever. He became a Primordial, but instead of focusing on his cultivation, he kept obsessing over defeating a rival of his, who I just learned was the reincarnation of Avalon."

"Oh, that doesn’t sound good at all," the woman said with a smile before adding, "He will probably snap back to his senses soon. Unlike you, he has always been a problem. I think I should have paid more attention to him."

"You are the Blood Matriarch, Mother. I am sure you have more important things to do than keep your attention on that brat. But yes, I am sure he will snap back to his senses after his recent defeat." Phanesha sighed and walked to a seat not far from where she had hugged her mother.
After sitting down, she turned and looked at her mother. "I am sure you didn’t drag me all the way here just to ask how I was doing. So why did you bring me here?"
The Blood Matriarch smiled and also walked to her seat.
"I certainly didn’t bring you here just for that. But I missed you regardless." She smiled, then her expression grew serious. "The reason I brought you here has to do with Avalon..."
"...He goes by Kent Madson now," Phanesha interjected.
"Sure." Blood Matriarch nodded, then she said, "I want you to send him a message for me."
Phanesha frowned, clearly not planning on seeking out that brat again. At least until the time came for her to train with him, she had no plans to be around him.

Kent was just too annoying, especially when Paragon was with him. The two of them were like the bane of her existence. They always found ways to anger her. If she got close to him, who knew what he would do next? Perhaps he might push her too far, ending in Kent’s death.
Seeing the expression on her face, the Blood Matriarch smiled.
"You know, I never thought a day like this would come, where you would frown at the mention of his name. He was your little crush when you were young, you know."
"MOTHER..."

Blood Matriarch laughed. "What is there to be angry about? Every friend of that brat has this unique talent for making beautiful ladies lose their minds. That said, he is a good person, and deep down, I know you know that too. So maybe cut him some slack.
"And for what it’s worth, if you had used that Primal Ascension Platform the last time, it would have ended in your death. Avalon... I mean, Kent, knew that, so he took the risk."
Phanesha’s brow furrowed as she listened to what her mother had said.

"It is the truth. He came to me before using it, and I personally inspected it. It was a Chaos-type Primal Ascension Platform, something you would have failed to use, and as we all know, failure means certain death during the Primal awakening. If anything, you should be grateful he took it from you.

"He is a good person, Phanesha, so instead of hating him, at least try to appreciate his selflessness. All eight of them are unique individuals whom none of us can compare to, so the least we can do is support them emotionally—or, in your case, physically and sexually."
"MOTHER!"
"Hehe." Blood Matriarch laughed, lifting both hands in mock surrender.
Phanesha merely smirked, somewhat wanting to return to Kent, who at the moment had no idea of the life he had lived before the universes were born. At least he wouldn’t be as annoying as her mother.
"What message do you have for him?" she asked.
Blood Matriarch waved her hand, manifesting a single-page manual.

"Hand this over to him. He will have to decipher it himself, since even I don’t know how. But tell him that even if he won’t remember who, the Weeping Monk said that what he wants is located here. By deciphering this anagram, he will get the answers he has been seeking.
"Apart from that, tell him that the tide is changing, so whatever he is up to, he had better hasten his pace, or he will be too late to do anything."
Phanesha grabbed the manual, scanned it for a few seconds, then stored it inside her soul.
"Is that all?" she asked, eager to leave before her mother became even more shameless.
Blood Matriarch waved her hand again, and several cultivation items appeared.
"Unlike you, your brother has lost his main body, so he will have to cultivate a new one. Give these to him, and make sure that until he is ready, he won’t fight that monster again.
"While that monster won’t kill him, he might become his heart demon, which we both know is even more terrible than death."
"I will do my best."
"That is all I want to hear. Be careful, though, and please don’t try to kill him again. If you force his hand, then even I wouldn’t be enough to save your skin."
"I don’t need you to save me, Mother. I can take care of myself, so maybe focus on yourself," she said with a smirk as she stood up, causing Blood Matriarch to chuckle.
"I will miss you too."
Phanesha ignored her shameless remark and shook her head.
"Send me back, please. Staying here is eating away at my sanity."
Blood Matriarch smirked and opened a portal for her. Phanesha merely smirked in return and walked through it. The portal closed behind her.
After she was gone, a figure clad in blood-red armor appeared. She had the same crimson hair, and her features were remarkably similar to Phanesha’s.
"Still hot-tempered, I see," she said with a smile, looking at the spot where the portal had closed.
"It seems so, big sister, but at least she isn’t slacking off. I just hope this time around she will learn to make friends and maybe create some bonds."
"You worry too much, Scarlet," the newcomer said, patting Blood Matriarch on the shoulder.
"Well, she is my daughter, so I have to worry about her. You will understand if you have your own child instead of spending your entire life moving from one battlefield to another."
The lady smirked.
"I am leaving, Scarlet. Call me if you need something that doesn’t involve lecturing me about the need to have my own children."
She vanished, leaving Blood Matriarch with a small smile on her face.

chapters.title: Chapter 1823: Aftermath
paragraphs: <You are now the Guardian of Planet XBX (God-Tier World)>
<You are now the Guardian of Planet Doorma (Immortal World)>
<You are now the Guardian of Planet Kokoro (God-Tier Planet)>
<You are now the Guardian of Planet Zhilakai (God-Tier World)>

Kent stood atop the shoulder of a large Celestial-level Dark Fiend Beast that Zaila had enthralled. During the final moments of the battle, she had unlocked a much deeper aspect of her Mind Cultivation Art, allowing her—just like Adina—to enthrall beings.
Adina had mesmerized her fair share of Dark Fiends, and the same was true for Ixeron, Kent’s beast companion, who possessed one of the most unique Mind Cultivation techniques in existence.
In short, Zaila could now enthrall beings, both humanoids and beasts.

Adina could mesmerize just about anyone, while Ixeron could place a Mind Hex on anyone. Of course, among the three of them, Zaila possessed the largest and strongest army due to how lethal her Enthrall ability was.
But Adina and Ixeron were no slouches either.
Regardless, Kent now found himself standing on the shoulder of a Celestial beast that would have probably loved to maw on him had it not been for its undying loyalty to Zaila.

Staring at the messages that kept appearing before his eyes, his smile could be seen from miles away. It appeared his wives and legion were doing great work, ensuring that the planets they had saved became his vassal worlds.
By becoming their Guardian, they now added to his growing soul strength, which he knew would expand his Soul Universe even further.
After this battle, he knew he would become a completely different person. But seeing these messages and feeling the changes happening within him, Kent knew things had taken a much deeper turn.
The battle had ended, but the gains kept coming.

Everything had ended as it was supposed to, if not for the small hitch with the Blood Empress. Regardless, Kent now knew he had to think ahead to what lay ahead and prepare for the danger he could sense slowly approaching.

He could tell something significant had happened, and that had led to this moment. Already, Paragon had revealed part of it, but for some reason, Kent could tell that was merely a tiny piece of the truth.
The main clue concerned the manual he had inherited with his legacy. Now, all that was left for him to do was unlock its pages and read.
He had already unlocked the first page, so soon he would learn something about the life that existed before all this chaos and mayhem.
The notifications continued for a couple of hours.
In the end, out of the 250 planets, 205 chose to make him their Guardian. Most of them were Immortal Worlds, but he had also become the Guardian of fifty-five God Worlds.
That alone was more than enough for him to accumulate an immense amount of Soul Essence, enough to nurture his Soul Universe and unlock some of its abilities.
He had held back both his Soul Universe and the Underworld Soul River during the battle because he could sense that they had undergone significant upgrades while he was training in the Chaos Chasm.

He had no idea how extensive those upgrades were, but he had no intention of testing them in a battle where his allies were present. If an asteroid were to explode now, what guarantee is there that the resulting shockwave would affect only the Dark Fiends?
He had no answer to that yet, so he held himself back. But with the influx of Soul Essence entering his soul now, he knew he could easily find a solution to whatever questions he had.
Eventually, the last of his wives and legion returned to the Supreme Planet where the main battle had taken place.

Lady Kenzie had already healed all of them, so physically, they were in perfect condition. However, mentally, they all needed some sleep to clear their minds. The battle they had just finished had demanded everything they had, so they were completely spent.
When everyone had returned, Kent cleared his throat and said,
"Thank you all for coming when I called. I know the battle was impromptu, but thanks to your dedication and contributions, we managed to close a Chapter of the Dark Era, making history."
They nodded, everyone happy that the battle was finally over.

"Now, before we all become too happy, it is imperative to understand that this is just the first of many battles we will find ourselves in. As most of you know, the Dark Empress came from the Dark Era, but like her, there are others out there, each eager and ready to try to conquer this universe, just as they did before.
"Many of you have fought in some of these battles before, so you can attest to the fact that what is coming is far more dreadful than this one.
"Because of that, I urge you all to train harder and prepare for the next one. We are what the universe will depend on from here onward, so at every turn, we must be ready to rise to the occasion.
"But I am proud of you all for coming through for me and for everyone. You will be rewarded accordingly when we return to the Tower."
They nodded, smiles appearing on their faces. Kent had already instructed the Tower to calculate their kills and convert each one into the Tower Points they had earned.

He planned to give everyone access to the Tower Shop so they could buy whatever they wanted. He would also give them the opportunity to train in the Chaos Chasm, since the Tower would soon establish a connection to it.
His rewards for them would surely surpass anything the universe itself could offer.
"For now, let’s return to the Tower, and I will relay further instructions there. I have some matters to handle here first."
They nodded and soon left the planet, returning to the Tower. Kent’s wives took Fiannarel with them so they could spend some time together.
Meanwhile, Kent was left alone with the Seven Blood Warriors and Uncle Drake.
Uncle Drake turned to Kent with a smirk.
"I suppose you will return to playing with Immortals and Gods now that the battle has ended."
Kent smiled.

"My life is a bit complex, so I will indeed return to such a life. But it won’t be for long, so whatever you have planned, you should speed it up. I have a feeling we will be entering another devastating battle soon."
"I will be ready. I have gained so much from this battle, so I will enter seclusion for a couple of years. Inform me if something comes up and I am not out yet."
"I will."

Uncle Drake nodded, bid him farewell, and teleported away. Kent knew that the next time they met, Uncle Drake would probably be even more powerful. Perhaps he would have reached the peak he once attained during the Primordial Era.
He looked forward to that.
Turning to the Seven Blood Warriors, Kent smiled.
"Thanks, guys, for the help. Things would have become dire if not for your support."
Veylan Seren laughed, as he always did, and replied,
"No need to thank us, Lord Kent. It has been a while since we fought in a battle of this magnitude. We all enjoyed it."
The others laughed in agreement.

chapters.title: Chapter 1824: Complete Annihilation
paragraphs: The Tower has merged back with her other halves, but she is yet to awaken, so for now, Kent planned to send the seven tribe leaders back to the Chaos Chasm to inform their people of the latest developments.
Tower said she would link or merge the Chaos Chasm with the tower, so it would become like another world inside the tower. It might even become the first world to merge with the tower.
However, since that place is for people who cultivate the Essence of Chaos, only those with a Chaos affinity would be allowed to go there.
Kent planned to offer cultivation techniques for cultivating Chaos Essence, especially to his wives and legion. This way, they can benefit from the overpowered nature of the Chaos Chasm.
But the natives of the Chaos Chasm can enter the tower and leave without having any special constitution or affinity.

Basically, Kent is focused on making sure his people have more powerful training companions. With Supremes, Celestials, and even Primordials available, they won’t have any shortage of sparring partners.
"You guys have to go back now and inform your people of the latest developments. Soon, portals will open in the various cities, and they will have the chance to enter the tower.
While it isn’t the vast universe out there, where there are millions of races, they would still be able to interact with people outside their race, which is more than enough for now."
The seven Blood Warriors, who are actually the seven tribe leaders, nodded. They are happy that, finally, they can leave the Chaos Chasm.
"Like I told the others, we will have more battles, perhaps much deadlier than this one, so you should be ready for whenever I come calling."

Kent knew that until he learned the main reason why he had created the Chaos Chasm and the seven races, he could only use the seven Blood Warriors as his personal weapons for the battles he planned on fighting soon.
The others in the Chaos Chasm can’t join, but Paragon told him they were created for a reason, so he hoped to know why he made them soon.
After instructing and thanking them, he sent them back to the Chaos Chasm. After they left, he took a deep breath before turning to the right.
"I suppose you haven’t returned to try and kill me again," Kent said, looking at an empty space. However, a few minutes after he spoke, Phanesha materialized out of thin air, frowning.
"How did you know I was here?" she asked, taking calm steps toward Kent.

"Sneaking up on me is impossible, even if you are the most powerful person in the universe," Kent said with a scoff, unbothered by the fact that he was all alone now with the woman who could easily snuff him out of existence.

"Strongest, you say?" To Kent’s shock, Phanesha smiled. "You really had no idea the kind of life you had lived, huh? To see me as the strongest in the universe clearly shows your ignorance is on another level. But who can blame you? By the standards set by the universe, I am indeed the strongest since I am a Primordial.
But if you think I am the worst thing out there, then you probably have another thing coming. But that isn’t why I am here."

She waved her hand, and the one-page scroll appeared. "Someone said I should give this to you. It can only be deciphered by you, apparently, so here you go," she said, making the scroll float toward Kent.
He caught it and, without scanning it, stored it in his space ring.

Phanesha said nothing about that but instead added what her mother, the Blood Matriarch, had asked her to tell Kent. "One last thing. I was told to tell you the tide is coming, so whatever you are up to, you’d better hurry before you’re too late.
That is all. See you later, or never." She was about to teleport away when Kent asked,
"How do I get in contact with you? You know about our deal."
She narrowed her eyes at Kent, but while the urge to slap him silly came to mind, she reined in her anger and produced a red token. "You can contact me using this."

She threw it at Kent, and before he caught it, she had long vanished. Kent grabbed the token, but to his shock, the force behind the throw sent him flying backward. He had to summon the Heaven-Splitting Jade Void Wings just to brace his fall.
"Bitch... One day, I am going to leave handprints on your ass," Kent cursed, feeling a painful sensation travel through his arm.

Somewhere in the void, Phanesha smirked. "He does have some strength in him, else he would have passed out by now." Regretting that she had missed her only chance to thrash Kent, she vanished deeper into the void.

Meanwhile, somewhere in the Celestial Realm on a planet known to belong to the Jian Great Family, chaos and mayhem covered every surface. Pools of blood mixed with fire and smoke permeate the entire place.

It appeared a terrible battle had occurred there, and from the look of things, every last member of the Jian Great Family had been killed. The only people still alive were children, pregnant women, and a few maids and guards who were not of the Jian bloodline.
It appeared whoever had sent the mission to the Blood Empress knew exactly what they wanted, so they made sure the core of the Jian Family was wiped out.
The Blood Temple agents had done a remarkable job cleaning the universe of such filth.

What Kent wanted to do had already been done by the Blood Temple, and it had been done thoroughly. They made sure the chances of the Jian Great Family ever rising back to their former glory were nonexistent.
In fact, given what had happened and the warning issued, those who had survived by chance would forever hide their identities as members of the Jian bloodline.
Colluding with the Dark Empress was just too insidious, and everyone who had a pair of functioning brain cells wouldn’t tolerate seeing a budding Jian Family ever again.

They had become enemies of the universe, and it all happened because of the mistake of a few. But with them used as scapegoats, it had now become clear to everyone that those who dared harbor beings who once tried to destroy this universe would not be tolerated.

The message had been sent out clearly, and the evidence was the river of blood left behind in the Celestial Realm. It had been made clear to everyone, and since it was the Blood Temple that had carried out the massacre, nobody dared question them.
Their reputation was on another level, so no one dared challenge their actions.
Not even the Universe Council dared question them. If only they knew that their hesitation and fear of confronting the Blood Empress was actually a good thing.

If they had come, then the already angry Phanesha, after enduring the teasing from both Kent and Paragon, would have unloaded her frustration on them. Perhaps some of them would have left her planet with broken bones and wounds that would never heal.
In a way, fear sometimes ruled, and these people had escaped a disaster simply because they were too afraid of the Blood Empress.

chapters.title: Chapter 1825: Tower Upgrades
paragraphs: Kent returned to the tower expecting to see the same thing. But to his shock, just the Mountain Garden was more than enough to tell him that a lot had happened.
The Mountain Garden, which used to overlook the cities while being rooted to the earth, now hung in the air, with waterfalls cascading down its four sides.

The garden was now much larger, decorated with all kinds of natural ornaments, while birds and butterflies filled the air. Aside from that, fruits and various natural treasures could be seen hanging all around.
His wives weren’t there, but he found Gaia and her friends having a tea party.
The moment they saw him, they all jumped into his arms. "Big Brother, we missed you so much."
"I missed you, ladies, too."
Now, the number of lolis in the tower had crossed ten. So unlike before, when it was only Gaia, Dori, and Akira, now, as they all jumped and clung to Kent’s body, he was completely covered.
Each of them found a spot to cling to, which surprisingly made Kent laugh, making him forget that he had just been in a deadly battle.
After hugging him, they dragged Kent over to join their tea party, which he happily accepted.
"Big Brother, are you finally back?" Dori asked after Kent had settled down, and they served him tea in a small cup. They were tiny ladies, so using such cups suited them well.
Kent took a sip of the tea before answering,

"Yes, I am finally back. I won’t be going anywhere for a while, so we will have more time to play. However, how about you girls come with me to check out the various changes that have happened to the tower? It could be fun, you know."
"YAY!"
They all jumped to their feet, ready to explore the tower with their Big Brother.
Kent was also happy they didn’t try to force him to stay and finish the tea first. They knew he was a busy man, so the offer to accompany him around the tower was everything they wanted.
After taking a few more sips of tea, they left the Mountain Garden and appeared inside the Legion Tower, where his legion was actively recuperating.
Some of them had even passed out. As for those who had died, they had been cocooned inside the Legion Tower, soon to be reborn.

Some had died saving their friends, while others had simply died because the opponents they chose were too strong for them to handle. Of course, when the Blood Ancestor arrived, some of them also perished because of his attack, which stopped Kent from killing the three Pseudo-Primordials at the same time.

Someone like Aetheris, the Flame Titan, died after taking a full-force attack from a Supreme-level Dark Fiend that had nearly ended Veera’s life. Even though she was a necromancer, she had sent all her undead into battle, while she herself was locked in combat against many Demigods.
She had been caught completely off guard. However, knowing how important she was to the battle, Aetheris didn’t hesitate to take the attack for her.
"Good thing the Legion Tower can revive them regardless of where they die," Kent sighed, putting it at the back of his mind to reward them when they were reborn.
But aside from the deaths that had rocked some members of his legion, several changes had appeared, with the most notable being the colossal arenas that had been added to the Legion Tower.
Before this upgrade, there were already arenas. However, they had now been redesigned so that each possessed a unique nature.

One of the arenas, called [Kaizo’s Colosseum], was built for brute fighters. The entire arena had been constructed to withstand any form of attack. Even if Primordials were to fight there, the chances of cracks appearing on its surface were next to none.
More importantly, if by some miracle someone managed to leave a crack in it, it would only take a few seconds and some Tower Points for it to repair itself.
Aside from that, the arena still retained its immortal nature, meaning that regardless of the attack or how gruesome the death was, the person would respawn.
Kaizo and Krex had died several times in the past, with Krex even holding the highest death count in the legion, totaling 1,242 deaths, with Kaizo following closely behind.
Now, the various arenas also broadcast battles throughout the tower, allowing people in other parts of the tower to witness the legendary fights that take place within them.

Aside from that, after every battle, the opponents involved would receive an evaluation from the tower detailing their mistakes and flaws in their attacks. This would allow them to correct those errors before going back into battle.

Lastly, and perhaps the biggest upgrade yet, was the introduction of the [Self Opponent] feature. Now, rather than asking for an opponent or sometimes even begging for one—something Kaizo did most often—they could create their own opponents.
The tower had already collected the combat data of every single person inside it, Kent included. So, with a mere tap of a button or a spoken command, they could create opponents for themselves.
It would perhaps become the most important feature in Kaizo’s life once he returned from his mission in the Undead Realm.

Every self-created opponent would have no flaws and could easily adapt to every form of attack. This, in addition to the arrival of the people from the Chaos Chasm, would, without a shred of doubt, benefit everyone inside the tower.
In total, there were fourteen arenas, each with a different design, taking into consideration the various abilities of the people living inside the tower.

Kent and his little minions explored the Legion Tower for a couple of hours, visiting all fourteen arenas. They also visited every single member of the legion, each of whom now had their own personal living space.
Kent made sure to thank them personally, which came as a shock to everyone. To them, going into battle whenever Kent called was the most important part of their lives.

They were his legion, so answering his call was their duty. However, Kent thanked them as though they had done him a great service. Surprisingly, this raised the respect they had for him by several degrees.
He also granted each of them access to the Tower Shop, allowing them to purchase items using the Tower Points the tower had already distributed to them.
Kent was now swimming in Tower Points, so giving each of them a share of what they had contributed during the Dark War seemed only right. In the end, they were happy, and he was very happy as well.
Before leaving for the Guardian Tower, he visited the cocoons of the seven who had died. They would, without a doubt, be compensated for their service as well.

Kent didn’t go ahead with the next plan the tower had come up with. He wanted the seven who had died to be reborn first before revealing who had achieved the highest kill count among all the members of his legion.
There was a special reward for the top three, so everyone was eagerly awaiting the announcement.ree
They soon left for the Guardian Tower, which, just like the Legion Tower, had also undergone many changes.

Before this upgrade, there were already arenas.
However, they had now been redesigned so that each possessed a unique nature.
One of the arenas, called [Kaizo’s Colosseum], was built for brute fighters.
The entire arena had been constructed to withstand any form of attack.
Even if Primordials were to fight there, the chances of cracks appearing on its surface were next to none.
More importantly, if by some miracle someone managed to leave a crack in it, it would only take a few seconds and some Tower Points for it to repair itself.
Aside from that, the arena still retained its immortal nature, meaning that regardless of the attack or how gruesome the death was, the person would respawn.
Kaizo and Krex had died several times in the past, with Krex even holding the highest death count in the legion, totaling 1,242 deaths, with Kaizo following closely behind.
Now, the various arenas also broadcast battles throughout the tower, allowing people in other parts of the tower to witness the legendary fights that take place within them.
Aside from that, after every battle, the opponents involved would receive an evaluation from the tower detailing their mistakes and flaws in their attacks.
This would allow them to correct those errors before going back into battle.
Lastly, and perhaps the biggest upgrade yet, was the introduction of the [Self Opponent] feature.
Now, rather than asking for an opponent or sometimes even begging for one—something Kaizo did most often—they could create their own opponents.
The tower had already collected the combat data of every single person inside it, Kent included.
So, with a mere tap of a button or a spoken command, they could create opponents for themselves.
It would perhaps become the most important feature in Kaizo’s life once he returned from his mission in the Undead Realm.
Every self-created opponent would have no flaws and could easily adapt to every form of attack.
This, in addition to the arrival of the people from the Chaos Chasm, would, without a shred of doubt, benefit everyone inside the tower.
In total, there were fourteen arenas, each with a different design, taking into consideration the various abilities of the people living inside the tower.
Kent and his little minions explored the Legion Tower for a couple of hours, visiting all fourteen arenas.
They also visited every single member of the legion, each of whom now had their own personal living space.
Kent made sure to thank them personally, which came as a shock to everyone.
To them, going into battle whenever Kent called was the most important part of their lives.
They were his legion, so answering his call was their duty.
However, Kent thanked them as though they had done him a great service.
Surprisingly, this raised the respect they had for him by several degrees.
He also granted each of them access to the Tower Shop, allowing them to purchase items using the Tower Points the tower had already distributed to them.
Kent was now swimming in Tower Points, so giving each of them a share of what they had contributed during the Dark War seemed only right.
In the end, they were happy, and he was very happy as well.
Before leaving for the Guardian Tower, he visited the cocoons of the seven who had died.
They would, without a doubt, be compensated for their service as well.
Kent didn’t go ahead with the next plan the tower had come up with.
He wanted the seven who had died to be reborn first before revealing who had achieved the highest kill count among all the members of his legion.
There was a special reward for the top three, so everyone was eagerly awaiting the announcement.ree
They soon left for the Guardian Tower, which, just like the Legion Tower, had also undergone many changes.

chapters.title: Chapter 1826: Guardian Tower Upgrades
paragraphs: Tower once told Kent that one day he would realise just how important the Guardian Tower is to his growth. That was three years ago, and today, he has finally seen it, and it is just too overpowered.
First, he had become the guardian of over 500 worlds, most added directly, with some added due to his influence.

For example, the medium worlds he had added before ascending to the High World had all become powerful worlds thanks to the resources he had left them, allowing them to spread their influence and win over other planets.
Now, he had become the guardian of 534 planets, with 220 of them being medium worlds. The rest are High to God Worlds, the places from which most of his gains keep coming.
Well, if this were before Tower had become whole, then he would have said his gains were only coming from the High to God Worlds.
However, things are very different now, or destined to become different, depending on what he does soon.
The moment he appeared inside the Guardian Tower, the messages that concerned that particular tower started to appear before his vision.

He quickly scanned through them, making sure he understood them well. In the end, they are all concerned about the newly awakened Guardian Dolls and other safety measures he can employ to strengthen and protect the worlds under his guardianship.

He had already purchased some and left them on the High Worlds he had become guardian of before ascending. Now, however, more have been added, and it appears he can purchase and remotely deploy them without being present.
Aside from that, he can upgrade the ones he has already purchased without recalling them first. He can remotely do any upgrade he wanted provided he has enough tower points or upgrade tokens.

But that is even the easiest part of it, since he only has to spend Tower Points, and the rest would be handled by the Tower. Kent knew he had some heavy purchases to make since he now had more worlds to protect.
They are aiding the growth of his soul essence, allowing his Soul Universe to grow more rapidly and unlock more abilities.
Of course, everything else was within expectation since Kent already knew that the more worlds he became guardian of, the more advanced the Guardian Tower becomes.
He, however, never expected the last message to show up, at least not while he never really saw something like that coming.
<You can now upgrade planets that are under your guardianship>
This measure had given him the chance to upgrade worlds under his guardianship, meaning he can upgrade medium worlds to High Worlds and High Worlds to Immortal Worlds.
It also means he can make God Worlds, Supreme Worlds, and so on. But as always, while this boon is something many would freak out about, Kent himself is freaking out.
But despite its overpowered nature, he knew there was a catch.

He dived deeper and saw that for a world to qualify for an upgrade, it must have reached some level of power. This power level had most to do with how many people living on these planets had reached some level of cultivation.

The max cultivation cap of a medium world is the Spirit Core Formation Stage, and to upgrade a medium world to a High World, there should be at least a hundred Spirit Core Formation Stage cultivators living in the world.

Back in Sonox, the number of Spirit Core Formation cultivators wasn’t even up to 50 when he arrived. Unlike the Immortal World, where there are many demigods, a medium world lacks resources, so producing Spirit Core Formation cultivators isn’t simple.
It can take someone almost their entire lifespan to rise to the rank of a Spirit Core Formation cultivator.
So, to upgrade them, there should be at least that many cultivators. But upgrading them naturally comes with so many benefits, the first being the lifting of their limitations.
They can rise beyond the Spirit Core Formation Stage and, more importantly, resources will be unlocked for them, allowing them to grow beyond that.
If a medium world upgrades to a High World, he would earn more soul essence, which is good for him.

Kent had already made provisions for some people who were much closer to the Spirit Core Formation Stage before he ascended. However, when he checked how many of these worlds qualified for an upgrade, only five met the requirements.
A few hundred are much closer, but he can only make five High Worlds now.
"Tower, how does it work?" Kent asked, hoping to hear from Tower. However, the silence soon made him aware that his lovely Tower was, at the moment, undergoing her complete awakening.
Luckily, he came with the next best people to answer him.
Dori looked at the message and answered:

"If the master issues the upgrade order, a planet-wide announcement would be made, alerting everyone to the upcoming changes that would rock their world. They would have time to prepare, since when a world awakens, the energy released is powerful enough to aid many breakthroughs.
Aside from that, the chances of there being a beast tide are high, so it is imperative to send adequate help to the planets involved before making any attempt to upgrade them."
"Oh, that makes sense." Kent had yet to upgrade a planet under his guardianship, but now that he had gained the power to upgrade them, his next plan would be to do that.
He tapped open the Guardian Store interface to review the various Guardian Dolls he had available. This time, they had been grouped by the planets’ ranks.

He reviewed them all, and to his shock, the dolls available were even more powerful than the ones he had already deployed. He knew he had to make some purchases, but for now, he placed a pin on it, since the last thing he wanted was to get carried away and spend more Tower Points than he could afford right now.
It is true that he is swimming in Tower Points, but that doesn’t mean he can just misuse them.
After learning from the 250 planets the Dark Empress had attacked, he knew he had to protect them well before things got out of hand next time.
The next place inside the tower he visited was the portals that led to the worlds he had become guardian of. Now, he could easily go there by simply walking through a portal.
"These upgrades would make things much easier should any of the planets under my guardianship come under attack."
After making sure he had covered every new upgrade inside the Guardian Tower, he left for the Inheritance Tower, where the various inheritances still remained.

Surprisingly, new inheritances had appeared, including even a few Primordial ones. This means whoever inherits them would have the cultivation arts of a Primordial and a sure chance to become a Primordial one day.
Kent was taken aback by this discovery, but he played it cool, knowing that once Tower was done, they would plan how best to handle these inheritances.
Because of such an inheritance, Elina had become the Nine Tribulation Dragon. If he can get more like her, then who is to tell what kind of power he would soon command?

He didn’t linger much in the Inheritance Tower since he ran the risk of overstaying if he started reading every detail about the inheritance. Some of the inheritances are just too wild. They came from people he knew, some friends, and many foes.
Later, he would dive deeper into all of them.
His next destination was the Dungeon Tower...

chapters.title: Chapter 1827: Two Black Dungeons
paragraphs: Most of the dungeons inside the Dungeon Tower have been cleared, leading to more warriors who make up the Eternal Wrath Legion joining the team. This was how the Eternal Wrath legion now numbers in over a hundred, making them the largest yet.
However, many dungeons are still pending clearance. Some appeared a couple of hours ago, with more to come when Tower is done.
Kent didn’t come for any of them.

He came here for the Black Dungeons. He was advised by Tower to ignore it the first time he saw it. So far, there are dungeons inside the tower with last-floor bosses seated comfortably at the peak of the Celestial Stage.
But the Black Dungeon is a mystery, one that Kent planned to figure out.
To his shock, however, when he appeared inside the Dungeon Tower, instead of one Black Dungeon, there were now two, and more importantly, they were now oozing unique auras.

The first one gave off a cold ice aura, and the second came with a flame-type aura. Feeling both, Kent felt a bone-chilling killing intent seep into his body, the kind that made him question whether or not entering these dungeons would be a wise decision.
"Big Brother, I feel like these dungeons are calamities waiting to happen," Akira said, holding on to Kent’s left arm. Well, judging by how small she is, she held on to his pinky...
"That is indeed true, Akira, and I had no plans on entering either of them right now. I first have to gather some information, or else I might just end up walking to my doom."

Inasmuch as he wished to handle whatever horrors the two Black Dungeons were holding, he knew he had to tread carefully. So he would first wait for Tower to gather whatever information it could find before walking into either of them.
He soon left the Dungeon Tower with his lolis and headed out to the Tower Cities.
The upgrades affected the cities, too. However, compared to how extensive the changes inside the mountain garden had become, the changes to the cities were minor.
But he was glad to see dozens of natural islands had appeared in the Tower Cities. These islands could be converted into dwellings for some of the high-ranking members of the various cities.
While Kent was handling matters in his front, somewhere on the Dead Planet, Uncle Drew and his team were surrounded on all sides by agents of the Soul Temple.
It had been weeks since they had arrived on the Dead Planet following the mission Kent had given them.
They had made so much progress, but likewise, problems were bound to happen, and this time, it was with the Soul Temple agents.
Weeks ago, Uncle Drew and his team had killed some agents from the Soul Temple who had been following them and had planned to use the ambush by the Sand Centipedes to pull a fast one on them.
Unfortunately for them, Uncle Drew had long noticed them, and so, while they were unaware, their lives were taken in one decisive attack...
But they didn’t die without alerting their fellow agents. Long story short, reinforcements from the Soul Temple arrived, and they started following the trail left behind by Uncle Drew and his team.
At first, it appeared they wouldn’t catch up to them, but along the way, Uncle Drew and his team were ambushed by some warriors from the Zahki Clan.

They had killed a member of this clan before entering the Death World. So they, too, had come for revenge, and despite Uncle Drew and his team doing their best to handle them swiftly, their battle dragged on for hours, resulting in the Soul Temple getting wind of them.
Now they had caught up to them and surrounded them, weapons drawn...
"So you are the people who dared kill members of the Soul Temple," a lady holding a dagger with short black hair asked, looking at Uncle Drew and his teammates like they were bugs.
Uncle Drew looked at her narrowly, then smirked. "You make it sound like your so-called Soul Temple is made up of sacred beings that are beyond death... How stupid."

The lady who asked the question didn’t react negatively, which told Uncle Drew and his team she was not an easy opponent. While the 24 who came with her clearly looked poised, she surprisingly had a good hold on her emotions.

"Do you know what happened to the last person to kill an agent of the Soul Temple?" She let a smile form on her face, her deep black eyes scanning Nara as she continued. "Their death was slow and painful. Later, they became the meal we feasted on, and let me tell you, such souls are the most delicious.
"Right now, I can smell the taste of your souls, and damn, you people have the best ones I have smelled yet. I am going to enjoy feasting on your souls."

Vargus lifted his giant axe off his right shoulder and rested it across his shoulders. "For reasons I can’t place my finger on, I think you will die miserably today. Call it a gut feeling, but your death will be brutal." He laughed and added,
"Of course, there is a way to save your skin, and that is to turn back and walk away with your minions. Trust me, I am not one to advise anyone, so take my words seriously."

This time, the lady frowned, and a deep killing intent mixed with Soul Qi seeped out of her body. It appeared she planned to fight after all, which, from where Vargus stood, sounded like a very bad idea.
Despite being surrounded, none of them panicked. In fact, they even pitied the 25 Soul Temple agents surrounding them.
Their confidence, of course, came from Eryndor...
"It appears feasting on your souls is the path you have picked, huh?" the lady sighed and turned to her teammates. "Guys, it appears we will have to do it the hard way."
They smiled, and they were about to charge forward when Eryndor lifted his staff and commanded,
"Hell Gate... Open."
Before any of them could move, the large Hell Gates snapped open, and from the first gate, Thrakos, the Demon of Dread, stepped out, a wide grin painting his face.
Zandros, Kha’zixarath, and Xuanli also came out of their separate Hell Gates, bringing with them a dreadful feeling that immediately caused the 25 Soul Temple agents to panic.
But it was already too late to regret.
"Guys, kill them, but make sure it is slow and painful," Eryndor gave the order, and the grins on his four Hell Demons’ faces sent chills down the spines of the Soul Temple agents.
"Ah, what a day to be alive," Thrakos said, scanning the Soul Temple agents like they were food served on a silver platter.

"It is rather sad, really. I never expected to be called back to fight after the chaotic one we recently fought." Xuanli looked at the leader of the Soul Temple agents and shook her head. "You are unlucky to have met me."
That was the last thing she heard before her soul was forced out of her body.
The next second, she and seven others found themselves on a battlefield, standing on one side while the other side was filled with thousands of souls ready to attack...
The next second, they attacked, and all eight of them were swallowed by the chaos of battle.

chapters.title: Chapter 1828: Black Star Domain
paragraphs: Uncle Drew and his teammates stood atop a small hill overlooking the devastated battlefield where the Hell Demons Eryndor had summoned were raining down destruction on the Soul Temple agents.
"We warned them, so this is all their fault," Nara said, taking a deep breath. She didn’t seem that bothered since the people being attacked were their enemies.

"But who could blame them? They saw a group of seven weaklings and thought they had struck it rich," Saden said with a chilling smirk. She really had no pity for these people. If anything, she wished to join Eryndor’s Hell Demons in torturing them.
Alas, they had to rush to the Black Star Domain, the main location of their mission.

"Let’s go. I have a feeling something big has happened back home, so the earlier we get things done here, the better. I wouldn’t want us to return to much stronger versions of the weaklings we left a couple of months ago," Uncle Drew said, drawing his teammates’ attention away from the onslaught happening below them.
They each had a sense that something big had happened while they were gone.
They asked their friends back home, but everyone said they had been clearing dungeons ever since they left. Of course, Uncle Drew and his teammates didn’t believe them.
The first sign came when their connection to the tower became much stronger. This told them the tower had become stronger in their absence.
But if that was normal, considering they had witnessed the tower grow every now and then, the second change that drew their attention clearly made them believe something had happened.
The second change was the sudden loss of connection with some of their pals.
Every last member of the Legion had a connection to each other, just as Kent had a connection to his wives.

So during the Dark War, when some of them died, they lost that connection for a few seconds before it faintly formed again. It reformed when the cocoons currently holding the bodies of the dead legions appeared in the legion tower.

They had experienced it before, so Uncle Drew and his team knew a big battle had happened and that some of them had died. For some reason, they all felt like the battle that had happened was one they were supposed to be in.
Of course, it was true that, at one point during the Dark War, they were also having their fair share of battles, so Kent couldn’t afford to pull them away.

But during the Dark Era, they were the ones who stood against the dark creatures, so perhaps the conclusion should have involved them. Unfortunately, they missed it, but they weren’t planning to miss the next one.
They were much closer to the Black Star Domain...

"I am just happy Kaizo isn’t around to have some fun. I can already imagine his reaction when he returns and finds out something big had happened in his absence," Vargus said, and his friends laughed.
Just anticipating Kaizo’s devastated expression put their minds at ease and even made them happy. His plight would surely make them very happy.
"Let’s go. We have quite the ground to cover."
They soon left, heading deeper into the dead planet. The battlefield they left behind for the four Hell Demons would surely end with devastation and regret.
But they had no plans on witnessing that.

Of course, Eryndor could witness everything through the eyes of his four Hell Demons. But he had no plans to since he knew the order he had given them would end with the death of every last soul temple agent.
He even wondered just what the Soul Temple would do when another set of agents suddenly died. Naturally, he looked forward to that.
After 15 hours of flying, the Night Riders finally arrived in the Black Star Domain.

"When the master said the Black Star Domain is a dangerous place in all of the Dead World, he clearly failed to do justice to just how dangerous it really is," Saden said, looking at the vast and scorching stretch where their mission officially begins.

All they knew was that when they arrived in the Black Star Domain, they were going to officially start their mission. However, Kent never said what kind of mission they were on. He only said that when they saw it, they would know.
Now they were in the Black Star Domain, and despite just entering it, they could already sense the danger.
Of course, while everyone sensed danger, one teammate wore a slight frown. Uncle Drew noticed the frown on Nara’s face and asked, "Is everything alright, Nightblade?"
They each had code names, with Nara, his second-in-command, being Nightblade.
"I am not sure, but I think the Night Heart is here, in the Black Star Domain."
"REALLY?" The rest of her teammates widened their eyes upon hearing what Nara said.

"Like I said, I am not sure, but I can sense it coming from deep within this place. Honestly, I might be wrong, but if I am not, then I think the mission has to do with us retrieving the Night Heart."

The Night Heart is a sacred relic carried by the Night Maiden during the Dark Era. It unlocked the 14th level of Hell, the realm where the Night Riders have their powers chained, waiting for them to reclaim them.
It was said that when the 69 Night Riders died, their various legacies returned to the Realm of the Night, waiting for their rightful owners to reclaim them.

Right now, they each have partial legacies. However, with the Night Heart, which only Nara can wield, they all can reclaim their full legacies and, more importantly, they can locate the rest of their members easily.
"What are we waiting for? If the Night Heart is here, then we should retrieve it fast. The faster we get our hands on it, the faster we can finally have the gang back together again."
Riding into battle with all 69 members sure would be a sight to behold. After all, the Night Riders are known for their aura, especially when riding into battle using their Hellhorses.

"We have to first make sure it is indeed the Night Heart," Uncle Drew said before turning to Saden. "You should take point on this one, Midnight Arrow. Your affinity for shadow and true darkness is perfect for this mission."
Saden nodded and activated her shadow. At once, an identical copy of her appeared and merged with Nara’s shadow.
"I will scout ahead and let you know what I find. Should I die, you all should stop following and wait for me to awaken first."
They nodded, and soon she was gone.

Her shadow spirit inside Nara’s shadow is her way back from the dead. While one death cannot claim her soul, two would do, so she left her shadow spirit with her teammates and ventured into the scorching depths of the Black Star Domain, knowing she could easily die if she messed around.
Luckily for her, she is a Night Rider with an affinity for flames, shadow, and darkness. This place is like a swimming pool for her.
After waiting 30 minutes, Uncle Drew and the rest of the Night Riders ventured after her, making sure they kept an open focus, scanning for the first sign of danger.
