chapters.title: Chapter 1829: Black Fire Demon Dragon
paragraphs: "Captain, I think I have located the source of the Night Heart, but I am not sure we can handle it," Saden’s voice rang in her teammates’ heads four days after arriving in the Black Star Domain.
She had taken the lead, scouting ahead to see if there were any dangers.
During the scouting mission, she had managed to evade most of the dangers but also encountered some truly chilling ones.
Regardless, after traversing the scorching and dangerous vastness of the Black Star Domain, she had arrived at the location where she knew their final mission would take place.
Uncle Drew and his teammates teleported and appeared beside her. Naturally, the moment they arrived, their gazes landed on the thing that made Saden say she wasn’t sure they could handle it.

That was because the creature they were looking at was a monstrosity like no other. It was a black dragon, its body three times Kent’s dragon form. Meaning it was 3 km long, which by dragon standards was large enough to be regarded as an Overlord.
But not only was this one no Overlord, but it was also dead—well, it was alive but dead.
It was an undead dragon at the rank of a Demigod, but none of the Night Riders believed the dragon before them was a Demigod. In fact, they didn’t believe it was even a god.
Its claws alone were enough to send shivers down the spine of anyone. And they sure did send shivers down the spines of the Night Riders.

"Looks like we have our work cut out for us, literally," Uncle Drew said with a smile, gazing at the giant dragon currently slumbering in the middle of a lava pool formed from a sea of flowing black flames.

"Whatever we are after is hidden beneath it, so regardless of how terrifying it may appear to be, we must kill it or find a way to get the Night Heart away from it," Nara revealed. Since she had the strongest connection to the Night Heart, she could feel the exact direction it was coming from.

"Killing it is impossible, so we should plan for a snatch-and-grab," Uncle Drew stated, not trying to hide the impossible nature of their mission. It wasn’t because they lacked the strength; they had plenty of that.
It was just that the dragon was far beyond anything their combined strength could handle.
The most they could do was fight it and find a way to take what they had come for. But looking at the monstrosity, Vargus couldn’t help but ask,

"I am not one to shy away from a good and impossible battle, but do we really wish to fight this dragon? I have this feeling deep within me that our deaths are currently slumbering there. It has no flaws from what I can perceive at the moment."
"If we play our cards right, then surely we can complete this mission. However, we will need the four Hell Demons, so Eryndor, summon them again."
Eryndor nodded and summoned his four Hell Demons, who had long finished torturing and killing the Soul Temple agents.
Now, they would get to fight something far beyond them.
Of course, when they appeared, all four of them sensed the challenge, and so they took a deep breath.
"Master, I never knew you held us in such high esteem. But aren’t you overestimating us a little?" Xuanli said, a small giggle escaping her lips.
"I mean, look at the monstrosity we are being asked to kill. This creature is straight from those dreadful zones in Hell, even more dreadful than the domain I ruled back then."
Eryndor laughed at Xuanli’s attempt to make them aware of the danger.
"We are going to fight it, and some of you may die or, worse, sustain grave injuries. Just so you know, I sympathize with you and promise to reward you later."
His four Hell Demons smirked, their expressions brightening up a bit. They recognized the challenge and, as Hell Demons, wished to live up to their master’s expectations.
Uncle Drew knew the plan had to be solid, so after three hours of strategizing, they were ready to move out.
"Good luck, everyone. If things end well, we will see each other later. If not, then see you on the other side."

With those final words, a shadow moved across the landscape at a terrifying speed, approaching the dragon. Just when Saden entered the 5,000-meter radius, the dragon snapped its crimson eyes open, waves of death qi emanating from them.
A powerful pressure descended upon the scorching field where the chaos of battle would soon reshape the landscape.
Saden staggered, but she quickly regained her balance and continued moving.

"You got this, Saden," Saden said to herself, pushing forward. Just when she entered the 500-meter range of the dragon, she stopped, and in her place, Vargus appeared and threw his battle axe, enchanting it with his energy.
The axe grew to 200 meters in length, with the blade alone measuring 100 meters.
Green flames mingled with lightning to bathe the axe.

This sudden change in the air made the dragon raise its head, or at least try to move. Just before it could lift its head, three Hell Gates opened above it, and Thrakos, Kha’zixarath, and Zandros jumped out, landing on the metallic back of the dragon.
They attacked at once, dividing the poor dragon’s attention. This split second of distraction gave the battle axe the perfect opportunity to land, and it did.
BOOOOM!
A powerful explosion rocked the landscape, sending a shockwave of black lava into the air.
"Oh, this is a bad idea," Nara said, but through the chaos and shockwave, she activated her Night Rider form, taking on the appearance of a wraith.

She is a half-demoness, half-wraith after all, so she assumed that form, discarding her physical body. The next second, she faded out of existence, and when she reappeared, she stood before the giant dragon, her 12-meter wraith form wielded a 14-meter-long greatsword poised for an attack.

Because the three Hell Demons had already distracted it, when Nara appeared, the dragon was caught by surprise. But she didn’t hold back for even a moment. She went for the kill immediately, her greatsword trailing green flames.
BANG!

Her sword struck the dragon’s neck as it tried to raise its head above the angle of the blade, but failed miserably. The sword landed squarely on its neck, and for a brief moment, one would wonder if death was certain.
However, when the dust cleared, and not even a dent appeared on its neck, the natural reaction should have been for Nara to widen her hollow wraith eyes.
But instead, she smiled chillingly. Then, still in her wraith form, she faded out of existence, her greatsword turning into mist.
The next second, the dragon lifted its head and roared furiously. Unfortunately for it, the attack had already been delivered, and the results were immediate.
Inside its tainted soul, Uncle Drew, Saden, Lene, and Xuanli appeared, thanks to Xuanli’s uncanny ability to transport tangible beings into the soul of anyone she came into contact with.
Standing 10 km away atop a mountain with the lolis, Kent smiled, seeing how well the series of attacks that had unfolded in less than two seconds had played out.
"Now then, show me how you can take down this monstrosity."

chapters.title: Chapter 1830: Dual Plane Assault
paragraphs: The plan was rather simple, yet it required decisive action.
Vargus, Nara, Eryndor, and the three hell demons were meant to attack on the outside, while Uncle Drew, Xuanli, Lene, and Saden were meant to attack in the soul plane.
This plan was possible simply because Xuanli was perhaps the only person in existence who could transport physical beings into the soul plane.
With her uncanny ability, Uncle Drew, who was known for his strategic planning and insidious ideas, came up with perhaps the most badass plan ever, allowing the battle to be split in two.

The problem, however, had to do with how they would get themselves into the soul of the Black Fire Demon Dragon. Xuanli would have to make physical contact with it before she could pull herself and everyone else into its soul.
But getting close to the dragon was, as one would say, virtually impossible. However, there was a solution, and it came in the form of a wraith.

Nara’s bloodline allowed her to take on the form of a wraith, so she activated it, allowing her to become nothingness. That nothingness allowed her to bypass the pressure being produced by the Black Fire Demon Dragon.
While she couldn’t maintain that form for long, she could keep it activated long enough to get close to the Black Fire Demon Dragon.
So Xuanli turned into a giant sword, and within her were hidden Uncle Drew, Saden, and Lene. All Nara had to do was get close and attack, which she did.
With the sword making contact with the Black Fire Demon Dragon, Xuanli entered its soul, bringing the others with her.
Now, the battles on the outside and inside the soul would be determined by how long they could hold on.

After all, despite invading its soul, the Black Fire Demon Dragon was able to keep its composure on the outside. It shook off the three hell demons and even unleashed a breath attack, pushing Vargus back.
But now that it had to defend against soul attacks, the battle on the outside had to be won no matter what.
Nara eyed the crystal on the Black Fire Demon Dragon’s chest and sighed. That was what they came for, and to get it, they would have to defeat the Black Fire Demon Dragon once.

Since it was an undead dragon, death was basically something they could not guarantee. But they didn’t need it to stay permanently dead. They just needed it to die for a few seconds so they could take the Night Heart.
"Vargus, keep it distracted. I have a plan," Nara, now back in her humanoid form, said before taking a step forward and disappearing from sight.

Vargus sighed and nodded. Then his body exploded with so much force that the ground beneath his feet split apart. He also disappeared and reappeared before the Black Fire Demon Dragon before attacking.
His axe carved a deadly arc through the air, landing a huge blow on the dragon’s side. However, instead of leaving a cut, his axe bounced back, sending vibrations through his arms.
He was besieged the next second, a powerful tail arriving before him like a whip. Luckily, Thrakos arrived and blocked the blow, sending a powerful shockwave flying in all directions.
Zandros and Kha’zixarath also attacked, but even though they poured all their energy into their attacks, not even a dent appeared on the hard, metallic-like skin of the Black Fire Demon Dragon.
"Just great. At this rate, we might as well tickle it," Vargus said with a smirk, jumping back to evade a claw attack. He knew he had to keep it busy, just as Nara had instructed.
Luckily for him, he wouldn’t have to do it alone since he had the three hell demons with him. But there was someone else who had been missing from the battle.

Eryndor seemed to have vanished from the battlefield. However, in truth, he had flown much higher and was setting up an attack formation that, if he could complete it fast enough — or at least before Vargus and the others were overwhelmed — would tilt the battle in their favour.
Of course, Nara also seemed to have something planned, but for now, Vargus and the three hell demons would have to hold back the Black Fire Demon Dragon for as long as they could.
Inside its soul, however, things were much different.
The Black Fire Demon Dragon had formed thousands of soul dolls, each imbued with the power of death and darkness.

Uncle Drew and the team inside its soul were now locked in a deadly dance of death and slaughter, the kind that would require one of two things: either they kill faster, which, according to Xuanli, would make its soul vulnerable, allowing them to wound it, or they get overrun and die in there.
So far, they were holding their own.

Uncle Drew had already gone full-on battle mode, cutting down one soul doll after another. In fact, he was cutting them down so fast that even the Black Fire Demon Dragon seemed to feel threatened by him.
Uncle Drew didn’t want the battle to last long, since he had already sensed danger nearby, so he wasn’t holding back at all.
And he wasn’t the only one. Lene was like a blur of death, her spear stabbing, slashing, and shattering the soul dolls every second. Wherever she passed, dozens of soul dolls died.

Saden was equally lethal with her bow. She had augmented her body and bow with her shadow spirit, so every arrow she fired was several times stronger than it would have been if she hadn’t augmented her bow.

As for Xuanli, since she was versed in soul attacks, she was the one dealing the most damage. She had unleashed her own soul army, making sure they fought and perished, knowing that regardless of the outcome, they needed only one death.
But achieving that was impossible, especially when the more they killed, the more soul dolls kept coming.
"I really hope the battle on the outside is going well. Beating an undead soul is virtually impossible," Xuanli said, plucking more strings on her zither.
"Just focus on keeping it distracted here. I trust them to pull it off," Uncle Drew said, cutting down soul dolls like they were bugs.
Kent remained standing with the lolis, watching the battle with a calm expression.

While only a few days had passed on the outside since the Dark War, months had passed inside the tower, so he had done so much, even fully exploring all the towers with the exception of the Harem Tower.
This meant that, aside from a couple of things he had planned for later, he was free to do whatever he wanted.
He had initially wanted to use the time to spend some relaxing moments with his wives, but they were with his sister, who had become something akin to both their teacher and friend.
They had said that when they were done, they would let him know.

So he left for the Dead World when he learned Uncle Drew and his team had arrived in the Black Star Domain. Knowing the kind of horror they would be facing, he decided to come and watch, and if they needed help, he would offer it.
So far, he was calmly standing there, watching the battles on both the soul and physical planes.

With her uncanny ability, Uncle Drew, who was known for his strategic planning and insidious ideas, came up with perhaps the most badass plan ever, allowing the battle to be split in two.
The problem, however, had to do with how they would get themselves into the soul of the Black Fire Demon Dragon.
Xuanli would have to make physical contact with it before she could pull herself and everyone else into its soul.
But getting close to the dragon was, as one would say, virtually impossible.
However, there was a solution, and it came in the form of a wraith.
Nara’s bloodline allowed her to take on the form of a wraith, so she activated it, allowing her to become nothingness.
That nothingness allowed her to bypass the pressure being produced by the Black Fire Demon Dragon.
While she couldn’t maintain that form for long, she could keep it activated long enough to get close to the Black Fire Demon Dragon.
So Xuanli turned into a giant sword, and within her were hidden Uncle Drew, Saden, and Lene.
All Nara had to do was get close and attack, which she did.
With the sword making contact with the Black Fire Demon Dragon, Xuanli entered its soul, bringing the others with her.
Now, the battles on the outside and inside the soul would be determined by how long they could hold on.
After all, despite invading its soul, the Black Fire Demon Dragon was able to keep its composure on the outside.
It shook off the three hell demons and even unleashed a breath attack, pushing Vargus back.
But now that it had to defend against soul attacks, the battle on the outside had to be won no matter what.
Nara eyed the crystal on the Black Fire Demon Dragon’s chest and sighed.
That was what they came for, and to get it, they would have to defeat the Black Fire Demon Dragon once.
Since it was an undead dragon, death was basically something they could not guarantee.
But they didn’t need it to stay permanently dead.
They just needed it to die for a few seconds so they could take the Night Heart.
"Vargus, keep it distracted.
I have a plan," Nara, now back in her humanoid form, said before taking a step forward and disappearing from sight.
Vargus sighed and nodded.
Then his body exploded with so much force that the ground beneath his feet split apart.
He also disappeared and reappeared before the Black Fire Demon Dragon before attacking.
His axe carved a deadly arc through the air, landing a huge blow on the dragon’s side.
However, instead of leaving a cut, his axe bounced back, sending vibrations through his arms.
He was besieged the next second, a powerful tail arriving before him like a whip.
Luckily, Thrakos arrived and blocked the blow, sending a powerful shockwave flying in all directions.
Zandros and Kha’zixarath also attacked, but even though they poured all their energy into their attacks, not even a dent appeared on the hard, metallic-like skin of the Black Fire Demon Dragon.
"Just great.
At this rate, we might as well tickle it," Vargus said with a smirk, jumping back to evade a claw attack.
He knew he had to keep it busy, just as Nara had instructed.
Luckily for him, he wouldn’t have to do it alone since he had the three hell demons with him.
But there was someone else who had been missing from the battle.
Eryndor seemed to have vanished from the battlefield.

However, in truth, he had flown much higher and was setting up an attack formation that, if he could complete it fast enough — or at least before Vargus and the others were overwhelmed — would tilt the battle in their favour.
Of course, Nara also seemed to have something planned, but for now, Vargus and the three hell demons would have to hold back the Black Fire Demon Dragon for as long as they could.
Inside its soul, however, things were much different.
The Black Fire Demon Dragon had formed thousands of soul dolls, each imbued with the power of death and darkness.

Uncle Drew and the team inside its soul were now locked in a deadly dance of death and slaughter, the kind that would require one of two things: either they kill faster, which, according to Xuanli, would make its soul vulnerable, allowing them to wound it, or they get overrun and die in there.
So far, they were holding their own.
Uncle Drew had already gone full-on battle mode, cutting down one soul doll after another.
In fact, he was cutting them down so fast that even the Black Fire Demon Dragon seemed to feel threatened by him.
Uncle Drew didn’t want the battle to last long, since he had already sensed danger nearby, so he wasn’t holding back at all.
And he wasn’t the only one.
Lene was like a blur of death, her spear stabbing, slashing, and shattering the soul dolls every second.
Wherever she passed, dozens of soul dolls died.
Saden was equally lethal with her bow.
She had augmented her body and bow with her shadow spirit, so every arrow she fired was several times stronger than it would have been if she hadn’t augmented her bow.
As for Xuanli, since she was versed in soul attacks, she was the one dealing the most damage.
She had unleashed her own soul army, making sure they fought and perished, knowing that regardless of the outcome, they needed only one death.
But achieving that was impossible, especially when the more they killed, the more soul dolls kept coming.
"I really hope the battle on the outside is going well.
Beating an undead soul is virtually impossible," Xuanli said, plucking more strings on her zither.
"Just focus on keeping it distracted here.
I trust them to pull it off," Uncle Drew said, cutting down soul dolls like they were bugs.
Kent remained standing with the lolis, watching the battle with a calm expression.

While only a few days had passed on the outside since the Dark War, months had passed inside the tower, so he had done so much, even fully exploring all the towers with the exception of the Harem Tower.
This meant that, aside from a couple of things he had planned for later, he was free to do whatever he wanted.
He had initially wanted to use the time to spend some relaxing moments with his wives, but they were with his sister, who had become something akin to both their teacher and friend.
They had said that when they were done, they would let him know.
So he left for the Dead World when he learned Uncle Drew and his team had arrived in the Black Star Domain.
Knowing the kind of horror they would be facing, he decided to come and watch, and if they needed help, he would offer it.
So far, he was calmly standing there, watching the battles on both the soul and physical planes.

chapters.title: Chapter 1831: Death Qi Manipulation
paragraphs: Kent, with his Eyes of Chaos active, could see both the battles happening on the outside and inside the Black Fire Demon Dragon’s soul.
Everything lay bare before him, almost as if the astral and physical planes were one.

Of course, it took someone with a much more robust soul to peer into another being’s soul and watch what was happening inside it. But with everything laid bare before his eyes, he could basically tell how the battles were going and who was going to win.
"Big Brother, do you think Big Sisters and Big Brothers will win this battle?" Akira asked, also watching the battle on both planes.
"Unless something happens soon, I am sure they will lose," Kent didn’t sugarcoat his words. He said it exactly as it was, and that made the little ladies beside him frown a bit.
They had clearly come to cheer on their Big Sisters and Big Brothers, so hearing they would lose didn’t sit right with them.
Luckily, before they could despair, something did happen.

Up in the air, Eryndor slammed the blunt end of his staff down, meeting nothing but air. However, despite there not being any solid ground beneath his feet, the staff struck an invisible wall, causing a formation to materialize.
The moment the formation appeared, Kent felt the air around the Black Fire Demon Dragon grow cold. It was as if Eryndor had unleashed an ice-based attack.
However, no ice formed.
Rather, he saw the death qi in the air begin to converge on a single spot.
Naturally, this piqued his interest, and he decided to focus on it further.
It took less than ten seconds for him to clearly see what was happening. ’No way.’
His brow furrowed, and before he could say anything, the moment Eryndor had been waiting for arrived.

Just as the Black Fire Demon Dragon grew more tense and was about to turn its attention to the chilling sensation in the air, a second formation appeared within the first, and from its core, a black beam exploded forward.
It took less than a moment for the beam to reach its chest and explode upon contact. The explosion was violent and chilling.
In fact, the explosion was death itself. The moment it happened, the entire space around the Black Fire Demon Dragon collapsed, revealing the void.
But while such a shocking sight was enough to stun anyone, for the first time since the battle began, the Black Fire Demon Dragon had sustained an injury.
And while it was the first, it was also devastating.
A large wound appeared on its chest despite its colossal body and super-hard skin having blocked every deadly attack that had been launched at it over the past couple of minutes.
"Don’t allow it to heal!" Eryndor’s voice came from the air just before a deadly tail came striking toward him. He conjured a shield, but it shattered upon impact with the tail.
Luckily, Eryndor had already teleported away, having accomplished his goal of injuring the Black Fire Demon Dragon and creating an opportunity for his companions to finally hurt it.

Vargus and the rest didn’t waste any time. All their attacks were aimed at the injured part of its body, resulting in what could be considered their first real chance of success. Well, at least they were trying to kill it while it was trying to stay alive.
They each wanted success, but only one side could remain standing. From Kent’s perspective, the outcome of this battle was rapidly approaching.
Unlike most, who had no idea where Nara had gone, he had known where she was from the very beginning and what she had been doing ever since she vanished.
He knew that Nara’s wraith form could only be used for fifteen minutes every twenty-four hours.
In that form, she had access to a unique attribute called Nothingness. This attribute allowed her to ignore all forms of physical attacks and even fade out of existence.
While faded out of existence, one requires a special type of perception to see her. Kent possessed the Eyes of Chaos, so he could see her even in her wraith-like state of nothingness.
She had used that form to send Xuanli and the others into the Black Fire Demon Dragon’s soul. Now, she was using it again to prepare an attack, just as Eryndor had done.
Initially, Kent had no idea what she had been up to.

But as time slowly passed, he sensed that she had been channeling death qi into her sword. Using her extensive knowledge of Death and swordsmanship, she continuously refined it by merging her sword energy with the death qi.
Slowly, she had been sharpening the death qi itself, something that required extreme focus for anyone whose understanding of both sword qi and death qi isn’t high enough.
Clearly, Nara wasn’t someone to underestimate when it came to energy manipulation.
But she kept her focus on Death Qi Manipulation, and just when she had only two minutes left before her wraith form expired, Eryndor created the opening she needed to make her move.
She waited and watched as Vargus sent the dragon’s head whipping back, and the three hell demons further expanded the wound on its chest.
This series of actions, while not preplanned, worked in her favour.
So she took it, and before the Black Fire Demon Dragon could regain its balance, she appeared once again, and her sword flashed forward.
"Death Severance."
At first, only a thin line of darkness, so cold and sharp, appeared in the air. But the next second, it exploded outward, and a massive sword arc formed from the fusion of Death Qi and sword energy.
"What the..."
Vargus and the hell demons, who were much closer to the dragon, felt their bodies grow tense as the sword arc appeared.
However, the tense atmosphere soon vanished, replaced by the chilling realization that the sword arc Nara had unleashed was meant to sever even death itself.
As such, the dragon, whose undead nature made it nearly unkillable, was now in danger.
It sensed it, and so did they all.
But before any of them could make a sound or the dragon could move to shield against the attack, it had already happened.
SHRIIINNNKKKK!
The sword arc landed on the Black Fire Demon Dragon’s neck, and at once, the void itself was severed. But it wasn’t the only thing that was cut.

The Black Fire Demon Dragon, whose body was as metallic as it was impervious, was cleaved apart, and its gigantic neck, which had seemed impossible to cut, was completely severed from its colossal body.

In what appeared to be a single instantaneous slash, the Black Fire Demon Dragon had lost its head. Its colossal body remained standing for a brief moment before toppling to the side. Meanwhile, its severed head was flung into the air before crashing heavily onto the ground.
Nara regained her corporeal form and appeared before the Night Heart embedded in its chest. She formed a hand seal and pointed at it.

At first, it trembled. Then, as if held back by something, it stopped. However, Nara had no intention of giving up. She formed more hand seals, and by the time she was done, the Night Heart emerged from the Black Fire Demon Dragon’s chest, shrank, and merged into her own.
"Move back, Lady Nara, before it revives!" Thrakos, the Demon of Dread, shouted.
But Nara merely smiled and turned to face him.
"It is dead, Sir Thrakos..."

chapters.title: Chapter 1832: Night Heart
paragraphs: "What do you mean by it is dead?" Zandros asked, narrowing his eyes at Nara, who stood beside the colossal body of the Black Fire Demon Dragon. It now lay headless and lifeless on the ground...
"It is as I said. The Black Fire Demon Dragon is dead."
Just as she said that, a portal opened, and Uncle Drew and the rest, who fought inside the soul of the Black Fire Demon Dragon, walked out, each wearing a stunned expression.

While killing the Black Fire Demon Dragon was a good thing, the plan didn’t include permanent death. In fact, the plan was to kill it temporarily, just long enough for them to get their hands on the Night Heart.
Killing the Black Fire Demon Dragon was never something they thought feasible. In fact, temporarily killing it was out of their hands for a few moments.
However, they made it happen, and the one who accomplished that was Nara, who had yet again returned to her humanoid form.

"I know it is bad to assume this wasn’t something possible, that none of us could handle it, but I would ask anyway... How the hell did you kill this monstrosity, Nightblade?" Uncle Drew asked, walking toward Nara.
The battle inside the soul plane had entered a rather chilling state, besieged on all sides by thousands of soul dolls. It was a breaking point for them.
However, before they could despair, a crack formed inside the soul, and that crack widened until the poor undead soul of the Black Fire Demon Dragon came undone.
That showed the Black Fire Demon Dragon had died, and despite waiting for a few seconds to see it rise back from the ashes, that never happened.

So, Nara killing the unkillable while she was not an undead was just shocking. If Kaizo or any of the undead had done this, no one would ask any questions. After all, they are undead, so killing another undead fits perfectly within their abilities.
Nara smiled, hearing Uncle Drew’s question.

"Let’s just say death isn’t as invincible as one would think," she turned to the Black Fire Demon Dragon’s severed and lifeless body and added, "I merely had to look for the undead vein within it and sever it. The rest, as you all know, is what lies before you now."

"As if it is as simple as you say. The undead vein is visible only to the undead. Kaizo said it is the most hidden part of their existence, mostly hidden within the necromancer," Saden pointed out, a flaw that made everyone wonder if Nara had a special set of eyes that allowed her to see the undead vein.

"Before you weirdos think it, the answer is no, I do not have any special sight that allows me to see undead veins. However, I sensed the location of this Black Fire Demon Dragon since it had the Night Heart embedded in its chest.
Had it not been for that, I wouldn’t have sensed it and severed it, so you can say we won because of the Night Heart."
"She is lying," suddenly, Kent’s voice entered everyone’s ears, causing them to turn in his direction.
Kent smiled back at them, walking with the lolis who were over the moon now that the big bad Black Fire Demon Dragon had been killed by their big sister, Nara.
"KENT!"
"MASTER!"
"RUTHLESS BANDIT!"
All kinds of names were called, depending on how everyone viewed Kent.

Nara, Lene, and Saden called him by his real name. While Lene and Nara had already gotten into his pants, Saden hadn’t. But she spends most of her time with Kent’s wives, so she has developed the habit of calling him by his first name.
Uncle Drew and the rest of the Night Riders called him Master because that was how they all addressed him.
As for the name Ruthless Bandit, the four hell demons who had met him and had firsthand experienced his ruthlessness called him that, visibly becoming a bit apprehensive.
While they got along with most of the Night Riders, the last person none of them seemed to find common ground with was the Ruthless Bandit.
One would say that, for Hell Demons, becoming kindred souls with the Ruthless Bandit, known for his evil ways, was expected. However, not only did they not see eye to eye, but they also feared him.
In their view, they were angels compared to the Ruthless Bandit, who could be considered a real demon. Evil incarnate, as Xuanli used to call him.
Kent, of course, recognized all four of them, so seeing the expressions on their faces, he smiled and said,
"It appears you guys aren’t happy to see me."

"Who in their right mind would be happy to see a man such as yourself? Or are you telling me the universe is so twisted now that even evil is considered normal?" Thrakos said, rooted in one place, ready to attack at a moment’s notice.
To his surprise, however, Kent laughed. "Thrakos, buddy, you always crack me up."
The four Hell Demons didn’t smile, not even for a moment. In their minds, whenever the Ruthless Bandit smiled, what followed always left a bad taste in the mouth.
But today, the opposite happened.
"Relax, you four. I am not the same person you knew. The me you knew was merely a small part of me, so rest assured, I won’t be torturing you guys this time around."
He walked toward Kha’zixarath, who remained in his beast form, and patted his head.
"Unless, of course, you want me to."
They didn’t dare make a sound.
Seeing this, Eryndor smiled, and an idea popped into his head. For now, he would keep it to himself, but the next time he summoned any of his Hell Demons, he would make sure Kent was there.
Nara jumped into Kent’s arms and kissed him. Lene did the same since she had also become one of Kent’s women.
"Why did you say Nara is lying?" Uncle Drew asked after the hugging and kissing were over.
"She didn’t lie about the undead vein part. She indeed sensed it because of the Night Heart. However, she lied about severing it." Kent turned and looked at Nara, who had a blush on her cheeks.
"Your death qi alone was too weak to cut through such thick skin. The only reason you were able to sever its head from its body was that you merged your sword qi with your death qi.
Now, while you succeeded on your first try, you won’t be able to use your sword qi for a couple of days since your crude method drained you completely."
Nara tried to channel her sword qi, but she realized she could no longer harness it. This made her frown slightly as realization dawned on her.
If she had failed to kill the Black Fire Demon Dragon with that one attack, then perhaps she would have found herself and everyone else in grave danger.
But luckily for her, she had managed to end its profane existence with that single attack.
"Relax, it is dead now, so there’s no need to think too much about it. That said, train your sword qi and death qi when you return to the tower."
She nodded, thankful she had succeeded when she did. The focus now was on awakening the Night Heart.

They didn’t dare make a sound.
Seeing this, Eryndor smiled, and an idea popped into his head.
For now, he would keep it to himself, but the next time he summoned any of his Hell Demons, he would make sure Kent was there.
Nara jumped into Kent’s arms and kissed him.
Lene did the same since she had also become one of Kent’s women.
"Why did you say Nara is lying?" Uncle Drew asked after the hugging and kissing were over.
"She didn’t lie about the undead vein part.
She indeed sensed it because of the Night Heart.
However, she lied about severing it." Kent turned and looked at Nara, who had a blush on her cheeks.
"Your death qi alone was too weak to cut through such thick skin.
The only reason you were able to sever its head from its body was that you merged your sword qi with your death qi.
Now, while you succeeded on your first try, you won’t be able to use your sword qi for a couple of days since your crude method drained you completely."
Nara tried to channel her sword qi, but she realized she could no longer harness it.
This made her frown slightly as realization dawned on her.
If she had failed to kill the Black Fire Demon Dragon with that one attack, then perhaps she would have found herself and everyone else in grave danger.
But luckily for her, she had managed to end its profane existence with that single attack.
"Relax, it is dead now, so there’s no need to think too much about it.
That said, train your sword qi and death qi when you return to the tower."
She nodded, thankful she had succeeded when she did.
The focus now was on awakening the Night Heart.

chapters.title: Chapter 1833: Night Riders
paragraphs: With catching up out of the way, the main event came.

Nara would have to awaken the Night Heart and use it to summon the rest of the Night Riders. In total, there were 69 Night Riders, and today, if she managed to awaken the relic that would grant her the power to access the Realm of the Night, she would be able to summon them.
But that wasn’t all.
Once all of them had been summoned, they would venture to the Realm of the Night, which is located on the 14th level of Hell, and receive their complete legacies.
Basically, after this awakening, the once-feared Night Riders would return again.
Kent may have conquered the Dark Fiends and the Dark Empress, and he may also be in the process of conquering the Star Beasts, but that didn’t mean he could relax.
The Void Beasts, Foreign Races, Flame Beasts, Chaos Abyss, Ice Demons, and many more were still out there, so he was going to need his most trusted aides, the Night Riders.
So, Nara’s success today would determine the future.
"Not that we all want to put pressure on you, but success today will go a long way, so don’t fail, Nara," Vargus said, a smile appearing on his face.
His friends cast him dubious looks, but they themselves wanted Nara to succeed because failure was not an option.
She herself knew she could not fail, so hearing Vargus’ words, she took a deep breath and closed her eyes.
Kent stood back, a smile playing on his lips as he watched the Night Riders do their thing.
He couldn’t help but cast his mind back to when he first met them. Back then, the Universe Council had declared an all-out war on him, and one of the teams they sent after him was the Night Riders.

When they met, a great battle ensued, one that tested the Night Riders and pushed them to their limits. However, they all soon realized that while they had come to kill, the Ruthless Bandit was merely toying with them, waiting for the main targets.

It turned out that, recognizing the potential of the Night Riders, the Universe Council felt threatened, so they sent them to fight the Ruthless Bandit, whom they recognized as an even greater threat.
They wished to use him as a weapon to kill the Night Riders, and then, when he was exhausted, they would swoop in and kill him and the rest of the Night Riders.
But they severely underestimated the Ruthless Bandit.
He saved them, and since then, their growth has been explosive.
’Just 69 of them were able to kill a lineup of over 2 million Dark Creatures. If they inherit their legacies again, I am sure they will become even more monstrous.’
The smile on his face brightened even more.
’Though I wonder if the Night Heart would accept her, considering she is no longer a virgin,’ Kent panicked a bit, but he pushed the thought aside and focused on the positive.
’If she awakens and binds with it, then she can command the night. Anyone who isn’t me, Pandora, or the two Grand Shamans would be powerless to stop the night from invading their souls.’
Night Riders are stronger during the night. They mostly ride into battle during the night. Of course, they aren’t weaker during the day, either.
But during the night, they are basically immortals, or for lack of a better word, undead.

During the day, Nara, with the help of the Night Heart, can create the night, so awakening it would help them more than one could imagine. Every day would be a nighttime for them. But first, awakening it was the most important part.
Deep inside an unknown realm, Nara stood face to face with a loli, barely three feet tall. She was adorable, with cute, round cheeks and white hair much longer than her body, flowing down her back.
Gaia and her minions would love her very much.
For a moment, she held a frown on her face.
Then she smiled.
"What took you so long, Big Sister?"

Nara sighed, a smile forming on her face as she reached forward and pulled the adorable young lady into her arms. This adorable little loli was, of course, the Night Heart, or more precisely, the spirit form of the Night Heart.
"I missed you so much, Little Night," Nara said, hugging her.
"I missed you too, Big Sister. I waited so long for you, but you didn’t come..."
"I am here now, Little Night, and this time we will never part again," Nara pulled the adorable little lady much closer, making her smile even more.
"I believe you, Big Sister," she pulled her head back and stared at Nara. "When can we leave? I want to meet the other big brothers and sisters, especially Big Brother Kael. I miss him so much."
Nara smiled and flicked Little Night’s forehead.
"You just reunited with me, and you are already thinking about others. I am heartbroken."
Little Night giggled and cupped Nara’s cheek.
"I am sorry, Big Sister. I will spend more time with you anyway, so after I meet them, we can have so much fun. I have discovered so many places in this realm that I want to show you."
"Fine. In that case, how about we form the bond and, while we’re at it, summon the rest of the Night Riders across the universe to my current location?"
"Okay, Big Sister."

Contrary to what Kent and the other Night Riders were worried about, whether or not Nara would succeed, the sly lady, who wasn’t worried even for a moment, was now drinking tea with Little Night, which was their bonding ceremony.
They would probably be stunned if they witnessed such a sight.
Thankfully, they couldn’t see what was happening, not even Kent. But the effects soon appeared, and every last one of them was stunned.
Suddenly, out of nowhere, Night Gates started opening all around them. The Night Riders became stunned for a moment, then they all started to smile.

From the Night Gates, warriors of various races, shapes, and sizes started to appear, each seated on a hellhorse. Their auras varied in strength, with some being Demigods, Gods, Supremes, and even, from three of the Night Gates, Pseudo-Primordials.
Kent stood to the side, watching them all arrive.
After about ten minutes, they had all appeared, each standing at attention, their focus rooted on Uncle Drew.
For a moment, nobody made a sound.
Suddenly, every last one of them saluted their captain.
Kent knew the Night Riders respected their captain more than anyone, but when he first knew them, Uncle Drew was a Celestial while most of them were Supremes.

Now, however, Uncle Drew was merely an Immortal Lord, while some of them were Celestials and Pseudo-Primordials. But despite this gap, all of them crossed their arms against their chests and bowed their heads toward him.
Kent felt a surge of pride.
He wasn’t the one at the receiving end of such respect, but he felt as though he was.
Uncle Drew smiled and also crossed his arms over his chest. After a few seconds, he lowered them and said jokingly,
"It is good to see you all again, but aren’t you forgetting someone?" His gaze shifted to Kent, who smirked and waved his hand absentmindedly.
"No need for that, guys."
They didn’t listen.

chapters.title: Chapter 1834: Reunion
paragraphs: Kent wasn’t really into this whole salute-and-response thing. He was more focused on results, so being greeted by all the Night Riders wasn’t necessary.
Regardless, he smiled and mimicked their style of greeting by crossing his arms over his chest and bowing slightly. This gesture put smiles on the faces of all the Night Riders present.
They recognised him as their one true master, who had trained them for years using the most gruelling methods known to man.
He basically forged them into weapons worthy of dominating battlefields.
So they appreciated him.
However, their main focus was Uncle Drew, who would decide where they should go next.
Just then, Nara opened her eyes, and a wave of darkness swirled around her for a few seconds.
When it cleared, the adorable Little Night stood beside her, her cute appearance making everyone want to grab her and play with her.
Of course, before they could, she had already jumped into Uncle Drew’s arms.
"Big brother, I miss you soo much."

Uncle Drew was caught off guard, but he managed to catch her before she slid off. Well, considering the mood she was in and how eager she was to finally see her big brother, Little Night held on to Uncle Drew with a firm grip.
Falling off his body wasn’t a possibility at all.
But one thing was weird.
While Little Night seemed eager and happy to have finally reunited with Uncle Drew, the latter had no idea who this little girl was.
In fact, aside from Nara, none of them did.
This was because, when they knew her, she was but a small raven that used to sit on Nara’s shoulder. She wasn’t a white-haired loli who was full of life and happiness.
So, holding her, Uncle Drew tried to accept whatever was happening. However, Little Night soon noticed the confusion and smiled before speaking...
"No need to be confused, big brother, it is me, Little Raven."
This time, Uncle Drew widened his eyes, clearly taken aback by the reveal. "Really..."
"Yes. I miss you soo much, big brother."
Of course, the raven they knew couldn’t talk. But it appeared she was intelligent and had grown fond of them. Basically, this was just one of the best moments of Little Night’s life.
In the past, she wasn’t sentient enough to talk. So she followed and observed, using the knowledge she had accumulated to grow stronger, and now, she was happy to have met her brother again.
"Wow, Little Raven has become much bigger now." Uncle Drew twirled her around in the air, causing Little Night to laugh and giggle, her hair waving behind her.
Kent, who knew Gaia and her minions, was barely holding back the urge to snatch the cute loli from Uncle Drew and initiate her into their fold, smiled and turned to Nara.
"Looks like we were worried over nothing."

She smiled and answered, "It appears so. However, things could have been different if Little Night hadn’t awakened when she did. Now, she is several times stronger than before, meaning we can finally get back our powers and continue to grow, unlocking more of the Night Riders’ powers."
Kent nodded, not particularly bothered.
He had already known that the Night Riders he knew weren’t at their peak, even back when every battlefield trembled under their feet.
They had hidden powers, and today, with the awakening of the Night Heart, they would be able to descend back to the Realm of the Night, located on the 14th level of Hell, and reclaim their legacies.
"I have to ask, though. Did you know something like this would happen?" Kent asked, looking at Little Night, who was now playing with Uncle Drew’s hair.
"I had my suspicions. Back then, during the climax of the Dark War, I sensed she had entered an evolution state. I never got the chance to examine her further, but that feeling remained.
Thankfully, I was right, and she had indeed awakened her spirit before we did."
Kent understood the feeling very well. He himself had experienced it during the final moments of the Flame War when he had to name his hammer and set it free by using his soul as a medium.
That gesture had awakened the true power of his hammer. Kent sensed that awakening went much deeper than what had happened immediately after he died.
He, of course, would have to confirm the extent to which that awakening and evolution had gone. But for now, he understood that the Night Heart wasn’t the old Night Heart he knew.
"Does it mean you can ride into the night again?" Kent asked, and Nara nodded.

"Indeed. My command over the Night has been restored, so regardless of the time of day, if I wanted to, I could command the night. However, I have reason to believe that when I finally reclaim my legacy, my control over the Night will enter a new phase.
Regardless, everything will be determined once we return from the Realm of the Night."
Nara turned to face the rest of her teammates, who, just as they viewed Uncle Drew, viewed her the same way. They all respected the second-in-command of the Night Riders.
In most cases, they called her Nightblade, but when she was acting as the wielder of the Night Heart, they called her Mistress of the Night or Night Maiden.

Her role in the team was vital, so they respected and obeyed her commands just as they did their captain. She might not be as impressive as Uncle Drew, but he had trained her, so they knew she was capable.
"Welcome, everyone. You’ve all been missed," Nara said, addressing her teammates. They smiled, hearing her words.
"You’ve also been missed, Vice Captain," Leo, a Night Rider wielding a saber with blood-red eyes, said, smiling. He stood beside his hellhorse, which also had red eyes.

Unlike most of the Night Riders who commanded green flames, those with unique affinities commanded different shades of the same flame. It came from the same source, but it took on the colour of their affinity.
Leo’s affinity for blood made his flames crimson.

"It is good I have been missed. But inasmuch as I would love for us to go on vacation and relax, you all have to know Night Riders don’t rest, so summoning you over wasn’t to give you a chance to rest.

The universe is at war, and so we are required. Recently, the last of the Dark Creatures were killed by the Chaos Dragon and his legion. But despite that success, there are more dangers out there that we have to address.

So we have to prepare, and to do so, we have to venture into the Realm of the Night and inherit our legacy. I don’t know how long it will take, but all of us here can leave at any moment from now, so we can get things done much faster."
"Yes, let’s go now," Vargus said, eager to become stronger too.
He could sense the aura coming off some of his teammates, especially the three Pseudo-Primordials. As someone who craved strength, he saw it as a challenge and wanted to become stronger much faster.
Even if he wouldn’t become a Pseudo-Primordial, he wanted to be able to stand with the rest of the team and fight like true Night Riders without looking weak.
But he wasn’t the only one who wanted to get going. Almost all of them wanted to go...

"Though I have to ask, won’t all of us leaving deprive Master Ruthless Bandit of the required manpower to handle whatever threat might emerge in our absence?" Mennal, one of the Pseudo-Primordials, asked, looking toward Kent.

"That won’t be necessary," Kent replied. "I have enough manpower to keep things going until you return. But even if I don’t, it isn’t like the universe doesn’t have its own warriors. If anything is to come, the Universe Council will step in, so relax for now and handle what you have to. I will hold down the fort in your absence."
She nodded...

Kent had the legion to indeed keep things going for now. Right now, he wanted to handle the issue at the Cult of Wisdom, then join a sect and participate in the sword competition to help him level up his sword cultivation.
He wasn’t worried about any invasion. If they came, he would find a way to hold them back. He just hoped they wouldn’t be gone for long.
Little Night jumped down from Uncle Drew’s arms and went to hug the rest of the Night Riders. After she was done, she approached Kent with measured steps.
Immediately, he knew she was afraid of him.
Honestly, he sensed that feeling from most of the Night Riders. His nature, as they knew it, was too evil, so it was a natural reaction on their part.
He was the Ruthless Bandit, after all.
Thankfully, before Little Night could despair, Gaia and her friends surrounded her and started playing with her hair and cute little clothes.
Kent smiled and cursed himself. ’I should redeem my image in her eyes since I seem to have traumatized her.’

chapters.title: Chapter 1841: Chaos Ascension King Legacy (1)
paragraphs: Among the many things Kent had to do, one of the most important was to find out what kind of life he had lived before the 13 incarnations he was currently recalling.

He had met Paragon, who seemed to have pointed out a time in the past, or perhaps yet to come, when he sought out seven individuals with overwhelming power and strength to aid him in something extremely vital.
Kent was part of that team, and while he would have loved to hear something good, it turned out they had failed to accomplish what they had set out to do.
That was what Kent wanted to know.
He wanted to know the kind of life he had lived that would compel a monster like Paragon to consider him one of the seven individuals in all of existence qualified to fight by his side.
At the end of the day, Kent knew that when it came to Paragon, nothing made sense, so he was determined to know more.
Of course, the Blood Empress had also shed some light on that life, and so being the only one who didn’t know made him a bit sad.
That changes today.
While he only had one page out of hundreds, he was content to know what was within those pages.
Kent sat down on a stone-like platform, immediately feeling his mind clear and his soul surge with power. Inside the Soul Tower, after the tower’s upgrade and awakening, a lot had changed.

One of those changes was the appearance of the Dao Enlightenment Stone. Just by sitting on it to cultivate, his comprehension of the Dao would become 300 times deeper, regardless of how deep or complex it was.
So he sat on it, knowing that what he was about to read contained so many secrets that he would either benefit from them or not.
But before all that, he summoned his loyal aide...
"Tower, my love, come over."
A loli clad in a three-piece white suit appeared from thin air, her wavy silver hair sweeping the ground behind her, a smile on her cute little face.
Kent furrowed his brow, seeing Tower appear as a loli.
She had big, round, silver eyes, cute little cherry lips, and round, adorable cheeks.
The Tower he knew, or had seen inside the Chaos Ascension King Trial Chamber, was much taller, more mature, and equally beautiful.
However, it appeared that while her beauty was now even more radiant, Tower had decided to become a loli just so she could blend in with Gaia and her minions.
She was just as cute and adorable as they were, which, from what Kent knew, made her one of them.
’Now, I do wonder, but which of my incarnations aided lolis in the past, resulting in so many finding their way to me?’ Kent asked inwardly, a smile forming on his face.

He hadn’t considered it yet, but out of the incarnations he had yet to recall, perhaps one of them had formed a Loli Legion. He doubted it, but he was also eager to find out why he seemed connected to lolis like that.
He already had over ten of them. Now, Tower had also joined them, and from the smile on her face, Kent knew she was happy.
"I won’t ask, so don’t tell me," Kent said with a smirk, causing Tower to giggle and jump into his arms, showering his face with kisses.
"Big Brother... can I call you Big Brother?" she asked, a bit hesitant to take Gaia’s advice.
She had already met them, and Gaia and her minions had told her that if she wanted to feel like family, she had to call Kent Big Brother.
That way, she could make demands, and as a big brother, Kent wouldn’t dare turn her down.

Come to think of it, all this started because of Li Hua. That little loli, who became Kent’s very first ward after he agreed to become her guardian, had polluted Gaia’s mind, leading Gaia to also pollute the rest of her sisters.
Now, whenever a new loli came along, they made sure she was comfortable before teaching her their ways. Li Hua would be proud of her achievements and insatiable love for money and shiny things.
Kent smiled and nodded. "You can call me Big Brother whenever you want. I don’t mind."
Tower nodded and then asked, "Are you planning to read the first page of the Chaos Ascension King Legacy Manual, Big Brother?"
"Yes. But before that, I want to know, are there any downsides to reading it?"
"Yes, but that all depends on how deep your comprehension abilities go." Tower turned sideways and looked at Kent.

"You see, every word inside that book is written using the language of the Dao. The beginning is simple, but as you progress further, the complexity will increase to the point that even Eternals would find it hard to look at a single word in the book.

Basically, this manual is the legacy, and as you read, so will you inherit it. The question then is, are you ready to pierce into the Dao and uncover its secrets? Because trust me, after reading this first page, the way you perceive things will start to change.
You will start to change, finally coming to terms with your 13 reincarnations and why you had to walk that path to begin with."
Kent sighed, a smile forming on his face. "So it all boils down to how fast I can comprehend my own Dao and inherit my legacy."

"Yes, Big Brother. But rest assured, you are much stronger and more intelligent than to face any challenges within the first couple of pages. That said, be ready for anything, since even I don’t know what is contained inside it."
Kent nodded and thanked Tower. "Thanks for the explanation, Tower. I will be sure to absorb everything, and hopefully, when it is over, I will have some answers to my endless ocean of questions."
"Good luck, Big Brother. If you need me, just call me. I will be here in no time."
Kent nodded and readjusted his posture. "I will, so don’t get too absorbed in your loli life."
Tower pulled on Kent’s slightly longer ear and ran off, vanishing from sight.
Kent smirked and flipped open the book, his mind instantly getting pulled inside.

chapters.title: Chapter 1842: Chaos Ascension King Legacy (2)
paragraphs: "If you are reading this, then it means I am dead... Well, I cannot die even if I want to, so I am probably living a new life, finally embracing my nature as the Primordial Chaos Dragon.
Isn’t it funny to live a full life, rise above all, yet fail to live a genuine life?
It is very funny indeed, and I paid dearly for it, a mistake I had planned not to repeat in these new lives you have probably already become aware of.

You know, Paragon used to say something along the lines of, ’Life is precious but also fragile. Those who have little lust for more, and those who have more don’t know what to do with it. I want my life to be full of blissful moments, regret-free, as well as difficult and full of adventures.’

The first time I heard him say this, I nearly smacked him silly, but now that I cast my mind back to the kind of life I had lived, I must say, he was right. I had lived a life of regret, so much so that I never knew happiness until my sworn brothers came into my life."
Kent’s eyelids twitched, a sense of recognition appearing in his eyes as he dived back into the second quarter of the read.
It appeared that although he only has access to one page, it has four paragraphs, each translated into dozens of sentences, allowing him to capture more context...
He proceeded to read the second paragraph...

"I wasn’t born of a man and a woman. Just a woman who was unfortunate enough to be the maid of a monster who called himself a man. My mother loved me so much that her love for me ended her already miserable life just as she was beginning to discover joy and comfort.

She named me Avalon because she thought my coming into the world was magic. I loved my name, and I was indeed a magici because, long before I was supposed to awaken, I had already awakened, and I was determined to make a life worth living for myself.
But how could the life of a slave maid and her bastard son be allowed to change? In their own words, they claimed it would be a disgrace to the family she was a slave of.
So they killed her and shackled me, making me a slave whose freedom was tied to his master. I never even got to mourn my mother, taking away everything I cherished and would remember her by.
But I was the Chaos Dragon... It is impossible to enslave the Chaos Dragon. So I did what a Chaos Dragon does best. I killed them all, both old and young, painting an entire city red.
They called it the Blood River Massacre, an event that would forever echo across the Universe Ocean, sending a warning down the spines of all who dared come close to the Primordial Chaos Dragon."

Kent felt chills run down his spine, and somewhere inside the Soul Tower, his wives and his big sister, Fiannarel, also trembled, feeling a wave of killing intent mixed with an incredibly chilling blood intent, one that caused goosebumps to appear even on Fiannarel’s skin.
"Ladies, I think we should leave, like now."
Thanks to her timely intervention, they managed to leave before the second wave of killing intent spread out, becoming even more insidious and bone-chilling.

Kent narrowed his eyes, feeling an overwhelming surge of anger, so much so that his heartbeat started to rise. He clenched his fist, and by the time the third wave of killing intent came out, his nails had dug into his palm, causing blood to run along and between his fingers.
Suddenly, the space around him started to freeze.
But while one might say it was his ice element acting out, the truth was that the aura emanating from his body was killing intent mixed with Blood, Death, and Evil Intent.

Many go their entire lives mastering only one or two of these four intents. However, by just reading a few passages, Kent seemed to have gained a much deeper understanding of all four. He even appeared to be using them alone to influence the laws around him.
The Soul Tower was soon frozen.
If his wives were around, all of them would have already passed out, their minds sent into a realm of evil, killing, death, and blood.
Luckily, they had long since left, thanks to Fiannarel’s quick thinking and decisive action.
But Kent didn’t stop at the second paragraph; he went further to the third...
"Regret. Did I regret killing the family that was supposed to be my family?" A smirk formed at the corner of Kent’s lips.
"...Never. I never regretted ending their lives. In fact, if I get the chance again, I will kill them using the most painful methods known and unknown to man.
Hatred is a dangerous weapon, and I have accumulated a lot of it. However, do I regret not being able to do anything for my mother before she took her last breath..."
The look on Kent’s face softened...

"I do regret that. She was my everything, and I watched her bleed out right before me. I failed her as a son and as the Primordial Chaos Dragon. I was a failure who only knew how to take revenge but not how to protect.

Mother once told me the essence of life is to protect and live happily. Too bad I cannot live that happy life, but I can protect it. I will protect and try to honor her last wish. I am the Primordial Chaos Dragon, but to live the kind of life my mother wanted me to, I will have to put away Chaos and embrace a new persona.
I will be called the Chaos Ascension King, someone whose mission is to protect all life in the Universe Ocean, and thus begin the life you are about to read...

My journey from start to finish will reflect how I approached cultivation, pain, and regret. I will explore everything I did, from the very beginning to the day I, alongside seven others, met someone far more dreadful than all eight of us combined...
I will explain how I had to die through 13 reincarnation cycles just so I could become who I was meant to be—the Primordial Chaos Dragon..."

chapters.title: Chapter 1843: Chaos Ascension King Legacy (3)
paragraphs: Before Existence came into being, there were no planets, galaxies, or universes. There was only the Primordial Chaos, or as many call it, the Universe Ocean/Primal Chaos.
Within the Primordial Chaos, there are no cities, only domains. I came from the Ash Domain, ruled by the Five Calamity Ash Tyrant, one of the Primals whose authority cannot be denied.

I was supposed to be the Chaos Dragon, an existence born from Chaos and destined to rule Chaos by birthright. However, I changed myself simply because I wasn’t pleased with who I was. I became the Chaos Ascension King.
But by becoming someone I wasn’t meant to be, I became someone who could live a life with unknown outcomes. I lusted for that life, and so I lived it.
I grew up knowing one thing—battles.
I fought my fair share and ran from a few. I even met death a few times, but who can say death is certain when you are destined to walk through Chaos and back?
I discarded that part of me, but that part never left me. My destiny soon found me, and that was the day I met him...

He calls himself the Lone Wanderer, someone without a home or domain. Before we met, I heard so many overly exaggerated stories about him. The funny yet chilling part was that every last story about him wasn’t exaggerated enough.
In fact, the real him and the stories were in stark contrast. He was a menace, one of the most dangerous souls I have ever met in this life and the next.
He opened my eyes to the truth.
A truth that, to this very day, remains elusive to all.
Existence as we know it is threatened by someone... a single individual... his name...
Kent snapped his eyes shut, blood oozing from his nose, ears, mouth, and even his closed eyes. He tried to scream, but all that came out was a hoarse sound.
For a moment, his complexion turned pale white. Then, in what could be considered the most dramatic turn of events, he fell backward and collapsed, all life draining from him.
Tower appeared instantly, and with a wave of her hand, Kent’s body was transported into a jade-like pod somewhere inside the Soul Tower.
The pod shut, and an unknown healing liquid appeared inside.
Lady Kenzie appeared beside Tower, and with a wave of her wand, the space around the pod was filled with plants and flowers, the air instantly turning into healing qi.
Everything happened in less than 2 seconds.
"He will be fine, my lady. He just needs time to heal," Tower said to Lady Kenzie. Had it not been for her presence inside Kent’s soul, he would have found himself in grave danger by now.
"What happened to him?" Lady Kenzie asked, clearly worried.

As someone connected to Kent’s life, she could tell he had narrowly escaped annihilation this time. Whatever he saw was clearly something he wasn’t supposed to see or even dare to read at this stage of his life.
He was not at the point in his life where he should be reading or seeing names of such caliber.
"I don’t know what Master saw, but clearly, he shouldn’t have tried to read it," Tower sighed. Then, with a wave of her hand, the Chaos Ascension King Legacy Manual flew into her hands.
She opened the first page, but aside from a few runes that only Kent would understand, the text he had read was gone. The blank page was all that was left for her to stare at.

Seeing that whatever had caused Kent’s sudden collapse couldn’t be accessed, she put away the manual and turned to Lady Kenzie. "I know that no matter what I say, you won’t listen, so take care of the Master. I am sure it won’t be long before he wakes up."
Lady Kenzie nodded, and soon Tower was gone.
Lady Kenzie moved closer and placed her hands on the healing pod, pouring more Life Qi into Kent’s body. She couldn’t take any chances, especially when it came to her one true master.
"You do know he is going to be fine, right?" Suddenly, Hades appeared inside the room, wearing a sleepy look. He yawned and leaned against the wall, crossing his arms over his chest.
Lady Kenzie turned and looked at him for a few seconds before turning away.
"What are you doing here, Death?"
Hades is Death Incarnate, or as Kent calls him, his Death Spirit. He named him Hades to humanize him, just as Lady Kenzie also has a name.

"What? Can’t I also come out to see how the Master is doing? Or are you telling me you’re the only one allowed to check on the Master’s well-being?" he scoffed and walked toward the pod, taking a much closer look.

"In case you are not aware, Master’s life is yours to handle, while his death is mine. Before he dies, I would have to die first, so maybe be grateful to me for making sure he didn’t die when he clearly should have."
Lady Kenzie flashed Hades a look that made the bastard grin and step back.
"That is just like you. The last I checked, you were ready to rebel. What changed?"

"What you called rebellion was merely me being loyal to the Chaos Ascension King, you know, our original master, Lord Avalon. Unlike you, who accepted becoming Lord Kent’s subordinate without a second thought, I remained loyal to Lord Avalon, and so I pushed back.
"Of course, now that we have gotten ourselves an upgrade, I dare not rebel unless, of course, I wish to perish. And that is deep for me to say, considering I am Death itself."

sentences.text: Before Existence came into being, there were no planets, galaxies, or universes.
There was only the Primordial Chaos, or as many call it, the Universe Ocean/Primal Chaos.
Within the Primordial Chaos, there are no cities, only domains.
I came from the Ash Domain, ruled by the Five Calamity Ash Tyrant, one of the Primals whose authority cannot be denied.
I was supposed to be the Chaos Dragon, an existence born from Chaos and destined to rule Chaos by birthright.
However, I changed myself simply because I wasn’t pleased with who I was.
I became the Chaos Ascension King.
But by becoming someone I wasn’t meant to be, I became someone who could live a life with unknown outcomes.
I lusted for that life, and so I lived it.
I grew up knowing one thing—battles.
I fought my fair share and ran from a few.
I even met death a few times, but who can say death is certain when you are destined to walk through Chaos and back?
I discarded that part of me, but that part never left me.
My destiny soon found me, and that was the day I met him...
He calls himself the Lone Wanderer, someone without a home or domain.
Before we met, I heard so many overly exaggerated stories about him.
The funny yet chilling part was that every last story about him wasn’t exaggerated enough.
In fact, the real him and the stories were in stark contrast.
He was a menace, one of the most dangerous souls I have ever met in this life and the next.
He opened my eyes to the truth.
A truth that, to this very day, remains elusive to all.
Existence as we know it is threatened by someone... a single individual... his name...
Kent snapped his eyes shut, blood oozing from his nose, ears, mouth, and even his closed eyes.
He tried to scream, but all that came out was a hoarse sound.
For a moment, his complexion turned pale white.
Then, in what could be considered the most dramatic turn of events, he fell backward and collapsed, all life draining from him.
Tower appeared instantly, and with a wave of her hand, Kent’s body was transported into a jade-like pod somewhere inside the Soul Tower.
The pod shut, and an unknown healing liquid appeared inside.
Lady Kenzie appeared beside Tower, and with a wave of her wand, the space around the pod was filled with plants and flowers, the air instantly turning into healing qi.
Everything happened in less than 2 seconds.
"He will be fine, my lady.
He just needs time to heal," Tower said to Lady Kenzie.
Had it not been for her presence inside Kent’s soul, he would have found himself in grave danger by now.
"What happened to him?" Lady Kenzie asked, clearly worried.
As someone connected to Kent’s life, she could tell he had narrowly escaped annihilation this time.
Whatever he saw was clearly something he wasn’t supposed to see or even dare to read at this stage of his life.
He was not at the point in his life where he should be reading or seeing names of such caliber.
"I don’t know what Master saw, but clearly, he shouldn’t have tried to read it," Tower sighed.
Then, with a wave of her hand, the Chaos Ascension King Legacy Manual flew into her hands.
She opened the first page, but aside from a few runes that only Kent would understand, the text he had read was gone.
The blank page was all that was left for her to stare at.
Seeing that whatever had caused Kent’s sudden collapse couldn’t be accessed, she put away the manual and turned to Lady Kenzie.
"I know that no matter what I say, you won’t listen, so take care of the Master.
I am sure it won’t be long before he wakes up."
Lady Kenzie nodded, and soon Tower was gone.
Lady Kenzie moved closer and placed her hands on the healing pod, pouring more Life Qi into Kent’s body.
She couldn’t take any chances, especially when it came to her one true master.
"You do know he is going to be fine, right?" Suddenly, Hades appeared inside the room, wearing a sleepy look.
He yawned and leaned against the wall, crossing his arms over his chest.
Lady Kenzie turned and looked at him for a few seconds before turning away.
"What are you doing here, Death?"
Hades is Death Incarnate, or as Kent calls him, his Death Spirit.
He named him Hades to humanize him, just as Lady Kenzie also has a name.
"What?
Can’t I also come out to see how the Master is doing?
Or are you telling me you’re the only one allowed to check on the Master’s well-being?" he scoffed and walked toward the pod, taking a much closer look.
"In case you are not aware, Master’s life is yours to handle, while his death is mine.
Before he dies, I would have to die first, so maybe be grateful to me for making sure he didn’t die when he clearly should have."
Lady Kenzie flashed Hades a look that made the bastard grin and step back.
"That is just like you.
The last I checked, you were ready to rebel.
What changed?"

Master has returned, and from the look of things, staying by his side will benefit me more than going solo.
And who said I wanted to rebel?" A smile formed at the corner of his lips.

And that is deep for me to say, considering I am Death itself."

’Bastard...’ she cursed inwardly and focused on making sure Kent was alright.

chapters.title: Chapter 1844: Undead Realm Mission (2)
paragraphs: [Somewhere in the High Undead Heaven - Kaizo and Selantra’s POV]
"Have you heard?" a man wearing a straw hat said, turning to a friend — or perhaps a fellow passenger — seated inside one of the Undead Trains — transport vehicles made from undead leviathans.
Anyone inside the Undead Train might as well be strangers meeting for the very first time.

However, judging by the way he turned to the fellow beside him, it appeared they knew each other. Or perhaps the man in the straw hat was simply an extrovert who found it easy to strike up conversations with just about anyone.
"Lord Lamine had recently awakened his Undead Star and summoned one of the Ancients. I learned the Undead Monarch even commended him and bestowed upon him the title of Undead Baron."
What he had to say, however, captured everyone’s attention.
They all turned to face him, asking for more context. Seeing that he had the floor, he smiled slightly and began to speak.

"Lord Lamine, as we all know, was one of the few who ever made it back from the Primordial Chaos. Of course, many say he was able to do so because of his ever-trustworthy Oracle, the Green Bone Oracle.

"However, regardless of what people think, I believe we all know that returning from the Primordial Chaos is next to impossible. He accomplished it, and now he has summoned an Ancient, making him one of the more powerful Undead Barons.
"I learned he will be unveiling the Ancient he summoned five months from today at a grand wine-and-dine event. Many Undead Barons will be in attendance, including even the Third Undead Princess."

"The Third Undead Princess? Isn’t she the only person to have summoned a Chaos-type Ancient several million years ago?" someone else inside the Undead Train asked, looking at the man in the straw hat.

"That’s indeed her. From what many have tried to hide—and please remember this is only a rumor—the Third Undead Princess apparently had a history with that menace who once terrorized the Undead Realm."
Many turned and looked at each other, almost as if hesitant to say the person’s name. Eventually, someone spoke.
"You mean that terrifying individual who was once known as the Bone Lich Undead Emperor?"
The man who spoke was handsome, with golden hair and golden eyes. He seemed normal, almost native, yet if one looked closer, he appeared foreign.
His words made everyone inside the Undead Train nod in silence.

There is a legend that, many years ago, a single Necromancer, together with his sixty-six Undead Generals, each commanding no fewer than a hundred warriors, invaded the Undead Realm and came dangerously close to annihilating the Undead Monarch and his legacy.
Of course, before that, he was someone many respected, for he had contributed immensely to the betterment of the Undead Realm.
Nobody truly knew what had happened between him and the Undead Monarch, considering they had once been akin to best friends.
But before he vanished, the two of them fought a great battle.

"Wasn’t he the only person to have sixty-six Ancients under his command back then? I wonder where he is now, considering nobody knows his whereabouts or has seen him in the last billions of years... I think."
Sighs filled the Undead Train.
"Maybe it is a good thing he isn’t here. Perhaps his return would be the apocalypse we have been waiting for all these years." A small wave of laughter spread throughout the Undead Train.
The golden-haired man also smiled and asked, "If you don’t mind me asking, how can one qualify to attend this wine-and-dine event?"
The man in the straw hat smiled and shook his head.

"Little buddy, as much as I would love to be there myself, to qualify, you either have to be invited personally or rank among the top three Undead Mercenary teams in all of Rex City. Otherwise, just focus on hearing what transpired during the event from those privileged enough to attend such a glorious gathering."
The golden-haired man smiled and nodded to the straw-hat man’s words.
Then he asked again, "I know you will laugh, but how does one go about ranking among the top three Undead Mercenary teams in the city? And most importantly, how can I become a mercenary?"

The straw-hat man turned to the golden-haired man and said, "Persistent, I see. Maybe that is a good thing since the Undead Realm itself forces people to be persistent. As for becoming a mercenary, you can choose to join an existing team, provided you are a Demigod or above.
"Second, if you want to form your own team, then you must visit the Undead Guild with a minimum of five other people and register it. Of course, that part is simple.

"As for ranking higher, here is how you do it. There are five levels of missions, each more dangerous and deadly than the last. The first are White Missions, which aren’t much of a concern. Then come Blue Missions, which, as you know, are a bit more challenging.

"Green Missions are considerably more dangerous, while Black Missions are on an entirely different level. But the most dreadful are Red Missions, and they mostly take place within the Seven Undead Graves.

"Completing a single Red Mission would, without a doubt, rank you among the top five. Of course, completing two Black Missions would also get you there. The reason is that, in the High Undead Heavens, not many mercenary teams have managed to complete Black or Red Missions.

"Those missions are meant for the Supreme and Celestial Undead Heavens. But all the same, if you want to rank higher, complete one Red Mission or two Black Missions. That said, I would advise you against it since they are extremely dangerous.
"Regardless, good luck, little man."
The golden-haired man smiled and nodded. "Thanks for the information, Senior."
Kaizo turned and looked at Selantra, who was seated beside him, resting her head on his shoulder without a care in the world.
’You heard the man, right? We have to get close to the Green Bone Oracle, and as it appears, she will be at the wine-and-dine event. So we have to get inside, no matter what...’
’I know, Kaizo. No need to disturb my sleep.’
Kaizo smirked.
’Then there’s no need to use my shoulder as your pillow.’
