chapters.title: Chapter 1845: Undead Realm Mission (3)
paragraphs: [Rex City - High Undead Heaven]
The undead train touched down in Rex City, one of the 13 High Undead Heavens.

It is home to a variety of undead, most of whom have pale white skin. Unlike many in the Infinity Universe, who view the undead as skeletons, they are actually humanoid, with only a few skeletons among them.
Kaizo and Selantra quickly entered the city, walking side by side.

When they arrived in the Undead Realm, they had to split up. Kaizo traveled with Selantra; Zareth traveled with Velmora; Sylara traveled with Morne; Elyndra traveled with Velithra; Vaelros teamed up with Seraphyne; and Varyn traveled with Varkhiel.
Twelve Demigods moving together through the Low and Middle Undead Heavens would raise too much alarm, so Kaizo had them move in pairs.
They had been on the move for months already. Finally, they arrived in Rex City, making it to the High Undead Heaven, where their mission would officially begin.
Their mission, of course, came in two phases. First, they had to retrieve the bones of some of the undead that the Bone Lich Undead Emperor had created back during the Undead Era.
Kent needed them to revive his once dreadful Undead Generals.
So he sent them there to get the job done. Once they were finished with that, their second mission was to retrieve some treasures he had stashed away for his future self.
Of course, to do all this, they first had to meet one of Kent’s friends, whom he had tasked with protecting something very precious to him.
Kaizo and Selantra managed to locate her, and upon arriving in Rex City, they quickly made their way deeper into the city.

A couple of minutes later, they arrived in front of an undead restaurant called Undying Cuisine. It is one of the top restaurants in the Undead Realm. They serve continental dishes with an extensive menu.
They have the Underworld Menu, Hell Menu, Abyssal Menu, and so on.
Kaizo and Selantra walked in, and the moment they set foot inside, a lady approached them with a polite smile.
"Welcome to Undying Cuisine. Do you have a reservation, or are you yet to get one?"
Selantra answered, "We already have a reservation under the name Blood Scarlet."
The lady walked to a table where a runic formation was visible. She examined it for a few seconds, then returned wearing the same polite smile.
"Kindly follow me."

They followed her across the restaurant hall, which, from what they saw, was much bigger inside than it looked from the outside. The formation used had woven a pocket-dimensional rune into it, giving it a much larger interior.
They soon approached a private room.

The waiter knocked, and a lady spoke from inside. She then opened the door for Kaizo and Selantra to enter. Walking inside, their gazes landed on Sylara and Morne, who were comfortably seated, sipping on Hell Wine.
"Took you guys long enough," Morne said, flashing a cute smile.
Kaizo and Selantra just smirked and sat down.

Seven days ago, Morne and Sylara reached out to them to inform them they had arrived in the High Undead Heaven. Kaizo then sent them to Rex City since he had information that the person they were looking for lived there.
He also reached out to the others, who were still on their way.
Naturally, being the first to arrive had become a competition between them over the past few months. While there was no reward, everyone wanted to be the first to arrive.
It appeared Sylara and Morne had managed to give everyone a full one-week head start.
"How did you two get here that fast?" Selantra asked, pouring herself a glass of Hell Wine.
Morne smiled and turned to Sylara, who knew what was coming, so she smirked and took a sip of her drink.

"Apparently, if you’re a beautiful redhead with cute red eyes in the Undead Realm, Barons kind of become obsessed with you," Morne laughed and added, "Sylara found herself a sugar daddy who took us from the Middle Undead Heavens to here in his private undead train."
"Oh, that is a bit unexpected, but do tell, how did it happen?" Selantra, who was up for some good gossip, shifted her chair closer to Morne, and they started talking, giggling every now and then.
Kaizo ignored them and turned to Sylara. "Do you think we have missed something big back home?"
Sylara looked up at Kaizo and smiled. Then she asked in a sarcastic tone, "Why? Do you want us to go back already?"
"No. It’s just that I can’t shake off this feeling that while we were gone, something big happened, and we missed it."

"As long as the Master is alive, something big will always happen. So if you are eager to be a part of the next one, then make sure we complete this mission as soon as possible. But yes, I also feel like we have missed something big."
Kaizo sighed.
He hadn’t been in many battles since they left the Infinity Universe, so he was a bit hungry for a good, chaotic battle where he could release some stress.
Thinking about the battles he had missed, he sighed again and changed the topic. "It appears the Third Princess will also be attending the Wine and Dine event in five months."
"Oh, that is something." Sylara set her wine glass down. "Do you think she will remember us?"

"That depends. She was rather close with the Master back in the day, so perhaps she would remember us. But I doubt she will be thrilled to see us, though. The last time we met, things didn’t end well,"
Kaizo sighed again, clearly thinking about how to approach the Third Undead Princess, who had been close to Kent’s past incarnation as the Bone Lich Undead Emperor.

"That is true. But from what I observed, she isn’t as crazy as the other princesses, so let’s keep a low profile when we manage to make it to the event. For now, we should focus on how to get inside."
Kaizo nodded. "Once the others arrive, we will register our mercenary team and take on Black Missions. We don’t have much time, so we’d better go all out..."

chapters.title: Chapter 1846: Undead Realm Mission (4)
paragraphs: [Four Months Later - Undead Mercenary Guild]
On a normal day, the number of people gathered inside and outside the Undead Mercenary Guild wouldn’t exceed 300.
It is true that one of the go-to places in any Undead Heaven is the Undead Mercenary Guild. But it doesn’t usually attract as many people as it did today.
Of course, the reason for that had to do with what had happened, or rather, what had been happening over the past four months.
Four months ago, an undead mercenary team registered itself under the name Chaos Dragon Undead Mercenary Team. The team consisted of twelve able undead warriors led by the Golden-Haired Divine Titan.
None of them used their real names, mainly for anonymity. However, Kaizo’s unique golden hair had made him a sensation throughout Rex City and the other twelve High Undead Heavens.
His fame only continued to grow as the days passed.
At first, when they registered, nobody really had high hopes for them. High Undead Heavens have a cultivation cap at the Universal God stage.
While Supremes and Celestials can leave and use their powers freely, the hierarchy had been structured in such a way that Gods were the strongest beings in this part of the Undead Realm.
Forming a team without a single God joining it simply wasn’t the kind of team many people would pay attention to.

"I don’t know if that’s jealousy talking or if you’re just an envious undead, but haven’t you heard? Before this Red Mission, they had already completed five Black Missions. Even an idiot can tell they truly have the means to handle such a mission."
"But it’s a Red Mission, and it took place in one of the most dreadful locations too..."
"That is true, but they aren’t the first to survive the Undead Weeping Smoke Sea. Many have survived that place, including Undead Baron Lamine."

"Dude, Lord Lamine had an Ancient accompanying him, and he still didn’t go after the Undead Kraken. They did, so don’t tell me any of this is normal. If anything, they should be investigated. Maybe they cheated."
"Cheated? Do you even hear yourself?"
Just before the discussions grew even more heated, an undead train landed, and twelve people stepped out, instantly capturing everyone’s attention.
Kaizo, with his golden hair and imposing physique, walked at the front, his steps heavy and resolute. Sylara walked behind him, with the rest following closely.
As they approached the Undead Mercenary Guild, the staff members all walked outside, and when the group drew closer, they bowed respectfully to the team that had accomplished the Red Mission.
Kaizo and his team paused.
They scanned the area, taking in the countless reactions around them. A faint smile appeared on the corner of Kaizo’s lips. He rose into the air and spoke.
"Let it be known that the Chaos Dragon Undead Mercenary Team has slain the Undead Kraken and completed the Red Mission in two months."
He waved his hand, and the colossal head of the dreadful beast that had claimed hundreds of thousands of undead lives flew into the air and remained suspended above everyone.
GASPS

All kinds of reactions spread through the crowd, with most people instinctively stepping back in sheer terror. Even in death, the Undead Kraken’s head radiated an overwhelming aura that struck fear into their hearts.
But as their fear gradually subsided, they all came to the same realization.
The Red Mission that countless mercenary teams had accepted over the years, only to fail, had truly been completed by the Chaos Dragon Undead Mercenary Team.

chapters.title: Chapter 1847: Undead Realm Mission (5)
paragraphs: [Meeting the Green Bone Oracle]

Kaizo’s declaration and the reveal of the head of the Undead Kraken had finally convinced everyone, causing all who doubted the fact that a team of 12 demigods could kill such a monstrosity to take deep sighs.
They had clearly underestimated the Chaos Dragon Undead Mercenary Team.
Some had expected that when Kaizo and his team arrived, the truth about them having lost some of their members while completing a red mission would be revealed.
They expected some of them not to return alive.
But not only were Kaizo and his team looking clean and radiant as ever, but they also seemed rather chill for people who had faced such a monstrosity.

Then again, the battle lasted only 5 hours, since long before they faced it, Kaizo and his team had gathered information about it and, drawing on their extensive battle experience, developed several plans to kill it.
They knew where to hit and how hard to hit it in order to kill it.

So going into the battle was already a win for them. Right now, the proof had been shown, and as Kaizo and his team moved into the Undead Mercenary Guild headquarters, the people outside fell into a frenzy.
"This is just so unbelievable, yet somehow, it makes sense that they were able to win," someone said, watching Kaizo and his team walk into the building.

"It makes sense because, looking at their track record over the past 4 months, they have proven to be one of the best Undead Mercenary Teams in the High Undead Heaven. Though I have to ask, where did they come from? I have never heard of them until 4 months ago when they started making waves."
"Same here. If they had lived in Rex City for long, I would have known or at least heard about them."
"Maybe they came from the Supreme or Celestial Undead Heavens, seeing as they were able to kill such a monster despite being demigods."
"It appears so. Though I wonder which Baron they serve."
As more and more people speculated about things, the ranking that displayed the various Undead Mercenary Teams was updated, and the Chaos Dragon Undead Mercenary Team shot to the first rank.
They would remain in that rank for the next thousands of years unless, of course, some other team managed to complete a red mission.
Kaizo and his team had left their mark, and that would go down in history for generations to come.
A few minutes after they entered the building, they walked out and made their way to their Undead Train. However, just before they could enter, a neigh came from one side.

They stopped and turned toward the arrival of two stags pulling a carriage made from the bones of a dead beast. Come to think of it, almost all transport systems in the Undead Realm were made from the remains of dead beasts.
The Undead Trains were made from the remains of Undead Leviathans.
It appeared nothing went to waste in the Undead Realm.
The carriage landed, and people gathered before scrambling away, almost as if the plague had arrived. Kaizo and his team focused on the carriage door, and a few seconds later, it swung open...
From within, a slender leg emerged, followed by the majestic figure of a woman whose beauty instantly captured everyone’s attention.

She had an hourglass figure that accentuated her hips and ass, allowing the barely fitting green gown she wore to cling tightly to her frame. It would have done her more good to walk naked since she was showing more skin than she covered.
Her boobs, which would make even Pandora or Mara turn their heads, gleamed like polished tofu on her chest, causing everyone around to swallow their saliva.
Her long green hair cascaded down her back, reaching her voluptuous ass, while her green eyes, hidden behind transparent glasses, pierced the soul of anyone who looked into them.
For a moment, many men had boners. However, the moment she took a single step and a cold killing intent spread across the space, all of them wiped the lustful thoughts from their minds.
Kaizo and his team instantly became alert. They looked at the woman approaching them and wondered why she was here, of all places.
She soon stopped a meter away from them and scanned all of them, focusing more on Kaizo.
"I am the Green Bone Oracle. Nice meeting you all," she said, extending her hand for a handshake, something that divided the feelings surging through everyone.
Some felt it was too much for the Green Bone Oracle, someone whose legend had long spread throughout the Undead Realm, to shake hands with a mere demigod.
They saw it as a disrespect to her image.
Then there were those who wished she had shaken their hands instead—the ones who wished to be in Kaizo’s place.
But the man in question didn’t mind because he was already familiar with this lady. In fact, he had interacted with her, fought with her, and defeated her many times before, so he wasn’t intimidated.
"Nice meeting you too, Lady Green Bone Oracle. I am the leader of the Chaos Dragon Undead Mercenary Team."
"Chaos Dragon... such a peculiar name..." She walked closer and leaned in, exposing her rather voluptuous breasts. "I wonder where you twelve found such a name."
Kaizo wasn’t intimidated despite sensing the overwhelming strength of a Pseudo-Primordial before him. In fact, he seemed too calm, prompting many people to wonder where his confidence came from.
He smiled and answered, "I read somewhere that a very long time ago, an entity known as the Primordial Chaos Dragon single-handedly carried the weight of an entire universe on his shoulders.
"He inspired us, and so we wished to be like him one day, or at least try to be like him."
"Is that so?" the Green Bone Oracle asked, not too bothered by Kaizo’s blatant lie.
He nodded.

"Very well. I can say you have a good start if you one day wish to carry the weight of the Undead Realm on your shoulders. But putting that aside, do you twelve mind sharing some tea with me? I have a message from the Baron for you."

chapters.title: Chapter 1848: Undead Realm Mission (6)
paragraphs: Sometime later, Kaizo, his team members, and the Green Bone Oracle were seated inside a private room in one of the most luxurious restaurants in Rex City.
The moment they settled down, she set her sights on all of them, this time with an intense gaze. For a few minutes, no words were spoken.
Then she spoke...

"You know, if I were to live in the Infinity Universe, I would be one of the people who had been alive since the Primordial Era. This shows I am rather old and, by extension, have seen my fair share of mind-bending things.
However, right now, I am finding it extremely hard to figure out how undead beings could reincarnate. The last time I checked, Undeads don’t have souls, so how is any of this possible?"
Kaizo looked at his friends, and for a moment, they laughed.
"I think you already know the answer, my lady, so why ask?"
The Green Bone Oracle sighed. "How is he doing?"
"Master Sanders is fine. He sends his regards."
"I see." The Green Bone Oracle smiled upon hearing that Kent was fine and still remembered her.
"Though I want to know, how are you guys still alive? I know you are Ancients, but the last time I checked, Undeads don’t have souls, so reincarnation is impossible."

Sylara answered, "It is true that we are undead, but the master wasn’t. He was half-human, half-undead, so he reincarnated, and since we were created by him, naturally, we were linked to his soul. So with him reincarnating, we also came back with him.
In fact, we never died if you look at it from a certain perspective."
"Unbelievable. No wonder the Undead Monarch hated his guts. His nature as an undead and a necromancer violates every rule in the books."
She shook her head and took a sip of her tea.
"So what are you doing here, Kaizo? Did you come for the things he left in my care?"
"Yes. We came for the bones of some of our friends, but he said we would need you for some of his treasures he had stashed away in one of the Undead Graves."

"Which one?" she asked, not too surprised by their reason for coming. A very long time ago, Sanders, the Bone Lich Undead Emperor, told her he would one day return to the Undead Realm, so she should hold on to some treasures for him.
Now, he had come for them.
"Banathra Valley."

Green Bone Oracle nodded. "I see. Then we will have to travel to the Supreme Undead Heaven since the entrance is located there. However, before we can do that, you twelve will have to attend the Wine and Dine event organized by the Baron.
"He sent me to personally invite you, and knowing him, he will try to pull you to his side, either by force or through persuasion.
"Regardless, he will, and you will have to accept whatever he has to offer. In fact, I encourage you to accept whatever he offers because, knowing him, he will go all out to get you on his side.

"But you have to be careful too. Completing a red mission isn’t something to scoff at, and the Undead Monarch will hear about it sooner rather than later. When he does, he will launch an investigation, and I am sure he will soon figure out your identities."
"We understand, and the reason we went all out was to draw your attention. That worked, so it was a success, but we will also focus on making sure we don’t leave too much of a footprint here.
"The master is not ready to return here just yet, and the last thing we want is to become opponents of that bastard."
"That is wise. So keep a low profile for now. After the Wine and Dine event, we will head to the Supreme Undead Heaven and retrieve the items from Banathra Valley.

"You should prepare, though. While my presence will boost your strength, inside Banathra Valley, I will be suppressed to the Supreme Stage, and as you already know, the dangers inside that place are things even Celestials would run from."
Kaizo and his team nodded. "We will be ready. We have a few weeks to prepare, so rest assured, when the time comes, we will handle everything with precision.
"That said, there is another issue we don’t know if you can help us with."
Kaizo said, diverting the conversation to something new.
"What do you need help with?"

"On our way to Rex City, we learned that the Third Undead Princess will also be attending the Wine and Dine event. I don’t know if you are aware, but she and Master Sanders were rather close back in the day, so she will recognize us.
"Of course, we aren’t worried about that. It’s just that the last time we met, she was fighting on her father’s side against the master, so we don’t know if she still holds on to her anger."

The Green Bone Oracle smiled and said, "Oh, she is still angry, all right. However, I am not sure her anger stems from Sanders fighting against her father. I think her anger has more to do with matters of the heart.

"That said, I am no expert in such matters, so if you want, I will organize a meeting between both parties, and you can settle this before the event. She will arrive in two weeks, so the meeting can take place in three weeks."
"That would be wonderful, my lady. Kindly organize that meeting, and we will take things from there."

The Green Bone Oracle nodded and took another sip of her tea. She was happy that Kaizo and the others were here. This meant Kent was alive, and considering how much she had missed him, she wanted to know more about him.

"How about this? Since your no-good master seems to have broken some hearts in the past, why don’t you all spend the next few weeks lying low? I will do my best to handle matters on my end and make sure none of the ladies who want his head discover that you are here."

It’s just that the last time we met, she was fighting on her father’s side against the master, so we don’t know if she still holds on to her anger."
The Green Bone Oracle smiled and said, "Oh, she is still angry, all right.
However, I am not sure her anger stems from Sanders fighting against her father.
I think her anger has more to do with matters of the heart.
"That said, I am no expert in such matters, so if you want, I will organize a meeting between both parties, and you can settle this before the event.
She will arrive in two weeks, so the meeting can take place in three weeks."
"That would be wonderful, my lady.
Kindly organize that meeting, and we will take things from there."
The Green Bone Oracle nodded and took another sip of her tea.
She was happy that Kaizo and the others were here.
This meant Kent was alive, and considering how much she had missed him, she wanted to know more about him.
"How about this?
Since your no-good master seems to have broken some hearts in the past, why don’t you all spend the next few weeks lying low?
I will do my best to handle matters on my end and make sure none of the ladies who want his head discover that you are here."

chapters.title: Chapter 1849: Undead Realm Mission (7)
paragraphs: [Meeting the Third Undead Princess]
Days passed since the meeting with the Green Bone Oracle.
She didn’t spend much time with Kaizo and his team, since she had only come to pass along the message from Undead Baron Lamine, or, as many call him, Lord Lamine.
But she managed to learn more about Kent and how much had passed since she had last met him.
Back when Sanders (Kent’s incarnation) arrived in the Undead Realm, he was besieged by some powerful undead beasts. Had it not been for her, he would have perished back then.

To thank her, Sanders spent most of his time doing all kinds of work for her, later becoming someone who also protected her in the shadows because of her standing. They had a complicated relationship, but their respect for each other was solid.
It was why Kaizo and his team never doubted her sincerity when she asked them to lie low for now. They knew she would never betray them, not even if her life was in danger.
So, as days went by, they awaited news of when they would be meeting with the Third Undead Princess, one of the women their master once moved with.
They wanted to make sure she was okay with their master before meeting her in public, where things could get messy real quick.
Luckily, two weeks and five days later, the Green Bone Oracle sent word that, in two days, they would meet the Third Undead Princess.
Two days later, all 12 of them arrived at the Grand Bone Restaurant, a rather exclusive establishment where only the rich and extremely wealthy dined.

Kaizo and his team were invited, so despite having to make reservations months or sometimes years in advance, they were allowed entry and even led, like dignified guests, to a private room where the meeting would take place.
As they walked through the nicely decorated halls of the restaurant, Kaizo and his team couldn’t help but sense some powerful presences hidden all around the restaurant.
’Looks like she came prepared,’ Morne said into the heads of his teammates, causing them all to nod inwardly.

’All the more reason to be careful then. I doubt she would kill us, but still, you can never know what goes on in the head of a woman. So we should be on high alert,’ Kaizo said, and while his words were true, the ladies within the team chuckled.
He made it seem like ladies are complicated creatures.
Ladies are simple creatures. They only become complicated when the wrong conditions are met.

A few seconds after entering, they arrived in a room where two people were already seated. One of them was, of course, the Green Bone Oracle, while the other was the Princess, seated elegantly with her face covered in a thin white veil.
Many wondered what she looked like under her veil, since only a handful had seen her true appearance.

Unlike the Green Bone Oracle, who was barely covered by her gown, she was clad in a gray-colored cloak that covered her entire body, hiding her assets. She also possesses long silver hair and enchanting gray eyes.
The moment Kaizo and his team entered the room, all 12 of them felt their consciousness invaded by a presence none of them could block.
This presence scanned their bodies and consciousness for a few seconds before pulling back.
"It is indeed you people," she spoke, letting out a sigh. "Sit down."
Kaizo and his team sat, every one of them alert. The fact that this lady managed to penetrate that deeply into their consciousness told them she was no longer someone they could mess with.
She was a Primordial, someone far stronger than even the Green Bone Oracle.

"What are you doing here?" she asked, looking directly at Kaizo, whom she remembered all too well from their shared past. When she met Sanders, he was with Kaizo. So even if she didn’t recognize any of them, Kaizo was someone she would remember.
"Master sent us," Kaizo replied, and she smiled.
"So he lacked the balls to come here. Instead, he sent his lackeys to come and die on his behalf." Cold air emanated from her body, causing the 12 Undead Generals to become even more alert.
"You know, the last time we met, you stabbed me with a poisoned dagger, young lady," she said, turning to Velithra. The latter trembled, sensing the cold gaze of the Third Undead Princess on her.
She fought through the intimidation and responded, "You were our enemy, so I had to. But you live now, so why don’t we call it a thing of the past?"
Velithra managed to even smile, though her smile seemed rather forced. It was plain as day that she was terrified of the woman looking back at her.
And it is perfectly normal to be terrified of her. Her true powers aren’t something to underestimate...

"Thing of the past, you say," the Third Undead Princess chuckled. "How about you, Vampire Demoness? You killed three of my subordinates and injured one of my Ancients. Right now, the only thing stopping her from cutting your head off is that I told her to hold on."

Sylara trembled as a pale figure clad in white armor appeared behind the Third Undead Princess, holding a scythe on her shoulder. She arrogantly tilted her head to the side and smirked, perhaps cherishing the look on Sylara’s face.
Sylara narrowed her eyes, then ignited two Blood Tattoos, instantly wiping away the intimidation around her and deep within her mind.
"I have done so many bad things, but one of the good ones was finally shutting your sharp mouth for good, White Lily."

Sylara stood up, pulled out two daggers, and pointed both at the white-armored lady holding the scythe. "Or do you think just because you are now a Pseudo-Primordial, you can take me on?" Sylara smirked and added, "Lower your cultivation to the True God Stage and come at me. Let’s see who dies in the end."
For a moment, the air in the room hung heavy. Then, out of nowhere, Kaizo exploded into resounding laughter, wiping away the seriousness in the air.
Everyone turned to look at him, wondering why he was laughing.

A few moments later, Kaizo managed to rein in his laughter and said, "It is good to see you haven’t changed, Dominique. I am sure Master would be happy to see you again after we bring you with us back to the Infinity Universe."

chapters.title: Chapter 1850: Undead Realm Mission (8)
paragraphs: "Huh, you can take me with you?" the Third Undead Princess asked, her expression softening.
All the coldness in her eyes vanished, replaced by the hope that she could leave the Undead Realm with Kaizo and the rest.
There are only two ways for an undead to go to the Infinity Universe.
The first is to sign a contract with a necromancer, something all undead hate. They are prideful beings, so signing a contract with a necromancer is considered beneath them.
The second method, of course, has to do with passing the Trial of the Dao. Those who pass gain the ability to go to the Infinity Universe, never to return to the Undead Realm ever again.

Only a few dare try this method since it is extremely difficult and dangerous. Of course, there is a third method, which mostly depends on the Undead Monarch, who has the means to invade the Infinity Universe through special gateways.
That method was used during the Undead Era when he, alongside the Abyssal and Resentful Races, invaded the Infinity Universe.
These methods all require great sacrifice, so most undead do away with all that and focus more on their lives in the vast and dangerous Undead Realm.
But for someone who wished to leave this place one day, the offer made her forget her anger toward Kaizo and his team.
Kaizo smiled and nodded. "We can take you with us, but you will be restricted in the places you can go. However, if you want, when we are leaving, you can come with us."
"I would love that," the Third Undead Princess, who goes by Dominique, said with a broad smile. She turned and looked at her subordinate clad in white armor and said,
"Stand down, White Lily."
"But—" White Lily tried to protest, but a glare from Dominique made her shut her mouth. She glared at Sylara, then scoffed, dissolving into sparks of light. Soon, she vanished from sight.
Sylara smirked and sheathed her daggers. Then she deactivated her Blood Tattoos and sat down.
She and White Lily were rivals back in the day. They had fought many times, with their last battle ending with Sylara nearly killing her.
It appears that after all these years, she still hadn’t forgotten that defeat. Unfortunately for her, Dominique had no plans to let her have fun torturing Sylara, at least not just yet.
Her happiness mattered more than petty squabbles.

Dominique scanned the faces of all 12 undead and said, "I don’t know why you are here, but completing a red mission was a bad move. In case you are not aware, all 12 of you are among the most wanted people on my father’s hit list.
Getting his hands on you will be the most cherished moment of his life, so you’d better be careful. He hasn’t said anything yet simply because he isn’t available right now.
But he will soon return, and I doubt he will be thrilled to learn that his past enemies are back and have started causing trouble everywhere."
Kaizo smirked and asked, "Where is he, by the way?"
"Father left for the Abyssal Realm a couple of years back to have a meeting with the Abyssal Empress and the Resentful Monarch."
Kaizo and his teammates narrowed their eyes, and Zareth asked in a deep tone, "Does this meeting have anything to do with the return of the Underworld Empress?"
Dominique frowned a bit. "Maybe, but why do you ask? The last I checked, you guys are from the Infinity Universe, so how do matters of the Underworld concern any of your business?"
Vaelros responded, "It is our concern because if he dares attack that place, he will lose, and this time, I am sure the Master will kill him for good."
Dominique frowned even more deeply. "I don’t understand. How do matters of the Underworld concern the Bone Lich Undead Emperor?"
The last she checked, the Underworld, while connected to the Infinity Universe, had its own ruler, and that ruler was the Underworld Empress.

She and the Undead Monarch had been enemies in the past, and so, naturally, they mostly fought whenever they met. Kent isn’t affiliated with the Underworld, so why would attacking it provoke his wrath?

"It is not our business to tell you why the Master will retaliate. However, know that the Master and the Underworld Empress share a very close bond. Attacking her would surely provoke his wrath, and trust me, if the last time you faced only a few thousand of us, then prepare for millions this time.
So if you have your father’s ear, make sure he doesn’t attack there, or don’t say we didn’t warn you."
Kaizo made sure she understood their stance. Thankfully, Dominique wasn’t one too deeply connected to her father, so she merely smiled and said,
"I don’t care what he does. But I will make sure he doesn’t doom the rest of us. That said, their meeting is mostly focused on the Abyssal Chaos, so maybe he wouldn’t attack the Underworld just yet.
But you have to hurry, finish your mission, and leave before he returns. I know with certainty he will figure out your identities even if I help you, so hurry with your mission and leave."
"Does that mean you wouldn’t be leaving with us?" Sylara asked.
"As long as I can return before my father notices I was gone, then sure, I will go with you. I want to meet that bastard and tell him a piece of my mind."
Kaizo nodded, and his team wasn’t too bothered that bringing her along might be a bad thing for Kent. They were more concerned with just how much trouble she would cause when she met Kent.
Regardless, she wouldn’t kill him, so they weren’t too worried.
Their meeting soon turned to catching up, with most of the questions being about Kent. They answered every last one of her questions, and when the meeting ended, she left.
A week later, the time for the wine-and-dine event arrived. Kaizo and his team attended, and by the time the event ended, they had become one of the many mercenary teams on Lord Lamine’s payroll.
Two weeks after that, they arrived in the Supreme Undead Heaven for their final mission.
